Fact.Name: Has Schedule C business income
Fact.Description: Whether the primary filer operated a sole proprietorship reported on Schedule C. Gate for the Schedule C intake.

Fact.Name: Claims Schedule C income
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: true only when /hasScheduleCIncome is answered and true (IsComplete pattern, as qbi:/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness). Unanswered resolves Complete false so returns without a Schedule C still resolve.

Fact.Name: Schedules C filed with this return
Fact.Description:
The sole proprietorships reported on this return — one item per Schedule C (Form 1040), "Profit or Loss From Business (Sole Proprietorship)". The form is filed once per business and its line 32 routes EACH form's line 31 separately to Schedule 1 line 3 and Schedule SE line 2, so the count is unbounded and a joint return may carry one business for each spouse.
A NEW COLLECTION RATHER THAN A REUSE, and the alternatives were checked rather than assumed. qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses is one item per section 199A qualified trade, business or AGGREGATION — a different grain in both directions (a QTB may be a K-1 trade or a rental enterprise with no Schedule C at all, and a Schedule B aggregation may span several). scheduleE:/rentalProperties is Schedule E Part I. Neither is a Schedule C, and the qbi collection's own Description says so.
NOT A SCHEDULE C: A TRIBE MEMBER'S FISHING RIGHTS-RELATED ACTIVITY. Income a member of an Indian tribe derives, directly or through a qualified Indian entity, from a fishing rights-related activity of the tribe (harvesting, processing, transporting or selling fish taken under a treaty, Executive order or Act of Congress fishing right secured by March 17, 1988) bears no income tax and no self-employment tax, so it is left off the return: it is not reported in any item's gross receipts, and the expenses allocable to it are not deducted on any item. A business that is wholly such an activity is not listed here at all.
The primary filer used by Schedule C attribution guards
The secondary filer used by Schedule C attribution guards

Fact.Name: Schedule C proprietor (which filer owns this business)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer who operated the sole proprietorship reported on this Schedule C — the primary filer or, on an MFJ return, the spouse. Mirrors /formW2s/*/filer and /formK1s/*/filer (the established per-form attribution pattern). PER-ITEM since the collection migration; it was the return-level /scheduleCFiler, and its own Description conceded the shape it was working around — "scalar rather than per-item because Schedule C is modeled as a single business". That is no longer true, and a couple who each run a business are now two items with two proprietors rather than one unrepresentable return. Unanswered defaults to the PRIMARY filer (the /formW2s/*/filer back-compat posture), so every committed scenario — none of which answers this field — keeps its existing attribution and no resolved value changes. interpretation:provisional — CHOSEN READING: an unanswered proprietor is the PRIMARY filer. REJECTED: refuse (knock out) an MFJ return with a Schedule C whose proprietor is unanswered, which would be the "refuse what you cannot attribute" posture once taken for K-1s; rejected here for the same reason the per-filer Schedule SE split rejected it there — it imposes a completeness/value change on every pre-existing return to guard a case the intake flow can simply require an answer for. Revisit if a real intake ever writes an MFJ Schedule C without a proprietor. THAT REVISIT FIRED AND THE REJECTION STANDS — what changed is that the case is now GUARDED instead of merely conceded. The clause above rests on "the intake flow can simply require an answer for" it, and invariant #7 puts that flow in the application's repo, so this dictionary was resting a wrong-filer attribution on a promise it does not hold. A knockout is still the wrong instrument, for exactly the reason given; the right one is the module family's submission block, and it landed as ../proprietorUnansweredOnMfj (see the block comment above ../belongsToPrimaryFiler for the whole argument and the 6,870.84 the silence costs). NOTHING ON THIS FACT CHANGED: it keeps its Placeholder and both belongsTo flags keep their bodies, so no resolved value moves. Removing the Placeholder would not have closed the defect anyway — ../belongsToSecondaryFiler rejects an unanswered ../filer at its IsComplete guard and takes the False fallthrough without ever reading it. NO secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ CONSISTENCY GUARD, deliberately and worth stating because eight modules (/formW2s, /interestReports, /form1099Rs, /unemployment, /hsaDistributions, /form1099Miscs, socialSecurity, and /dividendReports) carry one for exactly this shape: a filer switching from MFJ to MFS/single leaves a stale spouse-attributed form, and those modules refuse it via BlockSubmissionOnTrue. Here the MFJ guard on ../belongsToSecondaryFiler silently routes such a stale attribution to the primary's Schedule SE instead — which is the return-level behaviour for that return and so not a regression, and which /formK1s/*/filer also does (it carries no guard either). Adding the guard would be a THIRD form's worth of submission-blocking behaviour change riding on an attribution unit; it belongs with the K-1 one, in a unit that does both.

Fact.Name: Schedule C belongs to the secondary filer
Fact.Description: Whether the modeled Schedule C is the SECONDARY (MFJ spouse) filer's. Complete false on every return the corpus contains that is not an answered, MFJ, spouse-attributed Schedule C — deliberately, because this flag gates a Dollar that reaches Schedule SE and thence total tax, so an Incomplete here cascades through the whole return. It is NOT unconditionally complete-safe, and the two states where it is not are named here rather than claimed away: (A) /scheduleCFiler ANSWERED while /filingStatus is unanswered — /isFilingStatusMFJ is an Equal over a bare Writable with no Placeholder, so it is Incomplete, All returns Incomplete, and the True fallthrough yields Placeholder(false); (B) MFJ selected before the spouse exists in /filers, so /secondaryFiler's Find has no match and the Equal is Incomplete, making this fact Incomplete. In (B) the /scheduleCBelongsToPrimaryFiler complement is Incomplete too (Not is strict), so BOTH chains take Placeholder(0) and the profit reaches neither — the failure is a vanished /selfEmploymentTax, never a quietly low one. Both states are mid-interview shapes no committed scenario reaches; if an intake ever produces one, the fix is a Placeholder on /filingStatus, not a third guard here. TWO guards, both load-bearing: (1) /scheduleCFiler must actually be ANSWERED (the IsComplete-first pattern of /formK1s/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler — the Placeholder default is primary-filer, and reading it through a bare Equal would resolve Result.Placeholder); (2) the return must be MFJ, because filers:/secondaryFiler is a Find over /filers that has nothing to find on a single-filer return, so Equal(x, /secondaryFiler) would be incomplete there. Guard (2) does a SECOND job worth naming, because the corpus actually contains the case: /filers/*/isSecondaryFiler is NotEqual(Find(/filers, isPrimaryFiler), ..) and says nothing about filing status, so a NON-MFJ return carrying a stray second /filers member has a resolving /secondaryFiler. Attributing a business to that member would be meaningless — there is one taxpayer and one Schedule SE — so MFS, QSS, HoH and single all route to the primary chain. WHY THE GUARDS ARE NOT OPTIONAL, read off the engine rather than assumed: Expression.switch's resultRecurse carries an accComplete flag, and a When whose Result has no value both falls through AND clears it, so the case that finally matches is returned .asPlaceholder — the routed Dollar would stop being Complete, and with it every downstream fact up to /selfEmploymentTax, which the runner then omits from the snapshot entirely. /formW2s/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler carries neither guard, and the reason it survives does NOT transfer here — nor is it the Filter, which is the tempting wrong answer: FilterOperator does read an incomplete predicate as a plain false for MEMBERSHIP (results.map(_.getOrElse(false))), but the very next line sets complete = vect.complete AND results.forall(_.complete), so the filtered COLLECTION is itself Placeholder and the incompleteness is relocated, not absorbed. What actually saves the W-2 fact is that its risky consumer wraps the Filter in All(/isFilingStatusMFJ, ...) and AllOperator short-circuits on a Complete false — i.e. an outer MFJ guard, the same guard written directly onto this fact.

Fact.Name: Schedule C belongs to the primary filer
Fact.Description: Whether the modeled Schedule C is the PRIMARY filer's. Defined as the COMPLEMENT of /scheduleCBelongsToSecondaryFiler rather than as its own Equal(/scheduleCFiler, /primaryFiler), so that the two flags PARTITION the Schedule C: exactly one of them is true on every return, and /scheduleCNetProfit therefore reaches exactly one Schedule SE. A pair of independent Equals could both be false — an owner naming neither filer would silently drop the whole net profit out of the self-employment-tax computation, understating tax with nothing to detect it. /filers holds only the primary and (on MFJ) the secondary, so the complement is also the correct reading, not merely the safe one.

Fact.Name: Schedule C proprietor never named on a joint return
Fact.Description: Whether this Schedule C is on a joint return with its proprietor left unanswered — the one state in which ../belongsToPrimaryFiler is true because nobody said so rather than because somebody did. Complete false on every return that is not MFJ (the All short-circuits on the filing-status operand, and a return with one filer has one possible proprietor), Complete false whenever ../filer is answered whichever spouse it names, and Incomplete while /filingStatus itself is unanswered. See the block comment above for why this is a submission block rather than a knockout and why removing ../filer's Placeholder would not have closed it.

Fact.Name: A Schedule C on this joint return does not say which spouse owns the business
Fact.Description: Whether ANY Schedule C on a joint return has an unanswered proprietor. Blocks submission: the business would otherwise be filed on the primary filer's Schedule SE by default, which is an answer the filer never gave and, when the primary filer's social security wage base is already spent, an understatement of self-employment tax. Incomplete — and therefore blocking nothing — whenever any item's flag is Incomplete, which is the not-yet-answered filing-status state.

Fact.Name: Gross receipts
Fact.Description:
Schedule C LINE 1: gross receipts or sales, GROSS. Leave out income from a fishing rights-related activity of the filer's Indian tribe (see /scheduleCs): it is not subject to income tax or self-employment tax.
THIS USED TO SAY "returns/allowances (line 2) are netted in by the filer" AND IT MUST NOT SAY THAT ANY MORE. Line 2 is its own intake (../writableReturnsAndAllowances) and ../scheduleCGrossIncome subtracts it. A filer who followed the old instruction AND answers the new line-2 intake DOUBLE-SUBTRACTS returns. A filer who follows neither is unaffected: the line-2 intake defaults to 0.

Fact.Name: Returns and allowances (Schedule C line 2)
Fact.Description:
Schedule C line 2: returns and allowances, as a POSITIVE amount; the printed line is a subtraction and the sign is applied downstream by ../scheduleCGrossIncome.
IT ENDS A COLLAPSE. Before it, ../writableGrossReceipts carried the instruction "returns/allowances (line 2) are netted in by the filer", so line 2 had no separate existence and line 3 could not be computed. It has one now: gross receipts means LINE 1, gross, and returns are subtracted by the graph. A filer who continues to net them in and leaves this unanswered gets the same line 29 as before (this defaults to 0), so the change is additive on every existing return — but the RECORD is now faithful where before it was two numbers merged into one.
Min 0: returns and allowances are an amount returned, and the printed line's arithmetic already carries the sign. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Cost of goods sold (Schedule C line 4, from Part III line 42)
Fact.Description:
Schedule C line 4: cost of goods sold, the Part III line 42 result, as a POSITIVE amount. The Part III inventory arithmetic (lines 33-42) is NOT modelled; this is its bottom line, attested.
THIS IS THE FACT THAT MAKES LINE 7 EXIST: Schedule C LINE 7, gross income, is receipts minus COGS, and COGS has its own intake here rather than living inside a collapsed "total expenses plus cost of goods sold" figure from which nothing could extract it. The split is an intake choice this dictionary makes.
../writableTotalExpenses IS REDEFINED IN THE SAME UNIT to mean line 28 ALONE. Read its Description before answering either: a return that answers COGS here must NOT also carry it in the expense total, or line 29 subtracts it twice. Every committed scenario leaves this unanswered, so it defaults to 0 and no committed line 29 moves; the redefinition is forward-looking, which is exactly why it is stated on both facts rather than one.
Min 0. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Other income, including federal and state gasoline or fuel tax credit or refund (Schedule C line 6)
Fact.Description:
Schedule C line 6: other income, including any federal or state gasoline or fuel tax credit or refund. ADDED to gross profit at line 7, so it is the one Part I term that raises gross income rather than reducing it.
WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COMPLETENESS: it is the reason the direction of the line-1 vs line-7 gap was never determinable. Returns and COGS push line 7 BELOW line 1 while this pushes it ABOVE, so a successor substituting gross receipts for gross income erred in an unknown direction. With all three terms now modelled the substitution is unnecessary.
Min 0: the printed line names credits, refunds and other income, none of which has a loss form on the face. interpretation:provisional.
A Form 4797 line 35 recapture is NOT entered here: it is entered on ../writableForm4797Line35RecaptureAmount and added to line 6 for you (../scheduleCLine6OtherIncome, the printed line 6). Nor are amounts received in the business as shown on Form 1099-PATR (../writableForm1099PatrDistributionsInThisBusiness). DO include here: if the business use of leased listed property other than a vehicle dropped to 50% or less in 2025, the inclusion amount figured under chapter 5 of Pub. 946; prizes and awards related to the business; and other miscellaneous business income. NOT A DEFECT (row FED-1040SC-LINE6-OTHER-INCOME-004, ARGUE): line 6 is a residual of other business income whose items the instructions list for the filer to include, among them the leased listed property inclusion: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 6 "if the business use percentage drops to 50% or less on leased listed property (other than a vehicle), include on this line any inclusion amount. See chapter 5 of Pub. 946 to figure the amount." That inclusion is named in this question above; the Form 4797 recapture (../writableForm4797Line35RecaptureAmount) and the Form 1099-PATR amounts (../writableForm1099PatrDistributionsInThisBusiness) have their own computed legs of the printed line 6 (../scheduleCLine6OtherIncome).

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture reported on this Schedule C (line 6)
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION: "How much of your Form 4797 line 35 recapture comes from property whose section 179 deduction or depreciation you took on this Schedule C?" HELP TEXT: "When business use of section 179 property or listed property drops to 50% or less, Form 4797 Part IV figures a recapture amount on line 35. Report it as other income on the same form or schedule on which you took the deduction. Enter the part for this business here and leave it out of your line 6 other income answer: it is added to line 6 for you. If the property was used both in this business and to produce income, enter only the part attributable to this business; that part is subject to self-employment tax. Increase your basis in the property by the recapture amount." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 12, right column; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 6, right column; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p946.pdf, page 57, left column). ASKED WHEN: form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureToRoute is above zero, once per business. UNANSWERED: $0 for this business; when the amounts entered on every schedule do not add up to line 35, the return does not complete (form4797:/hasUnallocatedPartIVLine35Recapture). VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../form4797Line35RecaptureAllocated, hence line 6 (../scheduleCLine6OtherIncome), line 7, net profit, Schedule SE and the qualified business income computation, and the Form 4797 allocation check.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to this Schedule C (complete safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableForm4797Line35RecaptureAmount when the return files Schedule C (/claimsScheduleCIncome) and the question is answered, else $0. Counted by /scheduleCForm4797Line35RecaptureAllocatedTotal into the Form 4797 allocation check and carried to line 6 by ../form4797Line35RecaptureLeg, so the check and the line read one quantity.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to all Schedule C businesses (complete safe)
Fact.Description: The sum of /scheduleCs/*/form4797Line35RecaptureAllocated when the Schedule C collection exists, else $0. The Schedule C term of form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureAllocatedTotal.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture carried to this Schedule C line 6
Fact.Description: ../form4797Line35RecaptureAllocated when form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureIsAllocated is TRUE; NO default arm, so when the line 35 recapture is not fully allocated this leg, line 6, line 7 and net profit are Incomplete and the return refuses (legible through form4797:/hasUnallocatedPartIVLine35Recapture). $0 on every return with no Part IV amount.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-PATR distributions received in this trade or business
Fact.Description: SCREEN. QUESTION TEXT: "How much of the patronage dividends and other distributions on your Forms 1099-PATR (boxes 1, 2, 3 and 5) did you receive in this business?" HELP TEXT: the Schedule C instructions list amounts received in your trade or business as shown on Form 1099-PATR as line 6 other income; enter them here and not in the other-income amount, so they are counted once; leave out dividends on capital assets or depreciable property used in the business (not taxable; reduce the asset's basis). ASKED WHEN: the return records a Form 1099-PATR and this Schedule C business exists. UNANSWERED: $0 for this business, and the Form 1099-PATR amounts go to Schedule 1 line 8z instead (IN-56), so nothing is dropped. VALIDATION: dollars, not less than $0. FEEDS: ../scheduleCLine6OtherIncome and /scheduleCForm1099PatrDistributionsTotal.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-PATR distributions in this business, $0 when unanswered
Fact.Description: ../writableForm1099PatrDistributionsInThisBusiness floored at $0, or $0 when unanswered. Added to ../scheduleCLine6OtherIncome.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-PATR distributions reported on Schedule C, all businesses
Fact.Description: The sum of every Schedule C business's ../form1099PatrDistributionsInThisBusinessOrZero; complete $0 when no Schedule C is listed. income subtracts it from the Form 1099-PATR amounts it carries to Schedule 1 line 8z, so each dollar lands on one line.

Fact.Name: Other income (Schedule C line 6, as printed)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 6 as the form prints it: ../writableOtherBusinessIncome (the filer's other income, $0 when unanswered) plus ../form4797Line35RecaptureLeg (the Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to this business, which the Schedule C instructions place on line 6). The line 6 term of ../scheduleCGrossIncome (line 7).

Fact.Name: This Schedule C business is a fishing business (Pub. 505 carve-out)
Fact.Description:
Whether THIS Schedule C trade or business is fishing — "catching, taking, harvesting, cultivating, or farming any kind of fish, shellfish ... crustaceans, sponges, seaweeds, or other aquatic forms of animal and vegetable life", in Pub. 505's own words.
IT SELECTS, IT DOES NOT COMPUTE. Nothing about this business's tax treatment changes: line 7, line 29 and line 31 are identical whether or not this is answered. Its ONLY consumer is /scheduleCFishingGrossIncome, the Pub. 505 numerator term, because a filer may run a fishing business AND a non-fishing one and only the first belongs in that numerator. Summing every Schedule C line 7 would over-include, which is the error this one Boolean exists to prevent.
OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means NOT a fishing business, so a return that never saw this question contributes 0 to the fishing numerator rather than making it Incomplete. That is the categorical posture — absent means not in the carve-out — and it is the conservative direction here, because over-including would inflate a numerator that grants a penalty waiver. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Gross income (Schedule C line 7)
Fact.Description:
Schedule C line 7 = line 1 gross receipts, minus line 2 returns and allowances, minus line 4 cost of goods sold, plus line 6 other income. The form spells it as line 3 (1 minus 2), line 5 (3 minus 4) and line 7 (5 plus 6); the intermediate lines are not separately modelled because nothing reads them.
COMPLETE-SAFE AND ADDITIVE BY CONSTRUCTION: the three new subtrahend/addend intakes all default to 0, so on every return that answers none of them this equals ../writableGrossReceipts exactly — which is what /scheduleCs/*/tentativeProfit used to subtract expenses from. No committed line 29, line 31, QBI or SE-tax figure moves.
WHY IT WAS BUILT: Pub. 505's gross income from fishing list names "Schedule C (Form 1040), Profit or Loss From Business, LINE 7" as its first item, and this dictionary modelled only line 1. The gap was not a rounding difference — it is receipts minus COGS — and it was the last missing summand of the estimated-tax two-thirds numerator. interpretation:provisional.
STATUTORY EMPLOYEE LEG ON LINE 1: line 1 also carries ../statutoryEmployeeWagesFromLinkedW2s, the box 1 of every W-2 whose box 13 "Statutory employee" checkbox is set and which names THIS business as the Schedule C its income is reported on. That is the entry the Schedule C instructions print, and the same per W-2 figures come OUT of Form 1040 line 1a (formW2s:/wages) so nothing is counted twice. The leg is complete safe $0 and is $0 on every committed scenario, none of which checks box 13, so no committed line 7 moves. The minuend ../writableGrossReceipts is UNCHANGED and still bare, which is load bearing for qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/scheduleCLinkResolves.
CENTS ARE KEPT, NOT ROUNDED: lines 1 through 6 print cents, and a return that rounds rounds every amount or none (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 23 "round to whole dollars, you must round"), so line 7 is line 5 plus line 6 to the cent, not a whole-dollar figure beside cents. This line was formerly wrapped in Round.
LINE 6 is ../scheduleCLine6OtherIncome: the filer's other income ($0 when unanswered) plus the Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to this business (../form4797Line35RecaptureLeg).

Fact.Name: This business's Schedule C line 1, complete-safe
Fact.Description: ../writableGrossReceipts when the filer answered it, else $0. Read only by /scheduleCReportedGrossReceiptsTotal, so the bare ../writableGrossReceipts minuend that qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/scheduleCLinkResolves depends on is untouched.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 1 gross receipts, every business on this return
Fact.Description:
The complete-safe sum of every Schedule C's line 1 on this return, cents preserved. An unopened or empty collection contributes $0 -- the membership test is on the collection itself, never on an item, which is the unanswered-collection trap this dictionary has paid for three times.
RETURN-LEVEL AND NOT PER-BUSINESS, deliberately: no fact in this dictionary links a Form 1099-MISC to one of several businesses, so the only honest comparison is the whole return's. The per-item selector is the named successor.

Fact.Name: Schedule C gross receipts cover the Form 1099-MISC receipts reported to this return
Fact.Description:
Consistency fence. TRUE unless this return claims Schedule C income AND the Form 1099-MISC boxes that belong on a Schedule C and the filer has not explained (form1099Misc:/form1099MiscScheduleCReceiptsFenceFloor -- box 5, box 6, box 11 and the attested taxable part of box 10, less the documents attested as already reported correctly) total MORE than every Schedule C line 1 on the return put together.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY BEING COMPARED, stated plainly. The left side is a PER-PAYER total of four boxes from the return's Forms 1099-MISC. The right side is Schedule C line 1, GROSS RECEIPTS FROM ALL SOURCES, summed over every business on the return. These are not the same shape and the comparison is not like-for-like: it is an inequality between a strict subset of the return's receipts and the filer's own all-sources figure, which is sound only in the one direction it is used. It is NOT the scheduleF:/scheduleFLine6a1099MiscConsistent shape -- that fact compares Form 1099-MISC box 9 against the SAME printed line, 6a, and gates on that line being answered. The earlier claim that this was "the scheduleF shape" is withdrawn. A per-business selector, which would make the comparison narrower and truer, is the named successor.
THE IRS'S OWN ESCAPE IS WIRED IN, and without it this fence refused returns the printed instructions tell the filer to file. The Schedule C line 1 instruction's remedy for a Form 1099 total above line 1 is "attach a statement explaining the difference"; the Form 1099-MISC's remedy for an incorrect or erroneously issued form is "attach an explanation to your tax return and report your information correctly". Neither is a bar to filing. A filer who answers form1099Misc:/form1099Miscs/*/writableScheduleCReceiptsReportedCorrectly TRUE on a document removes that document from the left side, and the return files.
THE /claimsScheduleCIncome CONJUNCT IS THE SAFETY VALVE. A filer who reports box 6 income and has opened no Schedule C at all is not refused by this fence; that return is refused instead by form1099Misc:/knockoutForm1099MiscScheduleCReceiptsWithoutScheduleC, which blocks submission when the unexplained Schedule C boxes are above zero and no Schedule C is claimed. What IS refused here is the return that HAS a Schedule C, foots it below the receipts its own information returns report, and explains nothing.
ONE-DIRECTIONAL. Gross receipts ABOVE the Form 1099-MISC total are never refused: a business has customers who file no information return, and the payer threshold is $600.
IT FAILS CLOSED. An earlier version required both operands to be Complete before comparing and fell to a default TRUE arm otherwise, so a single contradictory box-10 attestation on one document -- an attested taxable part above its own gross -- made the left side Incomplete and switched the fence off FOR THE WHOLE RETURN, footing a Schedule C the same unit had just refused for a one-cent shortfall (probe rev-b). Those IsComplete conjuncts are gone. An Incomplete operand on a return that claims Schedule C income now makes this fact Incomplete, and Schedule C line 7 with it.
STILL TRUE, COMPLETE, ON EVERY OTHER RETURN: /claimsScheduleCIncome is complete-safe false on a return with no Schedule C, and the fence floor is a hard $0 wherever boxes 5, 6, 10 and 11 are unanswered, which is every Form 1099-MISC this dictionary had committed before this unit.

Fact.Name: This business's Schedule C line 7 when it is a fishing business, else 0
Fact.Description: ../scheduleCGrossIncome when ../writableIsFishingBusiness is answered true, else 0 — the per-business term of /scheduleCFishingGrossIncome. FLOORED AT $0 PER BUSINESS. Schedule C line 7 can be negative (returns and cost of goods sold exceeding receipts), and Publication 505 measures the two-thirds test on "the total of the income (not loss) amounts", so a fishing business whose line 7 is a loss contributes nothing rather than reducing another business's income. The floor is per business, not on the sum, because each line 7 is its own amount. Direction of the old unfloored reading: a negative line 7 shrank the numerator and could deny a farmer or fisher the 66 2/3 percent route (over-charge).

Fact.Name: Gross income from fishing businesses on Schedule C (Pub. 505 fishing item 1; exported, unwired)
Fact.Description:
Round(CollectionSum(/scheduleCs/*/fishingGrossIncome)) — the FIRST bullet of Pub. 505's gross income from fishing form-line map, and the TENTH and last summand of the estimated-tax two-thirds numerator.
WHY IT IS SELECTIVE RATHER THAN A TOTAL: a filer may run a fishing business and a non-fishing one, and only the first belongs in this numerator. Summing every Schedule C line 7 would over-include and inflate a ratio that grants a penalty waiver, so each business carries its own ../writableIsFishingBusiness attestation.
WHAT CONSUMES IT, as of the same day it was built: estimatedPayments:/grossFarmingFishingIncomeCurrentYear, the 2025 numerator of the farmer/fisher two-thirds test — which is now FILLED and no longer a records contract. This fact was the TENTH and last summand, and its landing is what made that fill possible. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Total business expenses (Schedule C line 28, other than the computed line-9 standard mileage)
Fact.Description:
Schedule C line 28 total expenses. The individual expense lines 8-27, home-office (line 30), and the vehicle/depreciation detail are collapsed into this one filer-supplied total.
THIS DOES NOT INCLUDE COST OF GOODS SOLD. It used to read "line 28 total expenses PLUS cost of goods sold (line 4)", and that collapse sealed COGS inside a total nothing could extract it from — which made Schedule C LINE 7 (gross income) structurally underivable and blocked the estimated-tax two-thirds numerator. COGS is now its own intake, ../writableCostOfGoodsSold, subtracted at line 7 where the form prints it. A RETURN MUST NOT CARRY COGS IN BOTH PLACES, or line 29 subtracts it twice. Every committed scenario leaves the new intake unanswered, so it defaults to 0 and no committed line 29, line 31, QBI or SE-tax figure moves — the redefinition is forward-looking, and it is stated on both facts rather than one because a stale reading of either is a double-subtraction. When /writableBusinessMilesDriven is answered, the line-9 standard-mileage amount is COMPUTED separately (/scheduleCCarTruckExpenses) and must NOT be included here again — this total is every OTHER expense. Business parking fees and tolls, which the instructions add to line 9, are entered on ../writableParkingFeesAndTolls, not here.
DO NOT INCLUDE ../writableStartUpExpendituresIncurred'S IRC §195 DEDUCTION HERE EITHER: it is computed separately (../startUpExpendituresDeduction) and added at line 28 the same way line 9 is, so a total entered here should exclude any start-up-cost amortization the filer might otherwise have folded into their own Part V figure.

Fact.Name: Business miles driven in 2025 (standard mileage rate)
Fact.Description: The number of business miles driven in 2025, for the Schedule C line 9 standard-mileage computation (Part IV line 44a). OPTIONAL — unanswered means no standard-mileage claim and line 9 resolves 0 (actual vehicle expenses may instead be included in /writableTotalExpenses, the instructions' other method). Eligibility is ATTESTED, not modeled: the filer owned the vehicle and used the standard mileage rate from the first year, or leased it and uses the standard rate for the whole lease (i1040sc Line 9). Fleet operation (5+ vehicles) not supported.

Fact.Name: Elects the actual-expense method for vehicle (car and truck) costs
Fact.Description: The ANNUAL election between the two Schedule C line-9 methods — FALSE / unanswered = the standard mileage rate (the landed default path); TRUE = the actual-expense method (business portion of operating costs). "You can deduct the actual expenses of operating your car or truck OR take the standard mileage rate" (i1040sc Line 9). OPTIONAL — when unanswered the line-9 amount is exactly the standard-mileage computation, so every prior Schedule C scenario is value-identical. Switching rules are ATTESTED, not modeled (SCOPE-OUT, surfaced): a filer generally cannot switch a leased vehicle from the standard rate to actual expenses after using the standard rate, and a vehicle depreciated with MACRS/section 179 under the actual method is generally locked out of the standard rate in later years (i1040sc Line 9; Pub 463 ch.4). This single-year engine takes the filer's election as given.

Fact.Name: Actual-expense method elected (complete-safe gate)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate mirroring /claimsScheduleCIncome — true only when /electsActualVehicleExpense is answered and true. Unanswered resolves Complete false, so the line-9 Switch defaults to the standard-mileage path and every prior scenario is value-identical.

Fact.Name: Total miles the vehicle was driven in 2025 (all purposes)
Fact.Description: The total miles driven for ALL purposes in 2025 (business + commuting + other = Schedule C Part IV line 44a + 44b + 44c), the denominator of the business-use percentage for the actual-expense method. OPTIONAL — used only when the actual-expense method is elected. Business miles are /writableBusinessMilesDriven (Part IV line 44a), reused so both methods share one business-miles intake.

Fact.Name: Total actual vehicle operating costs in 2025 (all-purpose, before business-use %)
Fact.Description: The TOTAL (all-purpose) actual operating costs of the car or truck for 2025 — gasoline, oil, repairs, insurance, license plates/registration, etc. — before the business-use percentage is applied. "Include on line 9 the business portion of expenses for gasoline, oil, repairs, insurance, license plates, etc." (i1040sc Line 9). SCOPE-OUT (surfaced, never silent): DEPRECIATION and section 179 belong on Schedule C line 13, and rent/lease payments on line 20a — NOT on line 9 (i1040sc Line 9: "Show depreciation on line 13 and rent or lease payments on line 20a. Do not deduct depreciation, rent or lease payments"). Those ride in /writableTotalExpenses (attested, same double-count discipline as the mileage writable), so this fact is line-9 operating costs only.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 9 — standard-mileage amount
Fact.Description: Business miles × the 2025 standard mileage rate of 70 cents per mile ("Multiply the number of business miles driven by 0.70. For example, 1,250 business miles driven × 0.70 = $875.00" — i1040sc). The standard-mileage branch of the line-9 method Switch (factored out here so line 9 can gate between standard mileage and actual expense). Complete-safe 0 when the miles question is unanswered. Whole-dollar rounded like every Schedule C line. Parking fees and tolls (which the instructions add to line 9 under this method) are ../writableParkingFeesAndTolls, added in ../carTruckExpenses.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 9 — actual-expense amount (business portion of operating costs)
Fact.Description: The actual-expense branch of the line-9 method Switch. Deductible line-9 amount = business-use percentage × total operating costs, where the business-use percentage = business miles ÷ total miles (Pub 463 ch.4, referenced by i1040sc Line 9). The exact ratio is applied to the Dollar operating-cost total and the product is rounded once to whole dollars (Schedule C rounds every line). Complete-safe 0 when the method is not elected (so this fact resolves 0 on every non-electing scenario, additive) and 0 when total miles is unanswered or zero (guards the divide-by-zero; a valid actual-expense election answers business miles, total miles, and operating costs). SCOPE-OUT: only the operating-cost portion is on line 9 — depreciation (line 13) and lease (line 20a) are excluded, per /writableActualVehicleOperatingCosts.

Fact.Name: Business parking fees and tolls (Schedule C line 9)
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "How much did you pay in parking fees and tolls for business use of your car or truck in 2025?" HELP TEXT: include parking and tolls for business trips only; parking at your regular place of work is commuting and is not deductible. Do not include these amounts in your actual operating costs or in your total expenses: they are added to line 9 here, with either the standard mileage rate or actual expenses. ASKED WHEN: this business has car or truck expenses (business miles answered). UNANSWERED POSTURE: $0. VALIDATION: Dollar, at least $0. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../parkingFeesAndTollsOrZero, a term of ../carTruckExpenses (Schedule C line 9).

Fact.Name: Business parking fees and tolls as entered, or $0
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of ../writableParkingFeesAndTolls: its value when answered (not below $0), else $0. A term of ../carTruckExpenses under either line 9 method.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 9 — car and truck expenses (method-gated)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 9, gated on the annual method election. When the actual-expense method is elected (/electsActualVehicleExpenseComplete) the amount is the business portion of operating costs (/scheduleCActualCarTruckExpense); otherwise (unelected / standard mileage) it is the standard-mileage amount (/scheduleCStandardMileageAmount) — the default. Both branches are already whole-dollar rounded, so no further rounding here. Business parking fees and tolls (../parkingFeesAndTollsOrZero) are added under either method: the instructions add them to the standard mileage amount, and under actual expenses a business trip's parking and tolls are wholly business, not a share of operating costs. World #1 additivity: with no election answered this equals /scheduleCStandardMileageAmount exactly, so every prior Schedule C golden is byte-identical.

Fact.Name: All investment in the Schedule C business is at risk (Schedule C line 32a / 32b)
Fact.Description: True when the taxpayer is FULLY at risk for the Schedule C business within the meaning of IRC §465 — all investment in the activity is at risk, so no Form 6198 At-Risk Limitation applies and the full line-31 loss is deductible (line 32a). When false, the simplified amount at risk (/writableScheduleCAmountAtRisk, Form 6198 line 10b) caps the deductible loss (Form 6198 line 21) — line 32b. When unanswered on a business with a profit, nothing turns on it. When unanswered on a business with a loss, line 31 is not determined and the return is held (../lossAtRiskAndParticipationAnswered names the hold in flow:/flowIncomplete): the instructions ask the box before the loss is figured, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 15 ("Figuring your loss. Before determining your loss, check"). Mirrors /rentalProperties/*/fullyAtRisk and /formK1s/*/fullyAtRisk (both scheduleE) — the third instance of this pattern, not a new one. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Amount at risk in the Schedule C business (Form 6198 Part II line 10b)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's amount at risk in the Schedule C business from the SIMPLIFIED computation (Form 6198 Part II line 10b): adjusted basis on the first day of the year + increases − decreases, entered as not less than zero. Supplied directly as a single input — the line-by-line Part II build (and the detailed Part III) is not modelled, same as /rentalProperties/*/amountAtRisk and /formK1s/*/amountAtRisk (both scheduleE). Consulted ONLY when /writableScheduleCAllInvestmentAtRisk is answered AND false. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: The §465 at-risk limitation applies to the Schedule C loss (Form 6198 required)
Fact.Description: Box 32b for the at-risk rules: TRUE when ../writableAllInvestmentAtRisk is answered false (some investment is not at risk, so Form 6198 caps the deductible loss at the amount at risk), FALSE when it is answered true (32a). Incomplete while line 32 is unanswered: the instructions ask the box before the loss is determined (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 15 "Figuring your loss. Before determining your loss, check"), so it no longer defaults to "no limitation". ../atRiskCappedNetProfit reads the answer with its own IsComplete guard, so a business with a profit is unaffected by an unanswered line 32.

Fact.Name: Schedule C net profit or loss before the §465 at-risk limitation (line 31, unlimited)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 31 BEFORE any at-risk limitation: line 29 tentative profit minus line 30 business use of home. May be a loss (negative). This is the figure before the at-risk boundary; it now feeds the at-risk cap instead of being the final answer. The computed line-9 standard mileage sits on the expense side (inside line 29); line 29 is split out and the simplified-method line 30 is subtracted here (both terms complete-safe 0 when their intakes are unanswered — prior scenarios value-identical). CENTS KEPT: no whole-dollar Round here, so lines 29 and 31 equal the printed line 7 (in cents) less line 28 and line 30 exactly; a return rounds all its amounts or none (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 23 "round to whole dollars, you must round"). The return-level /scheduleCNetProfit still rounds the Schedule 1 line 3 total.

Fact.Name: Schedule C loss before the at-risk limitation, as a positive amount (Form 6198 line 5)
Fact.Description: The Schedule C business's current-year loss as a POSITIVE amount (Form 6198 Part I line 5 loss): when /scheduleCPreAtRiskNetProfit is negative this is its absolute value; otherwise 0. The pre-at-risk loss magnitude — the input to the Form 6198 line-21 smaller-of test. Mirrors /rentalProperties/*/rawLoss.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C business's net profit or loss after the §465 at-risk limitation only
Fact.Description: ../preAtRiskNetProfit, CAPPED by the §465 at-risk limitation when ../atRiskLimitationApplies and the pre-cap figure is a loss. THIS WAS ../netProfit's OWN BODY before the §469 passive-activity layer landed — every word of that fact's prior Description applies here unchanged, including the per-business migration history. ../netProfit now reads this fact and applies one further limitation on top. A loss with line 32 unanswered (neither 32a nor 32b) is Incomplete here, not passed through as fully at risk: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 15 ("Figuring your loss. Before determining your loss, check").

Fact.Name: The §469 passive-activity loss limitation applies to this business (Schedule C line G, No, and a loss)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the filer answered Schedule C line G "No" (../writableMateriallyParticipated false) AND ../atRiskCappedNetProfit (the loss after the section 465 at-risk cap) is a loss: THIS business has a passive activity loss that Form 8582 limits. INFORMATIONAL since FED-1040SC-LINEG-PASSIVE-LOSS-028: ../netProfit no longer suspends on this flag; it applies the Schedule C passive pool (../section469SuspendedPassiveLoss), which allows the loss up to the passive income. FALSE when line G is Yes or the business has no loss; Incomplete while line G is unanswered on a loss (the same hold ../lossAtRiskAndParticipationAnswered names).

Fact.Name: This business's share of the unallowed passive activity loss (Form 8582 Part VII column (c))
Fact.Description: The part of THIS business's passive loss that IRC 469 does not allow this year, as a POSITIVE amount: the Schedule C passive activity loss (/scheduleCPassiveActivityLossDisallowed, the aggregate passive losses over the aggregate passive income, IRC 469(d)(1)) times this business's share of the aggregate losses (../passiveActivityLoss over /scheduleCPassiveActivityLossTotal), rounded to the cent. That is Form 8582 Part VII: column (b) divides each individual loss by the total of the losses, and column (c) multiplies each ratio by the passive activity loss (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8582.pdf, page 12 "Column (b). Divide each of the individual losses shown"; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8582.pdf, page 13 "Multiply each ratio in column (b) by the amount on line"). $0 for a business the filer materially participated in (line G Yes), for a passive business with a profit, and for every passive loss when the passive income covers the losses. The allowed loss (../netProfit) is the loss less this amount. Incomplete while the pool itself is undetermined (a line G or line 32 answer the pool needs is missing). IRC 469(b) carries this amount to 2026; no 2026 fact reads it back in (no prior-year unallowed loss intake exists). The pool is the Schedule C businesses only; a passive Schedule C beside passive income or a suspended passive loss in the Schedule E pool is refused by /knockoutScheduleCPassiveActivityNotPooled.

Fact.Name: This business's passive income (Form 8582 Part V column (a))
Fact.Description: THIS business's profit after the at-risk rules (../atRiskCappedNetProfit above $0) when it is a passive activity: line G answered No, a trade or business in which the filer does not materially participate (IRC 469(c)(1)). $0 when line G is Yes, and $0 for a business with a loss (its loss is ../passiveActivityLoss), including a loss with line G unanswered (that business's own line 31 is held instead). Incomplete when line G is unanswered on a business with a profit: whether that profit is passive income that frees another business's passive loss is unknown, so /scheduleCPassiveActivityIncomeTotal waits for the answer. Read only by that total.

Fact.Name: This business's passive loss, as a positive amount (Form 8582 Part V column (b))
Fact.Description: THIS business's loss after the at-risk rules (../atRiskCappedNetProfit below $0), as a positive amount, when it is a passive activity (line G answered No). $0 when line G is Yes and $0 for a business with no loss. Incomplete when the business has a loss and line G is unanswered, or when line 32 is unanswered on a loss (../atRiskCappedNetProfit is then Incomplete): the pool cannot be figured without them. Read by /scheduleCPassiveActivityLossTotal and ../section469SuspendedPassiveLoss.

Fact.Name: A Schedule C loss has line G and line 32 answered (a flow:/flowIncomplete reason)
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when THIS business shows a loss before the at-risk rules (../preAtRiskNetProfit below $0) and line G (material participation) or line 32 (32a all investment at risk, 32b some not at risk) is unanswered. Line G decides whether the loss is a passive activity loss that Form 8582 limits (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 5 "Limit on losses. Your business activity loss may be limited if"), and the instructions ask the line 32 box before the loss is determined (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 15 "Figuring your loss. Before determining your loss, check"). Line 31 (../netProfit) is Incomplete on the same population. TRUE on a business with a profit or no loss, and when both are answered.

Fact.Name: Every regular-method home office answers Form 8829 line 2 (flow:/flowIncomplete member)
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when any Schedule C elects the regular (Form 8829) method (/scheduleCs/*/electsRegularHomeOfficeMethodComplete) and leaves Form 8829 line 2, the total area of the home (/scheduleCs/*/writableHomeOfficeTotalArea), unanswered: line 3 divides line 1 by line 2 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8829.pdf, page 1 "Divide line 1 by line 2"), so the business percentage, line 36 and Schedule C line 30 (/scheduleCs/*/homeOfficeRegularDeduction) are not determined. TRUE otherwise, including on a return with no Schedule C list.

Fact.Name: Statutory employee wages are on their own Schedule C (flow:/flowIncomplete member, IN-280)
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when a Schedule C carries the box 1 wages of a linked statutory employee Form W-2 and also other gross receipts on line 1 (/knockoutScheduleCStatutoryEmployeeWagesCombinedWithOtherReceipts true). The reason directs the filer to a second Schedule C: "If you had both self-employment income and statutory employee income, you must file two Schedules C. You cannot combine these amounts on a single Schedule C" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 5). Two Schedules C compute: the statutory one stays off Schedule SE and the other is charged self-employment tax. Ruling IN-280: the combined schedule is an entry the instructions forbid, so no figure computed from it is the tax; it is held with this named reason (row FED-1040SC-LINE1-STATUTORY-COMMINGLING-060). TRUE on every other return.

Fact.Name: Every Schedule C loss has line G and line 32 answered (flow:/flowIncomplete member)
Fact.Description: FALSE, and the return held with this as its reason in flow:/flowIncomplete, when any Schedule C on the return shows a loss with line G or line 32 unanswered (/scheduleCs/*/lossAtRiskAndParticipationAnswered false on that business); line 31 of that business is Incomplete on the same population. TRUE on a return with no Schedule C list, and when every business either shows no loss or answers both lines.

Fact.Name: Schedule C passive income, all businesses (Form 8582, the Schedule C income in Part I)
Fact.Description: The sum of /scheduleCs/*/passiveActivityIncome: the profit of every Schedule C the filer did not materially participate in (line G No). IRC 469(d)(1)(B)'s aggregate passive income, limited to Schedule C; a return whose Schedule E pool also holds passive activity is refused by /knockoutScheduleCPassiveActivityNotPooled. $0 when the Schedule C list is unanswered or empty.

Fact.Name: Schedule C passive losses, all businesses, as a positive amount (Form 8582 Part VII column (a) total)
Fact.Description: The sum of /scheduleCs/*/passiveActivityLoss: the loss, after the at-risk rules, of every Schedule C the filer did not materially participate in (line G No). IRC 469(d)(1)(A)'s aggregate passive losses, limited to Schedule C, and the denominator of each business's Form 8582 Part VII column (b) ratio. $0 when the Schedule C list is unanswered or empty.

Fact.Name: Schedule C passive activity loss disallowed this year (IRC 469(d)(1))
Fact.Description: The passive activity loss of IRC 469(d)(1): the amount, if any, by which the aggregate Schedule C passive losses (/scheduleCPassiveActivityLossTotal) exceed the aggregate Schedule C passive income (/scheduleCPassiveActivityIncomeTotal); $0 when the income covers the losses. IRC 469(a)(1) disallows it, and Form 8582 Part VII allocates it to the loss businesses (/scheduleCs/*/section469SuspendedPassiveLoss).

Fact.Name: This Schedule C business's own net profit or loss (its line 31)
Fact.Description:
Schedule C line 31 for THIS sole proprietorship: ../atRiskCappedNetProfit (line 29 less line 30, after the section 465 at-risk rules), with the passive activity loss rules of IRC 469 applied to a loss. A profit is line 31 as figured. A loss with line G Yes (material participation) is line 31 as figured. A loss with line G No is a passive activity loss: the loss less this business's share of the unallowed passive activity loss (../section469SuspendedPassiveLoss), so passive Schedule C losses are allowed up to the passive Schedule C income on the return and the excess is allocated ratably to the loss businesses (IRC 469(d)(1), 26 U.S.C. 469, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title26-section469&num=0&edition=prelim "the aggregate losses from all passive activities for the taxable year, exceed"; Form 8582 Part VII, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8582.pdf, page 12 "Column (b). Divide each of the individual losses shown"). Example: business A loses 4,000 and business B earns 4,000, both line G No: the passive activity loss is 0 and A's line 31 is the whole 4,000 loss.
HOLDS. A loss with line G unanswered, or with line 32 unanswered (neither 32a nor 32b), is Incomplete here, and ../lossAtRiskAndParticipationAnswered names the hold in flow:/flowIncomplete: line G decides whether the loss is passive (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 5 "Limit on losses. Your business activity loss may be limited if"), and the line 32 box is checked before the loss is determined (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 15 "Figuring your loss. Before determining your loss, check"). An unanswered line G or line 32 on a business with a profit holds nothing.
THE POOL IS SCHEDULE C ONLY. Passive income or a suspended passive loss in the Schedule E pool (rentals, Schedule K-1s) does not net against this pool; such a return is refused by /knockoutScheduleCPassiveActivityNotPooled. A prior-year unallowed passive loss of a Schedule C business has no intake. Body history: this was the return-level /scheduleCBusinessNetProfit, which was itself the former body of /scheduleCNetProfit; until FED-1040SC-LINEG-PASSIVE-LOSS-028 a passive loss was suspended in full whatever passive income the return held.
THE CAP IS PER-BUSINESS, AND THE MIGRATION IS WHAT MAKES THAT LITERAL. Section 465 measures the amount at risk in one ACTIVITY, so capping a combined multi-business loss against a single amount at risk was never the form's arithmetic; before the migration the model could not express the difference because there was only ever one business. It now applies each item's own ../writableAmountAtRisk to that item's own loss, and /scheduleCNetProfit sums the capped results. At zero or one item — every committed return — that is the identical expression.
On every return with no working interest and a single business this equals /scheduleCNetProfit exactly.

Fact.Name: A statutory employee W-2 is reported on THIS Schedule C
Fact.Description:
True when at least one W-2 has box 13 checked AND names THIS /scheduleCs item as the Schedule C its box 1 is reported on. The Boolean half of the route; the Dollar half is ../statutoryEmployeeWagesFromLinkedW2s below.
TWO GUARDS, BOTH LOAD BEARING. (1) The outer IsComplete on /formW2s: CountOperator returns Incomplete on any Incomplete element and an absent collection resolves Placeholder, so a return with no W-2 section answered would otherwise make this Placeholder and carry that into Schedule C line 1. FALSE is the true answer there, not merely a safe one: a return with no W-2s has no statutory employee wages. (2) The HEAD of the All is formW2s:/formW2s/*/isStatutoryEmployeeRoutedToScheduleC, which is always Complete; AllOperator short circuits on a Complete false head, so the Equal against an unanswered link is never forced. Drop that conjunct and this fact goes Incomplete on every ordinary return, because the link is deliberately un Placeholdered.
TYPE: Boolean, complete safe FALSE. False on every committed return, none of which checks box 13.

Fact.Name: Box 1 of the statutory employee W-2s reported on THIS Schedule C
Fact.Description:
The sum of formW2s:/formW2s/*/statutoryEmployeeWagesToScheduleC over the W-2s that name THIS /scheduleCs item, cents preserved. THE AMOUNT THAT MOVED: the printed instruction says to enter statutory employee box 1 on line 1 of Schedule C, and this is that entry, taken from the W-2 rather than asked again. formW2s:/wages subtracts the same per W-2 figures from Form 1040 line 1a through the same gate, so the box 1 amount lands on exactly one line of the return.
A LEG OF LINE 1, NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR IT. ../scheduleCGrossIncome still reads ../writableGrossReceipts as a BARE dependency and this is added beside it. Two reasons, and the second is not obvious: (a) this module never silently ignores an answered intake, so a filer who types the wages into gross receipts AS WELL is left with a VISIBLE double entry rather than a silently discarded answer, the same posture qbi records for two businesses sharing one Schedule C; (b) qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/scheduleCLinkResolves load bears on that bare minuend, testing an unanswered Schedule C by the Incompleteness line 31 inherits from it. A substitutive Switch would have made an unanswered statutory Schedule C Complete and defeated that guard one module over. A statutory employee Schedule C therefore still wants its gross receipts answered, at $0, which is this family's ordinary prompt posture.
MULTIPLE W-2s ON ONE SCHEDULE C ARE SUMMED, deliberately. The two schedules rule separates statutory employee income from self employment income; it does not require a separate Schedule C per statutory employer, so two W-2s from the same trade may share one business.
COMPLETE SAFE $0, by the same two guards ../hasLinkedStatutoryEmployeeW2 documents: the outer IsComplete on /formW2s keeps an absent W-2 collection out of the sum (SumOperator, like Count, is Incomplete on any Incomplete element), and the always Complete routing gate in All head position keeps the Equal against an unanswered link unforced. $0 on every committed return.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C reports statutory employee income, complete safe
Fact.Description:
Complete safe reading of ../writableIsStatutoryEmployeeIncome, the Schedule C line 1 checkbox: that intake's value when the box was answered, else false. It is the gate ../primaryFilerNetProfit and ../secondaryFilerNetProfit apply before handing this business's line 31 to Schedule SE line 2.
UNANSWERED MEANS NOT A STATUTORY EMPLOYEE, which is the pre existing behaviour exactly: every committed scenario leaves the checkbox unanswered, so this resolves Complete false and every committed Schedule SE line 2, self employment tax and total tax figure is byte identical. IsComplete never propagates incompleteness, so no return is made Incomplete by the gate.
WHY A WRAPPER AND NOT A DIRECT READ: the checkbox is an optional Boolean intake, so a bare Dependency on it inside a When would make the two Schedule SE feeder facts Incomplete on every return that never saw the question. Same one box idiom as ../line35InventoryAtBeginningOfYearEntered and form8396:/form8396CarryforwardIn2022.
DERIVED FIRST, ATTESTATION AS FALLBACK. The first case is now ../hasLinkedStatutoryEmployeeW2: when a W-2 with box 13 checked names THIS business, this is TRUE without asking. ../writableIsStatutoryEmployeeIncome is KEPT and is still the answer on every other return, so nothing that ships today changes and every committed scenario, none of which checks box 13, still reads the attestation and resolves false. The predicate the fallback sits behind is a real question about a real source (is there such a W-2 on this return), not IsComplete on a complete safe fact.
THE DERIVED ARM WINS OVER AN ANSWERED ATTESTATION, and that is the OPPOSITE of the "the answer always wins" rule qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/hasQbiAnswer states one collection over. The distinction is what the answer is ABOUT. There, the filer is answering an AMOUNT the graph could also derive, and a filer who knows better must be able to override it. Here, the attestation is a CONSEQUENCE of a document the return already carries: if a W-2 on this return has box 13 checked and names this Schedule C, then this Schedule C reports statutory employee income, and a filer who unchecks the box is not exercising judgment but contradicting the W-2. Letting the attestation win would un gate ../primaryFilerNetProfit and charge self employment tax on wages from which social security and Medicare tax were already withheld, which is the exact wrong answer /flowKnockoutStatutoryEmployee exists to prevent.
THE ATTESTATION IS NOT RETIRED, and the reason is that its arm is still reachable: the W-2 link is new, an imported or partly answered W-2 section may carry no link at all, and a filer may reach the Schedule C checkbox before the W-2 that explains it. DISPOSITION keep-fallback: the attestation still answers every Schedule C that no linked statutory employee W-2 points at.

Fact.Name: This business's line 31 when it is a STATUTORY EMPLOYEE Schedule C, else $0
Fact.Description:
This Schedule C's own line 31 (../netProfit) when ../isStatutoryEmployeeIncome, and $0 when it is not. The per item half of /statutoryEmployeeScheduleCNetProfit below.
WHAT IT IS FOR, and it is a single printed instruction. Every earned-income worksheet that collects Schedule C line 31 says to leave a statutory employee's line 31 out of that collection, because the SAME income is collected on its own line as Schedule C LINE 1 instead: Schedule 8812's Earned Income Worksheet line 2b, "Do not include on this line any statutory employee income or any other amounts exempt from self-employment tax", against its line 2a, "Enter any statutory employee income reported on line 1 of Schedule C"; and EIC Worksheet B Part 2's "Don't include on these lines any statutory employee income" against Part 3's "Enter the amount from Schedule C, line 1, that you are filing as a statutory employee". This fact is the amount those exclusions name, so a consumer that collects line 31 can subtract it by name.
THE EIC SIDE ALREADY HAD ITS ANSWER AND DID NOT NEED THIS FACT; the Schedule 8812 side did. scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome answers Worksheet B Part 2 by summing the GATED per filer totals /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit and /secondaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit, which are already $0 on a statutory business through ../primaryFilerNetProfit's gate. Its section 24(d) twin scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax cannot do the same, because its minuend is /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax, a RETURN LEVEL net that has no per filer gated form: the section 931/933 exclusion it carries is not partitioned by filer. So the exclusion is expressed there as an explicit subtrahend, and this fact is that subtrahend's per item term.
SIGNED, deliberately: line 2b says "net profit or (loss)", so a statutory business's LOSS must come out of the collection too. Not floored here.
TYPE: Dollar, complete safe $0 - the gate is complete safe FALSE and ../netProfit is complete safe, so this is Complete $0 on every committed return, none of which checks box 13 or the Schedule C line 1 checkbox.
GATE CORRECTED: an earlier draft gated on ../isStatutoryEmployeeIncome, whose ATTESTATION arm reaches Schedule Cs with NO linked box-13 W-2 - a population the narrowed guard does not refuse and the 2a add-back (route-gate-keyed) does not cover, so the 2b subtraction alone dropped that filable return's line 18a by the whole net profit (measured 60,000 -> 20,000, taxpayer-adverse). Now gated on ../hasLinkedStatutoryEmployeeW2, the SAME routed population 2a adds back, so 2a and 2b always fire together and the attestation-only population keeps its pre-existing treatment (line 31 rides the SE line into 18a - imperfect against the worksheet's line-1 answer, the SAME pre-existing gap the EIC side carries, named as the attestation-only follow-up unit rather than half-fixed here).
THE FOLLOW-UP UNIT IS BUILT AND THE GATE IS BACK TO ../isStatutoryEmployeeIncome. The paragraph above is kept as record, and the sentence it ends on is DISCHARGED rather than falsified: the 2a add-back it said the attestation-only population lacked EXISTS as of this unit (../primaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeLine1 and its secondary twin below, summed into /primaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeScheduleCLine1 and reaching every 2a-analog through income:/statutoryEmployeeWagesInEarnedIncome and income:/primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages). F1's INVARIANT is what forces the gate back: 2a and 2b must fire together over the SAME population, and with 2a now covering both arms a 2b keyed on the route alone would leave an attestation-only business's line 31 inside the collection AND add its line 1 beside it - the double count 2b exists to prevent, in the taxpayer-favourable direction this time. ../isStatutoryEmployeeIncome is exactly the union of the two arms, so the two lines cover one population again.
THE VALUE THAT MOVES, named per the value-movement rule. Node fixture tests/nodes/ty2025/income/statutory-attestation-only-schedule-c-keeps-pre-existing-18a: an attested Schedule C (line 1 50,000, expenses 10,000, line 31 40,000) beside a NON-statutory W-2 of 20,000. This fact 0 -> 40,000, /statutoryEmployeeScheduleCNetProfit 0 -> 40,000, scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax 40,000 -> 0, Schedule 8812 line 18a 60,000 -> 70,000. 70,000 is the printed worksheet's own foot: line 1a 20,000 plus line 2a 50,000 (Schedule C LINE 1) plus line 2b 0. The old 60,000 answered line 2b with the very line 31 the worksheet tells you to leave out, and answered line 2a with nothing at all. The committed corpus is untouched: no scenario checks either box.

Fact.Name: This business's Schedule C line 1 when it is an ATTESTATION-ONLY statutory Schedule C of the PRIMARY filer, else $0
Fact.Description:
../writableGrossReceipts when ALL of: this return claims Schedule C income, ../isStatutoryEmployeeIncome, NOT ../hasLinkedStatutoryEmployeeW2, and ../belongsToPrimaryFiler. $0 otherwise. The per item half of /primaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeScheduleCLine1 below.
WHY ../writableGrossReceipts IS LINE 1 HERE, and it is exact rather than approximate. Line 1 of Schedule C is modelled as the minuend of ../scheduleCGrossIncome (line 7): the bare ../writableGrossReceipts PLUS ../statutoryEmployeeWagesFromLinkedW2s. Under this fact's Not(../hasLinkedStatutoryEmployeeW2) conjunct that second leg is identically $0 - it sums only over W-2s that name THIS business, and by hypothesis none does - so on this population line 1 and the intake coincide. Lines 2, 4 and 6 are lines 2, 4 and 6; they belong to line 7 and the worksheet asks for line 1.
READ BARE UNDER A COMPLETE SAFE GATE, the same posture ../statutoryEmployeeNetProfit takes on ../netProfit. The gate resolves Complete false on every committed return — though NOT because all four conjuncts are unconditionally complete-safe (../belongsToPrimaryFiler's own block in this file names two states where it is not; what protects this fact is ARM ORDER — the two checkbox conjuncts sit ahead of belongsTo* and AllOperator short-circuits on a Complete false, so a return that never checks the statutory box never evaluates the fragile conjunct). The first three conjuncts are complete safe (/claimsScheduleCIncome and ../isStatutoryEmployeeIncome are IsComplete wrappers, ../hasLinkedStatutoryEmployeeW2 has its own two guards, ../belongsToPrimaryFiler is the Not of a complete safe Boolean), so an unanswered return takes the False fallthrough and this is Complete $0. An answered checkbox with unanswered receipts is Incomplete here - deliberately, and it costs nothing: that same return is already Incomplete through ../netProfit at line 2b — and on the per-filer 2441/section-219 chain this fact now also feeds, the same input state is unfilable by a different route: writableGrossReceipts is read bare inside scheduleCGrossIncome, so line 31, /scheduleCNetProfit, /totalIncome and AGI are all Incomplete and the return cannot file — so an IsComplete-to-$0 arm would only buy a return that adds nothing at 2a while excluding nothing at 2b, which is the worse half of the pair rather than a safer one.
SIGNED? NO FLOOR AND NO SIGN QUESTION. Line 1 is gross receipts, a receipts line; unlike the line 2b amount it is not a "profit or (loss)". Negative receipts are not a thing the intake admits.
CENTS PRESERVED, not Rounded: the consumers round at their own printed lines, which is what income:/statutoryEmployeeWagesInEarnedIncome's readers and the per filer earned income pair already do with the routed sums.
THE PRIMARY/SECONDARY SPLIT is ../belongsToPrimaryFiler's, the same partition ../primaryFilerNetProfit uses, and it is needed because Form 2441's earned income is figured per spouse ("If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately") and because IRC 32(c)(2)(B)(i) computes an individual's earned income without regard to community property laws. An unanswered proprietor routes the business to the primary filer, which is the collection's own back compat default.
TYPE: Dollar, complete safe $0 on every committed return - none checks the Schedule C line 1 checkbox (1,538 statutoryEmployee occurrences across scenarios/, 0 true, re-measured this session).

Fact.Name: This business's Schedule C line 1 when it is an ATTESTATION-ONLY statutory Schedule C of the SECONDARY filer, else $0
Fact.Description:
The secondary (MFJ spouse) twin of ../primaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeLine1, which carries the full reading of why ../writableGrossReceipts IS Schedule C line 1 on this population, why the population excludes the routed businesses and why the amount is read bare under a complete safe gate. Identical but for ../belongsToSecondaryFiler in place of ../belongsToPrimaryFiler.
THE TWO FIELDS PARTITION every attested business's line 1 exactly once, because ../belongsToPrimaryFiler is defined as the Not of ../belongsToSecondaryFiler - the same property ../primaryFilerNetProfit and ../secondaryFilerNetProfit rely on. Nothing can drop out of the pair and nothing can appear in both.

Fact.Name: This business's line 31, as a term of the PRIMARY filer's Schedule SE line 2
Fact.Description:
This Schedule C's own line 31 (../netProfit) when the PRIMARY filer is its proprietor, and $0 when he is not. CollectionSum over this field is the primary's Schedule SE line-2 Schedule C term (/primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit below). The per-item half of the filer partition, and the shape the migration needed: Schedule SE is a per-INDIVIDUAL form (IRC 1402) but Schedule C is per-BUSINESS, so the join between them is a sum over the businesses one individual owns — which cannot be written at all while there is a single return-level business. Mirrors scheduleE:/rentalProperties/*/activeEligibleNet (a per-item Switch summed at the top level) rather than a Filter, so no per-item incompleteness can make the filtered COLLECTION itself Placeholder.
SIGNED: a loss stays negative here so it nets against that filer's other self-employment income on his own Schedule SE line 3 ("if you had a loss in one business, it reduces the income from another"), and is floored only later on his line 4a/4c. It does NOT carry the working interest — that is added once, at the return level, on /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit itself.
STATUTORY EMPLOYEE GATE: $0 also when ../isStatutoryEmployeeIncome, the complete safe reading of the Schedule C line 1 checkbox. Social security and Medicare tax were already withheld from statutory employee wages, so the Line 31 instruction sends that line 31 to Schedule 1 line 3 and expressly keeps it off Schedule SE line 2; before this edit the chain ../netProfit to here to /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit to /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine2 had no such gate anywhere and charged the tax. The gate is on THIS fact rather than on ../netProfit because line 31 itself is unaffected — only its Schedule SE leg is. Complete safe, so every committed return is byte identical.

Fact.Name: This business's line 31, as a term of the SECONDARY filer's Schedule SE line 2
Fact.Description:
This Schedule C's own line 31 (../netProfit) when the SECONDARY (MFJ spouse) filer is its proprietor, and $0 when she is not. The complement of ../primaryFilerNetProfit above; because ../belongsToPrimaryFiler is defined as the NOT of ../belongsToSecondaryFiler, the two fields PARTITION this business's line 31 — exactly one of them carries it — so no profit can be dropped from, or double-counted into, the self-employment-tax computation. Signed, for the same reason as the primary term. Does not carry the working interest.
STATUTORY EMPLOYEE GATE: the twin of the one on ../primaryFilerNetProfit — $0 also when ../isStatutoryEmployeeIncome. Both feeders carry it, so a statutory employee Schedule C contributes 0 to BOTH Schedule SEs rather than migrating to the other spouse's; the partition is preserved in the sense that matters, which is that no line 31 reaches a Schedule SE twice and none reaches the wrong one.

Fact.Name: Allowed section 179 deduction included in this Schedule C business's net profit
Fact.Description: The allowed section 179 deduction already inside THIS business's line 13 and so inside its line 31: the filer's answer (../writableSection179ExpenseIncludedInNetProfit) when given; otherwise, when the business names its Form 4562 copy (../writableForm4562CopyNumber), that copy's line 12, the section 179 amount allocated to it, which its line 22 carries to line 13 ($0 when the copy's line 12 is unanswered). Incomplete when neither is known: the graph cannot tell how much of an entered line 13 is section 179.

Fact.Name: Allowed section 179 deductions included in all Schedule C net profits
Fact.Description: Sum of the current-year allowed section 179 deductions already included in each Schedule C business's net profit (/scheduleCs/*/section179IncludedInNetProfit: the filer's answer, else the linked Form 4562 copy's line 12). This is a pre-limit line-11 input, not another deduction. Complete $0 when /scheduleCs is unanswered; Incomplete while any business's amount is unknown, rather than silently assuming that a mixed line-13 expense was all regular depreciation.

Fact.Name: Schedule C business-income contribution before the included section 179 deduction
Fact.Description: Pre-section-179 view of /scheduleCNetProfit for Form 4562 line 11: the current Schedule C net profit (including the off-collection working-interest term) plus the allowed section 179 deductions already included in the separate Schedule C business net profits. The underlying line 31, Schedule 1 income, QBI, and Schedule SE computations are unchanged. Each business's included section 179 amount is its answer or its linked Form 4562 copy's line 12 (/scheduleCs/*/section179IncludedInNetProfit). While one is unknown, this is the plain /scheduleCNetProfit only on a return where no section 179 deduction reads Form 4562 line 11 (scheduleE:/section179ElectingActivityCount is 0, form4562:/form4562Line8TotalElectedCost is $0 and no line 10 carryover is answered above $0), and Incomplete otherwise: Pub. 946 figures the limit without regard to the section 179 deduction, so the post-section-179 profit is never used where it could move one.

Fact.Name: Schedule C net profit or loss
Fact.Description:
Schedule C line 31: line 29 tentative profit minus line 30 business use of home (/scheduleCPreAtRiskNetProfit), CAPPED by the §465 at-risk limitation when /scheduleCAtRiskLimitationApplies and the pre-cap figure is a loss — the SMALLER of /scheduleCRawLoss or /writableScheduleCAmountAtRisk, entered as the loss (negative). A profit is never affected regardless of the at-risk answer (the limitation only ever SHRINKS a loss; Form 6198 has no effect on a positive line 31). Flows to Schedule 1 line 3 / total income with SE tax. This fact CONFLATES "line 31 as filed" with "the amount Form 6198 allows to flow onward" — the vendored form keeps these as two separate steps (line 31 is filed unconditionally; box 32b's Form 6198 line 21 is what actually reaches Schedule 1 line 3 / Schedule SE line 2), but this model has never carried that distinction (the original scope note said plainly "the line-32 at-risk limitation on losses is not modeled"), and /scheduleCNetProfit is mef-exported AND the single point every downstream consumer (the two per-filer Schedule SE terms, /totalIncome, QBI, /section8582Magi) reads — rewiring all of them to a second fact would multiply the risk of an inconsistent partial application for the SAME conflation this codebase already carries elsewhere.
AS OF THE WORKING-INTEREST FILL this is the COMBINED line 31, and as of the collection migration the first term is a SUM: every entered Schedule C's own line 31 (CollectionSum over /scheduleCs/*/netProfit) PLUS scheduleE:/workingInterestNetProfit, an oil or gas working interest routed off Schedule E Part I and deliberately left outside the collection. Combining at line 31 is the form-faithful join: a second trade or business files its own Schedule C, and it is the line 31s that meet at Schedule 1 line 3 and Schedule SE line 2 (Schedule C line 32's own instruction, cited below). Every consumer named above keeps reading this fact; the two per-filer terms below deliberately do NOT read it, and say why.
⚠ THOSE TWO SENTENCES ARE NO LONGER TRUE, AND THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE THEM IS KEPT BECAUSE ITS WARNING WAS HONOURED RATHER THAN OVERRIDDEN. The warning was against a PARTIAL application - moving one consumer to a second fact and leaving the rest. What landed is the opposite: every money consumer was classified against ITS OWN statute in ONE unit, and the table is on /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax. FOUR MOVED to that fact - income:/totalIncome (Schedule 1 line 3), income:/totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi (its dominance bound), socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3 (the Form 1040 line-8 proxy) and scheduleE:/section8582Magi. TWO STAYED ON THIS FACT - scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome, because section 1402(a)(6) computes net earnings from self-employment "without regard to section 933", and scheduleE:/rentalSection179IncomeLimit, because nothing vendored answers it either way. The two per-filer Schedule SE terms are unaffected as always: they sum /scheduleCs/*/primaryFilerNetProfit and /scheduleCs/*/secondaryFilerNetProfit directly. WHAT THIS FACT STILL IS: the mef-exported Schedule C line 31, unchanged in body and in value on every return, and the SELF-EMPLOYMENT-TAX basis. A re-body was never the answer, because section 1402(a)(6) forbids the self-employment tax shrinking when the income tax does. ⚠ THE PRINTED-FORM RESIDUAL, STATED BECAUSE NO PUBLICATION ADJUDICATES IT. This line 31 keeps the combined figure while Schedule 1 line 3 now carries less, and there is NO printed reconciliation line between them. THE CHOICE MADE: line 31 stays whole - its own instruction is "Subtract line 30 from line 29", pure arithmetic on that business's receipts and expenses with no exclusion concept in it - and the exclusion is taken at Schedule 1 line 3, whose content section 933(1) governs ("shall not be included in gross income"). THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, named rather than left implicit: reducing line 31 itself would have made the mef export disagree with the taxpayer's own books AND would have dragged the self-employment tax down with it. DIRECTION OF THE RESIDUAL: NO tax effect - every dollar downstream is on the basis its statute requires - it is a DISCLOSURE gap on the printed return, where line 31 and line 3 differ by the exclusion with nothing on the form naming why. IT IS A MODELLING DECISION AND NOT A TRANSCRIPTION, and the reason no source settles it is structural: Publication 1321's model is that a bona fide resident does not file a Schedule C for the excluded business at all, so the IRS never has to reconcile the two figures. Collecting the exclusion per item is this dictionary's shape, not the IRS's. Tagged ai-only where the choice is taken, on income:/totalIncome.
