THE SINGLE-BUSINESS CONFLATION IS RETIRED FOR SCHEDULE C ITSELF, which is what the migration bought, and the paragraph that used to stand here is corrected rather than preserved: it said this mef-exported line 31 "prints two businesses' net as one" whenever a return carried both a Schedule C business and a working interest, and named that as a second route to oos-schedulec-home-office-depreciation-detail's one-Schedule-C-per-return limit. Entered businesses are now items and each keeps its own line 31, its own home-office gross-income limitation and its own section 465 cap, so the conflation survives only for the WORKING INTEREST, which has no owner intake and therefore no item — one blended figure for one modeled Schedule C plus that activity. Return-level results (total income, self-employment tax, the §179 business-income limit) were never affected, because each is a sum over businesses anyway.
This exported line 31 itself is unchanged, but scheduleE:/rentalSection179IncomeLimit now reads /scheduleCNetProfitBeforeSection179 for its Schedule C term. That companion adds back only each business's allowed §179 deduction already included here; all Schedule 1, QBI, and Schedule SE readers continue using this exact line-31 value. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Schedule C net profit or loss (that filer's Schedule SE line 2)
Fact.Description:
The Schedule C line-31 term of the PRIMARY filer's Schedule SE line 2 — the sum of the line 31s of the businesses that are HIS, and zero for each that is the spouse's. Signed: a loss stays negative here so that it nets against HIS other self-employment income (Schedule SE line 3 combines a filer's own businesses; "if you had a loss in one business, it reduces the income from another"), and is floored only later, on his line 4a/4c. On every return that leaves the proprietor unanswered — which is every committed scenario — this is the whole of every entered business's line 31.
A COLLECTIONSUM SINCE THE MIGRATION, and that is the point of the migration for this fact: Schedule SE is per-INDIVIDUAL and line 3 combines that individual's OWN businesses, which is a sum this could not express while there was a single return-level Schedule C. The per-item term it sums (/scheduleCs/*/primaryFilerNetProfit) carries a business's line 31 only when ../belongsToPrimaryFiler, so the two per-filer facts partition every business's profit exactly once.
TWO TERMS SINCE THE WORKING-INTEREST FILL, and the split is the whole point. The first term is the sum above; the second is scheduleE:/workingInterestNetProfit, added UNCONDITIONALLY. Reading the combined /scheduleCNetProfit here instead would have handed a working interest to whichever spouse /scheduleCs/*/filer names — putting one person's trade or business on the other's Schedule SE, measured against HER wage base, which is the section 1402 per-individual violation this attribution exists to prevent. The working interest goes to the primary filer because the royalty surface carries no owner intake at all (/writableRoyaltyIncome is a return-level scalar), so the primary is the same back-compat default /scheduleCs/*/filer itself takes when unanswered. interpretation:provisional — a working-interest owner intake is the fact that would retire it. No committed scenario answers the proprietor, so this arm is witnessed by the node test scheduleC/working-interest-with-spouse-owned-schedule-c rather than by the corpus.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Schedule C net profit or loss (that filer's Schedule SE line 2)
Fact.Description:
The Schedule C line-31 term of the SECONDARY (MFJ spouse) filer's Schedule SE line 2 — the sum of the line 31s of the businesses that are HERS, and zero for each that is not. This is the fact that closes the mis-attribution the per-filer Schedule SE split disclosed: before it, a spouse-owned Schedule C was enterable and landed silently on the PRIMARY's Schedule SE, measured against HIS line-8a wage base and netted against HIS self-employment income, which section 1402's per-individual computation forbids. Complete-safe 0 on every non-MFJ return and on every return that leaves every proprietor unanswered. Signed, for the same reason as the primary term: her Schedule C loss must net against her OWN K-1 earnings on her own Schedule SE line 3 — that is one person's single computation, not the cross-spouse netting the Community-income paragraph forbids. A CollectionSum since the migration, which is what lets a couple who each run a business file two correct Schedules SE instead of one wrong one.
READS THE BUSINESS FIGURES, NOT THE COMBINED LINE 31, since the working-interest fill: an oil or gas working interest routed here from Schedule E has no owner intake and is attributed to the PRIMARY filer (see that term above), so it must not reach her Schedule SE merely because /scheduleCs/*/filer names her as a business's proprietor. Value-identical on every committed return, all of which carry at most one business and no working interest.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 29 — tentative profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: Line 29 = LINE 7 GROSS INCOME minus line-28 total expenses (the collapsed total plus the computed line-9 standard mileage). Split out of the old line-31 body so the home-office deduction (line 30) can subtract from it AND serve as the simplified method worksheet's line-1 gross income limitation. Complete-safe 0 when Schedule C is not claimed. Equal to the net profit whenever line 30 is 0. CENTS KEPT: no whole-dollar Round here, so lines 29 and 31 equal the printed line 7 (in cents) less line 28 and line 30 exactly; a return rounds all its amounts or none (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 23 "round to whole dollars, you must round"). The return-level /scheduleCNetProfit still rounds the Schedule 1 line 3 total.

Fact.Name: Home office square feet used regularly and exclusively for business, regularly for daycare, or regularly for storage of inventory or product samples (simplified method election)
Fact.Description:
The square footage of the home used regularly for the business (Pub 587 qualified business use — ATTESTED, not modeled). OPTIONAL — answering it IS the year-by-year simplified-method election (i1040sc: "Make the election by using the simplified method to figure the deduction"); unanswered = no home-office claim via this path. The engine applies the 300 sq ft cap (worksheet line 2 "smaller of the square feet you actually used or 300"), UNLESS ../writableHomeOfficeSimplifiedMethodSharedWithOtherBusinesses narrows it — see that fact.
"EXCLUSIVELY" IS NOT ALWAYS REQUIRED, the same two IRC §280A(c) exceptions ../writableHomeOfficeBusinessArea's own Description names for the regular method: storage of inventory or product samples (§280A(c)(2), home must be the sole fixed business location) and daycare (§280A(c)(4) — see ../writableHomeOfficeIsDaycareNotExclusive, whose hours ratio now reduces the simplified method's own $5 rate the same way it reduces the regular method's business percentage).
Part-year monthly averaging (Pub 587 Example 1: 420 sq ft from July 20 averages to 125) is modeled for a start and a stop of business use during the year, via ../simplifiedMethodPartYearMonthsQualifying. SCOPE-OUTS remaining (surfaced, never silent): an area CHANGE during the year that is not a full start or stop; the daycare multi-part-of-home allocation worksheet (same scope-out ../writableHomeOfficeBusinessArea names).

Fact.Name: This home's 300 sq ft simplified-method limit is shared with another qualified business use
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the filer (or spouse) also claims the simplified method for ANOTHER qualified business use of THIS SAME HOME this year — a second Schedule C business, a Schedule F farm, or a partner's Form 8829-equivalent use, all sharing one home. Pub. 587 states the 300 sq ft maximum applies once PER HOME, not once per business: "If you conduct more than one business qualifying for the deduction, you are limited to a maximum of 300 square feet for all of the businesses. Allocate the actual square footage used (up to the maximum of 300 square feet) among your qualified business uses in a reasonable manner. However, do not allocate more square feet to a qualified business use than you actually use for that business." A separate "Shared use" rule covers the same 300 sq ft ceiling being divided between DIFFERENT people (e.g. roommates) sharing one home; this fact's population is the SAME filer's own multiple qualified business uses.
WHY AN INTAKE RATHER THAN A COMPUTATION: this dictionary has no home-identity entity linking two /scheduleCs items (or a Schedule C item to a Schedule F farm) to the SAME physical home, so the fact of sharing — and the allocation itself — cannot be derived from anything already on the return. ATTESTED, the same posture ../writableAllInvestmentAtRisk and the §931/933 territory-income facts take for a cross-item relationship the graph cannot see structurally. Optional; unanswered/false leaves ../writableHomeOfficeSquareFeet at the default full 300 sq ft cap, which is correct for the (overwhelmingly common) single business per home. Asked alongside ../writableHomeOfficeSquareFeet. Feeds ../writableHomeOfficeSimplifiedMethodAllocatedSquareFeet.

Fact.Name: This business's allocated share of the home's 300 sq ft simplified-method limit
Fact.Description: THIS business's reasonable allocation of the home's single 300 sq ft ceiling, when ../writableHomeOfficeSimplifiedMethodSharedWithOtherBusinesses is true — Pub. 587's own worksheet line "Reasonable allocation of line 3c to this qualified business use." The filer allocates the actual combined square footage used across ALL qualified business uses of the home (not to exceed 300 total) among them "in a reasonable manner"; this is that allocated figure for THIS business alone. ../homeOfficeDeductionSimplified uses this instead of the flat 300 cap when it is answered, so two co-located businesses that correctly allocate 150 sq ft each get 150+150=300 sq ft of combined benefit rather than 300+300=600 (the under-charge this fact closes). NOT STRUCTURALLY ENFORCED ACROSS BUSINESSES — the same disclosed gap ../writableHomeOfficeSimplifiedMethodSharedWithOtherBusinesses names: nothing on this return can verify that a sibling business's own allocation, wherever it is filed, sums to 300 or less with this one. Asked when the sharing flag is true, and REQUIRED then: the instructions allow one 300 sq ft maximum for all of the businesses, so a shared home with no allocation leaves ../homeOfficeDeductionSimplified Incomplete rather than giving this business the whole 300.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 30 — business use of home (simplified method body)
Fact.Description:
LAYERED to close three named under-charges: the Simplified Method Worksheet — line 2 = min(square feet, the 300 sq ft cap OR, when this home is shared with another qualified business use of the filer's, ../writableHomeOfficeSimplifiedMethodAllocatedSquareFeet); line 3c = ../simplifiedMethodLine3cRate ($5.00 times the daycare decimal, to two decimal places); line 4 = line 2 × line 3c × ../simplifiedMethodPartYearMonthsQualifying ÷ 12; line 5 = the smaller of the line-1 gross income limitation (../homeOfficeGrossIncomeLimitation: line 29 plus home-use gains less unrelated losses, or, when some income is earned at another place of business, the home-use share of gross income less line 28 and those losses) or line 4, floored at 0.
PER-HOME SHARING: ../writableHomeOfficeSimplifiedMethodSharedWithOtherBusinesses and ../writableHomeOfficeSimplifiedMethodAllocatedSquareFeet let a filer with two co-located businesses cap each one at its OWN allocated share of the home's single 300 sq ft ceiling, rather than each independently claiming the full 300; shared with the allocation unanswered leaves this Incomplete. Unshared (the default): LesserOf(sq ft, 300).
PART-YEAR AVERAGING: the ÷ 12 monthly-averaging term is 1 (12/12) whenever business use ran the whole year; a start or a stop during the year reduces it (../simplifiedMethodPartYearMonthsQualifying).
DAYCARE RATE REDUCTION: Pub. 587's own simplified-method rule for a daycare facility not used exclusively for business — "you must reduce the prescribed rate (maximum $5 per square foot) before figuring your deduction. The reduced rate will equal the prescribed rate times a fraction" — is the SAME ../form8829DaycareHoursRatio the regular method's ../form8829BusinessPercentage now applies, reused rather than re-derived (one quantity, one fact). 1/1 (no reduction) for every non-daycare return, so this term is arithmetically inert except on the population ../writableHomeOfficeIsDaycareNotExclusive names.
Complete-safe 0 when the square-feet question is unanswered. The ORIGINAL (pre-layering) body was lifted UNCHANGED out of the old /scheduleCHomeOfficeDeduction into its own fact so line 30 can gate between the simplified and the Form 8829 regular method.

Fact.Name: All of this business's gross income is from the business use of this home
Fact.Description: QUESTION: "Is all of this business's gross income from your business use of this home?" Answer No when some of the income comes from a place of business other than this home (an office, a shop, a client's site you work from). HELP: the business-use-of-home deduction cannot exceed the gross income from that use of the home, less the business's other expenses. When all of the income is from this home, that limit starts from Schedule C line 29; when some of it is earned elsewhere, only the part earned from the use of this home counts, figured by the time you spend at each location and other facts. ASKED WHEN: a home office is claimed for this business, by the simplified method (../writableHomeOfficeSquareFeet answered) or the regular method (../electsRegularHomeOfficeMethod yes). REQUIRED THEN: unanswered leaves the gross income limitation (../homeOfficeGrossIncomeLimitation), and so Schedule C line 30, Incomplete; nothing guesses Yes, because Yes gives the larger limit. FEEDS: ../homeOfficeGrossIncomeLimitation (Simplified Method Worksheet line 1, Form 8829 line 8).

Fact.Name: The part of this business's gross income from the business use of this home
Fact.Description: QUESTION: "How much of this business's gross income is from your business use of this home?" HELP: start from Schedule C line 7 gross income and the gains from Form 8949 (and Schedule D) and Form 4797 that belong to this business, and enter the part earned from the business use of this home. Consider the time you spend at each location and other facts. ASKED WHEN: ../writableHomeOfficeAllGrossIncomeFromHomeUse is No. REQUIRED THEN: unanswered leaves ../homeOfficeGrossIncomeLimitation, and Schedule C line 30, Incomplete. VALIDATION: Dollar, not below 0, and not more than Schedule C line 7 plus this business's Form 8949 and Form 4797 gains (the screen warns above that). FEEDS: ../homeOfficeGrossIncomeLimitation, which subtracts Schedule C line 28 and the losses in ../writableHomeOfficeLossesNotAllocableToHomeUse from it.

Fact.Name: Gain derived from the business use of this home, shown on Form 8949 or Form 4797
Fact.Description: QUESTION: "Did you have a gain derived from the business use of this home that is reported on Form 8949 (and Schedule D) or Form 4797? If so, how much?" HELP: for example, the business part of a gain on selling the home, or on property used in the business at home. ASKED WHEN: ../writableHomeOfficeAllGrossIncomeFromHomeUse is Yes (when it is No, such gains are already inside ../writableHomeOfficeGrossIncomeFromHomeUse). UNANSWERED: $0, as the printed worksheet line B reads "Enter any gain": a blank printed optional line is a zero, and blank is the smaller limit, never the larger. VALIDATION: Dollar, not below 0. FEEDS: ../homeOfficeGrossIncomeLimitation (worksheet line B; Form 8829 line 8).

Fact.Name: Losses on Form 8949 or Form 4797 allocable to this business but not to the business use of this home
Fact.Description: QUESTION: "Did this business have losses reported on Form 8949 (and Schedule D) or Form 4797 that belong to the business but not to its use of this home? If so, how much (as a positive number)?" HELP: for example, a loss on selling business equipment kept away from the home. ASKED WHEN: a home office is claimed for this business, by either method, whatever the answer to ../writableHomeOfficeAllGrossIncomeFromHomeUse. UNANSWERED: $0. This blank is the TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE direction (a blank loss leaves the limit larger), and it is defaulted because the printed worksheet line D is an optional entry ("Enter the total amount of any losses"), the same reading the printed Form 8829 lines take for a blank optional entry; the question must be put to every home-office filer so the default is only ever a true zero. VALIDATION: Dollar, not below 0. FEEDS: ../homeOfficeGrossIncomeLimitation (worksheet line D; Form 8829 line 8).

Fact.Name: Gross income limitation for the business use of this home (Simplified Method Worksheet line 1; Form 8829 line 8)
Fact.Description: The most the business use of this home can deduct beyond the uncapped mortgage interest and taxes. When all of the business's gross income is from this home (../writableHomeOfficeAllGrossIncomeFromHomeUse Yes): Schedule C line 29 (../tentativeProfit) plus the gain from the business use of the home on Form 8949 or Form 4797 (../writableHomeOfficeGainFromBusinessUseOfHome), minus the losses on those forms allocable to the business but not to the use of the home (../writableHomeOfficeLossesNotAllocableToHomeUse). When some of the income is from another place of business (No): the part of the gross income from the business use of this home (../writableHomeOfficeGrossIncomeFromHomeUse), minus Schedule C line 28 (../line28TotalExpenses), minus the same losses. Incomplete while the Yes/No question, or on No the home-use income, is unanswered. May be negative; each reader floors what it takes. Read by ../homeOfficeDeductionSimplified (worksheet line 1) and ../form8829RemainingLimitAfterMortgageInterestAndTaxes (Form 8829 line 15 = line 8 minus line 14), and printed by form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line8BusinessIncomeLimit.

Fact.Name: Gain from the business use of this home, or $0
Fact.Description: ../writableHomeOfficeGainFromBusinessUseOfHome when answered, floored at $0, else $0 (worksheet line B reads "Enter any gain"). Read by ../homeOfficeGrossIncomeLimitation.

Fact.Name: Losses allocable to the business but not to the use of this home, or $0
Fact.Description: ../writableHomeOfficeLossesNotAllocableToHomeUse when answered, floored at $0, else $0 (worksheet line D reads "Enter the total amount of any losses"). Read by ../homeOfficeGrossIncomeLimitation.

Fact.Name: Simplified Method Worksheet line 3c — the $5 rate times the daycare decimal, to two decimal places
Fact.Description: Line 3a ($5) times line 3b (../form8829DaycareHoursRatio: the Daycare Facility Worksheet decimal for a daycare facility not used exclusively for business, otherwise 1.0), entered to two decimal places as the worksheet prints it, before line 4 multiplies it by the square footage. $5.00 on every non-daycare return. The cents rounding is the Dollar rounding of the product (half-to-even on an exact half cent, which the worksheet does not address). Read by ../homeOfficeDeductionSimplified.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 30 — business use of home (method-gated)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 30, gated on the home-office method election. When the REGULAR (Form 8829) method is elected (/electsRegularHomeOfficeMethodComplete) the amount is the Form 8829 allowable deduction (../homeOfficeRegularDeduction, the layered mortgage-interest-and-taxes / operating-expense / depreciation computation); otherwise (unelected / simplified) it is the Simplified Method Worksheet amount (../homeOfficeDeductionSimplified, the default). Both branches are already whole-dollar rounded, so no further rounding here. With the regular method unelected this equals ../homeOfficeDeductionSimplified exactly.

Fact.Name: Elects the regular (Form 8829) method for business use of home
Fact.Description: The ANNUAL election between the two Schedule C line-30 home-office methods — FALSE / unanswered = the simplified method (the landed default path; $5/sq ft capped at 300 sq ft); TRUE = the regular method on Form 8829 (actual expenses allocated by business-use percentage). "If you are not electing to use the simplified method, use Form 8829 to figure the expenses you can deduct" (i1040sc). OPTIONAL — when unanswered the line-30 amount is exactly the simplified computation, so every prior Schedule C scenario is value-identical. The taxpayer may choose either method year by year; this single-year engine takes the election as given.

Fact.Name: Regular home-office method elected (complete-safe gate)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate mirroring /electsActualVehicleExpenseComplete — true only when /electsRegularHomeOfficeMethod is answered and true. Unanswered resolves Complete false, so the line-30 Switch defaults to the simplified path and every prior scenario is value-identical.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 1 — area used regularly and exclusively for business, regularly for daycare, or for storage of inventory or product samples (sq ft)
Fact.Description:
The square footage of the home used regularly for the business (Form 8829 Part I line 1; Pub 587 qualified business use — ATTESTED, not modeled), the NUMERATOR of the business-use percentage (line 3 = line 1 ÷ line 2). OPTIONAL — used only when the regular method is elected.
"EXCLUSIVELY" IS NOT ALWAYS REQUIRED, and the printed line says so directly: Form 8829's own line 1 caption is "Area used regularly AND EXCLUSIVELY for business, REGULARLY FOR DAYCARE, OR FOR STORAGE OF INVENTORY OR PRODUCT SAMPLES" — three populations, only the first of which needs exclusive use. IRC §280A(c)(2) waives "exclusively" for space used on a regular basis to store inventory or product samples of a trade or business that sells at retail or wholesale, PROVIDED the home is the SOLE fixed location of that trade or business — a storage area used for other, non-business purposes some of the time still belongs on this line at its full square footage. §280A(c)(4) waives "exclusively" for a daycare business (see ../writableHomeOfficeIsDaycareNotExclusive for how that population's business percentage is reduced instead, by the hours the space was actually used).
SCOPE-OUTS remaining (surfaced): the multi-part-of-home allocation for a daycare filer whose home mixes an exclusively-business area with a partly-business area (i8829's own "Special Computation for Certain Daycare Facilities," a three-step worksheet this dictionary does not build).

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 2 — total area of home (sq ft)
Fact.Description: The total area of the home (Form 8829 Part I line 2), the DENOMINATOR of the business-use percentage. OPTIONAL — used only when the regular method is elected. A valid regular-method election answers business area, total area, indirect expenses, direct expenses, and home depreciation (enter 0 where none). The engine guards the divide-by-zero (total area must be > 0 for the regular deduction to compute a non-zero business percentage).

Fact.Name: This area is used regularly, but not exclusively, in a daycare business that has applied for (and not been rejected), been granted (and still has in effect), or is exempt from a state license, certification, registration, or approval as a daycare center or family or group daycare home (Form 8829 Part I, "go to line 4")
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../writableHomeOfficeBusinessArea's space is used regularly, but not exclusively, in a daycare business qualifying under IRC §280A(c)(4) — the population Form 8829 Part I routes with "For daycare facilities not used exclusively for business, go to line 4. All others, go to line 7." A daycare business that DOES use its space exclusively answers false (or leaves this unanswered) and takes the ordinary line-3 percentage unreduced, same as any other filer. Optional; unanswered = false, the current behavior. The question states the licensing condition of IRC §280A(c)(4)(B): a daycare business that has not applied for, been granted, or been exempted from a state license, certification, registration, or approval does not qualify for the exception, so its non-exclusive space is not business area and is left off line 1 and the simplified-method square feet. When TRUE, both hours questions are required (see ../form8829DaycareHoursRatio). Feeds ../writableHomeOfficeDaycareHoursUsed, ../writableHomeOfficeDaycareHoursAvailable, and through them ../form8829BusinessPercentage.

Fact.Name: Total hours the facility was used for daycare during 2025 (Form 8829 line 4)
Fact.Description: The total number of hours ../writableHomeOfficeBusinessArea's space was actually used for the daycare business during 2025 — days used × hours per day, already summed by the filer. Example from the instructions: used Monday-Friday 12 hours/day for 250 days, plus 50 Saturdays at 8 hours/day, enters 3,400 (3,000 weekday hours + 400 Saturday hours). Asked when ../writableHomeOfficeIsDaycareNotExclusive is true. Unanswered leaves ../form8829DaycareHoursRatio at its complete-safe default (no reduction) rather than guessing a usage pattern. Feeds ../form8829DaycareHoursRatio, and through it ../form8829BusinessPercentage.

Fact.Name: Total hours the space was available for daycare during 2025 (Form 8829 line 5)
Fact.Description: The total number of hours ../writableHomeOfficeBusinessArea's space was AVAILABLE for daycare use during 2025 — the denominator of the hours ratio. Enter 8,760 (the hours in a full calendar year) unless the daycare business started or stopped during 2025, in which case the instructions require prorating: "multiply 24 hours by the number of days available and enter the result." Asked when ../writableHomeOfficeIsDaycareNotExclusive is true, right after ../writableHomeOfficeDaycareHoursUsed. Unanswered leaves ../form8829DaycareHoursRatio at its complete-safe default (no reduction). Feeds ../form8829DaycareHoursRatio.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 6 — daycare hours-used ratio (decimal)
Fact.Description: ../writableHomeOfficeDaycareHoursUsed ÷ ../writableHomeOfficeDaycareHoursAvailable — "Divide line 4 by line 5. Enter the result as a decimal amount." 1/1 (no reduction) whenever ../writableHomeOfficeIsDaycareNotExclusive is false or unanswered, so every non-daycare return is arithmetically untouched by this fact. When that flag is TRUE both hours are REQUIRED: an unanswered hours entry, or hours available of 0, leaves this ratio Incomplete, and with it line 7, line 30 and the simplified-method rate, because the statute reduces the expenses by the hours ratio and an unreduced 1/1 would overstate them. CEILINGED AT 1/1: the printed line has no cap, but hours used cannot exceed hours available on a correctly-completed return, and this fact refuses to let a data-entry error (used > available) INCREASE the business percentage above the exclusive-use reading.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 7 — business percentage (canonical, replaces the inline area ÷ total-area reading)
Fact.Description:
../writableHomeOfficeBusinessArea ÷ ../writableHomeOfficeTotalArea (line 3), times ../form8829DaycareHoursRatio (line 6) — "Business percentage. For daycare facilities not used exclusively for business, multiply line 6 by line 3. All others, enter the amount from line 3." THE CANONICAL LINE 7, reused by every Part II/III computation that used to inline line 3 on its own: ../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesDeduction, ../form8829OperatingExpensesWithCarryover, ../form8829BusinessBasisOfBuilding, and ../homeAdditions/*/businessBasis all read THIS fact now rather than re-deriving line 3 themselves — the one-quantity-one-fact fix each of those facts' own Description named as a gap it shared with its siblings, closed here in one place rather than four.
BYTE IDENTICAL FOR EVERY NON-DAYCARE RETURN: ../form8829DaycareHoursRatio is 1/1 unless ../writableHomeOfficeIsDaycareNotExclusive is answered true with both hours writables answered, so this fact reduces to the SAME line-1-over-line-2 division every one of the four call sites computed inline before this unit, and every one of their own committed node tests stays byte-identical (no fixture answers the new daycare writables). Divide-by-zero guard: total area 0 resolves this to 0, the same guard every call site already carried individually.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 — operating expenses, indirect (before business-use %)
Fact.Description:
The TOTAL Form 8829 Part II OPERATING expenses for the whole home that are allocated to the business by the business-use percentage — insurance, rent, repairs and maintenance, utilities, and other indirect expenses (Form 8829 Part II column (b): lines 16-22 only). "Generally, enter 100% of your indirect expenses ... in column (b)"; line 24 multiplies column (b) by the business percentage (line 7). This single Dollar input collapses the column-(b) operating-expense total; the engine applies the business-use percentage once.
MORTGAGE INTEREST AND REAL ESTATE TAXES (lines 10-11) ARE NOT HERE: they moved to ../writableForm8829IndirectMortgageInterestAndTaxes when the layered deduction-limit order landed (see ../homeOfficeRegularDeduction), because §280A(c)(5)(B)(i) excepts them from the limitation entirely rather than capping them alongside operating expenses. ../writableForm8829OperatingExpenseCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear carries the line-25 prior-year carryover this total combines with. SCOPE-OUTS (surfaced, never silent): casualty losses (line 9) and the excess-mortgage / excess-real-estate-tax Line 16/17 worksheets are not separately modeled.
PART-YEAR USE: "If you did not operate a business for the entire year, you can deduct only the expenses paid or incurred for the portion of the year you used your home for business" (i8829 Columns (a) and (b)). Enter only the expenses of the months the home was used for business, not the whole-year total; the graph does not prorate this entry.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 — operating expenses, direct (before the daycare hours ratio)
Fact.Description:
The TOTAL Form 8829 Part II OPERATING expenses that benefit ONLY the business part of the home (column (a), lines 16-22 only). "Enter 100% of your direct expenses on the appropriate line in column (a)" (i8829 Line 7). They take no area percentage. On a daycare facility not used exclusively for business they are reduced by the hours ratio (../form8829DaycareHoursRatio, line 6): IRC 280A(c)(4)(C) limits the expenses attributable to that portion to the hours-used share, and Pub. 587 Example 1 enters "$171 (34.25% × $500) on line 20, column (a)". The ratio is 1 on every other return, so there the entry is deducted in full. OPTIONAL — enter 0 when none.
MORTGAGE INTEREST AND REAL ESTATE TAXES (lines 10-11) ARE NOT HERE: they moved to ../writableForm8829DirectMortgageInterestAndTaxes for the same reason named on ../writableForm8829IndirectExpenses.
PART-YEAR USE: "If you did not operate a business for the entire year, you can deduct only the expenses paid or incurred for the portion of the year you used your home for business" (i8829 Columns (a) and (b)). Enter only the expenses of the months the home was used for business, not the whole-year total; the graph does not prorate this entry.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 — deductible mortgage interest and real estate taxes, indirect (before business-use %)
Fact.Description:
The TOTAL Form 8829 Part II lines 10 + 11, column (b): the mortgage interest and real estate taxes paid for the whole home, before the business-use percentage. "Generally, enter 100% of your indirect expenses ... in column (b)"; line 13 multiplies column (b) by the business percentage (line 7). WHERE THE BUSINESS PART GOES depends on the deduction the filer takes. An itemizer puts it on lines 10 and 11, which §280A(c)(5)(B)(i) excepts from the gross-income limitation (../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesDeduction, added to line 30 in full), with any interest the home mortgage interest limits leave out on line 16 and any real estate taxes the state and local tax deduction limit leaves out on line 17; the personal part goes to Schedule A lines 8a and 5b (../form8829PersonalHomeMortgageInterest, ../form8829PersonalHomeRealEstateTaxes), so an itemizer enters this home's amounts here and not again on Schedule A, and says how much of it is real estate taxes (../writableForm8829IndirectRealEstateTaxes). An itemizer enters only the interest on loans used to buy, build, or substantially improve this home. Some itemizer returns are refused (form8829:/knockoutForm8829ItemizerMortgageInterestAndTaxesNotSplit names them). A filer who claims the standard deduction puts it on lines 16 and 17 instead, with the operating expenses, under the limitation (../form8829StandardDeductionMortgageInterestAndTaxes); for that filer enter only the interest on loans used to buy, build, or substantially improve this home (not a home equity loan used for other things), and all the real estate taxes on it. Optional — enter 0 when none. Combined into one Dollar input the same way ../writableForm8829IndirectExpenses collapses its own column, since neither printed line distinguishes an excess-interest/excess-tax worksheet result this dictionary vendors.
PART-YEAR USE: "If you did not operate a business for the entire year, you can deduct only the expenses paid or incurred for the portion of the year you used your home for business" (i8829 Columns (a) and (b)). Enter only the expenses of the months the home was used for business, not the whole-year total; the graph does not prorate this entry.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 — deductible mortgage interest and real estate taxes, direct (before the daycare hours ratio)
Fact.Description:
The TOTAL Form 8829 Part II lines 10 + 11, column (a): deductible mortgage interest and real estate taxes that benefit ONLY the business part of the home. They take no area percentage; on a daycare facility not used exclusively for business they are reduced by the hours ratio (../form8829DaycareHoursRatio), as IRC 280A(c)(4)(C) reduces every expense attributable to that portion. Routed like ../writableForm8829IndirectMortgageInterestAndTaxes (lines 10 and 11 for an itemizer, lines 16 and 17 for a filer who claims the standard deduction); see that fact's Description. Optional — enter 0 when none.
PART-YEAR USE: "If you did not operate a business for the entire year, you can deduct only the expenses paid or incurred for the portion of the year you used your home for business" (i8829 Columns (a) and (b)). Enter only the expenses of the months the home was used for business, not the whole-year total; the graph does not prorate this entry.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 — of the home's indirect mortgage interest and real estate taxes, the real estate taxes
Fact.Description: The part of ../writableForm8829IndirectMortgageInterestAndTaxes that is state and local real estate taxes on the home (Line 11 Worksheet line 2); the rest of that amount is the home's mortgage interest. Asked of a filer who itemizes, because the two go to different lines: the business part of the mortgage interest to Form 8829 line 10 (and line 16 for any interest the home mortgage interest limits leave out), the business part of the real estate taxes to line 11 (and line 17 for any taxes the state and local tax deduction limit leaves out), and the personal parts to Schedule A lines 8a and 5b. For a filer who itemizes and enters an indirect amount, the Form 8829 lines stay unresolved until this is answered, and an answer larger than the indirect amount leaves them unresolved too. Optional for a filer who claims the standard deduction, whose amounts go on lines 16 and 17 together. Enter 0 when none of the amount is real estate taxes.

Fact.Name: Business part of the home's mortgage interest and real estate taxes (Form 8829 lines 10-14, or lines 16-17)
Fact.Description: ../writableForm8829DirectMortgageInterestAndTaxes times ../form8829DaycareHoursRatio (1 unless the space is a daycare facility not used exclusively for business; IRC 280A(c)(4)(C)) plus ../writableForm8829IndirectMortgageInterestAndTaxes times ../form8829BusinessPercentage (line 7). Each intake is read as $0 when unanswered, so a regular-method return that never reaches these questions computes without them. Divide-by-zero guard: total area 0 gives $0. WHERE IT GOES depends on the deduction the filer takes: an itemizer claims it on lines 10 and 11, the tier ../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesDeduction deducts outside the income limit; a filer who claims the standard deduction claims it on lines 16 and 17 instead (../form8829StandardDeductionMortgageInterestAndTaxes), with the operating expenses, under the income limit.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 14 — deductible mortgage interest and real estate taxes (itemizers; outside the income limit)
Fact.Description: Form 8829 line 14 for a filer who itemizes (scheduleA:/claimsItemizedDeductions true): ../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesBusinessPart less the business part that goes on lines 16 and 17 (../form8829ItemizerExcessMortgageInterestAndTaxes: the interest the home mortgage interest limits leave out, and the real estate taxes beyond the state and local tax deduction limit), so line 14 is the line 10 interest plus the line 11 taxes plus any direct amount. It is added to ../homeOfficeRegularDeduction in full, uncapped by the gross income limitation (IRC 280A(c)(5)(B)(i): these amounts are allowable whether or not the home is used for business), and it reduces the limit left for the other two tiers (line 15 = line 8 minus line 14; ../form8829RemainingLimitAfterMortgageInterestAndTaxes). For a filer who claims the standard deduction it is $0: "If you claim the standard deduction, you will not include any mortgage interest or real estate taxes on lines 10 and 11; instead, you will claim the entire business use of the home portion of those expenses using lines 16 and 17" (../form8829StandardDeductionMortgageInterestAndTaxes). The returns the split does not figure yet are refused by form8829:/knockoutForm8829ItemizerMortgageInterestAndTaxesNotSplit.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 lines 16 and 17 — mortgage interest and real estate taxes of a filer who claims the standard deduction
Fact.Description: For a filer who claims the standard deduction (scheduleA:/claimsItemizedDeductions false), the business part of the home's mortgage interest and real estate taxes (../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesBusinessPart), entered on lines 16 and 17 instead of lines 10 and 11. Lines 16 and 17 are operating expenses, so this amount joins line 26 (../form8829OperatingExpensesWithCarryover) and is allowed only up to the income limit left after line 14 (line 27). $0 for an itemizer, whose amount is on line 14. Line 16 takes only interest on loans used to buy, build, or substantially improve the home; the intake's question says so.

Fact.Name: This business figures a regular-method Form 8829 on a return that itemizes
Fact.Description: True when the filer itemizes (scheduleA:/claimsItemizedDeductions), this business elects the regular method with every required Form 8829 input answered (../regularHomeOfficeInputsComplete), and the home's total area is more than zero. Only then do the home's mortgage interest and real estate taxes go on Form 8829 lines 10 and 11 with the personal part on Schedule A. Complete on every return: every operand is an IsComplete test or a complete-safe fact.

Fact.Name: The home's indirect mortgage interest and real estate taxes, $0 when unanswered
Fact.Description: ../writableForm8829IndirectMortgageInterestAndTaxes when answered (never below $0), else $0: the same reading ../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesBusinessPart gives the intake.

Fact.Name: Line 11 Worksheet line 2 — the real estate taxes paid on the home
Fact.Description: The real estate taxes within the home's indirect mortgage interest and real estate taxes (../writableForm8829IndirectRealEstateTaxes). $0 when there is no indirect amount. Unresolved when there is an indirect amount and the real estate tax part is unanswered, or is more than the indirect amount: the return cannot tell the interest from the taxes, and the two go to different lines of Form 8829 and Schedule A.

Fact.Name: The home mortgage interest within the home's indirect mortgage interest and real estate taxes
Fact.Description: ../form8829IndirectMortgageInterestAndTaxesOrZero less ../form8829HomeRealEstateTaxes: the interest on the loans used to buy, build, or substantially improve the home. Unresolved when the real estate tax part is.

Fact.Name: Line 11 Worksheet line 6 — the business part of the home's real estate taxes
Fact.Description: For a regular-method business on a return that itemizes (../form8829ItemizerRegularMethod): the home's real estate taxes (../form8829HomeRealEstateTaxes) times the business percentage on Form 8829 line 7 (../form8829BusinessPercentage). This whole amount is left out of Schedule A line 5b; the part within the state and local tax deduction limit goes on Form 8829 line 11 and the rest on line 17. $0 otherwise.

Fact.Name: The business part of the home mortgage interest (Form 8829 lines 10 and 16)
Fact.Description: For a regular-method business on a return that itemizes: the home's indirect mortgage interest and real estate taxes times the business percentage (line 7), less the business part of the real estate taxes (../form8829Line11WorksheetRealEstateTaxesBusinessPart), so the two business parts add to exactly the business part of the indirect amount. The part the home mortgage interest limits allow goes on line 10 (../form8829Line10DeductibleMortgageInterestBusinessPart) and the rest on line 16. $0 otherwise.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 10 — the business part of the deductible home mortgage interest
Fact.Description: Step 1 treats all the home mortgage interest as a personal expense and figures what Schedule A would allow; Step 2 puts the part of it for this home on line 10, and line 13 takes the business percentage of it. Schedule A applies the home mortgage interest limits in proportion, by the debt-limit fraction (scheduleA:/scheduleAMortgageDebtLimitFractionPerThousand), so the business part on line 10 is ../form8829HomeMortgageInterestBusinessPart times that fraction, and the rest goes on line 16 (Excess mortgage interest). $0 when there is no business part; unresolved when the fraction is.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 16 of a return that itemizes — the business part of the excess mortgage interest
Fact.Description: The business part of the home mortgage interest (../form8829HomeMortgageInterestBusinessPart) less the part of it on line 10 (../form8829Line10DeductibleMortgageInterestBusinessPart): the interest the home mortgage interest limits keep off Schedule A, on the loans used to buy, build, or substantially improve the home. An operating expense, allowed only up to the income limit left after line 14. $0 when the limits do not reduce the interest.

Fact.Name: Line 11 Worksheet line 7a — the state and local taxes other than the business part of the home's real estate taxes
Fact.Description: Line 5 (the personal state and local income or sales taxes, all the real estate taxes on the home, the other real estate taxes and the personal property taxes) less line 6 (the business part of the home's real estate taxes). That is the state and local tax total on Schedule A line 5d (scheduleA:/scheduleALine5dStateAndLocalTaxes), which carries the home's real estate taxes less their business part.

Fact.Name: Line 11 Worksheet lines 7c and 7d — the state and local tax deduction limit before any reduction ($40,000; $20,000 if married filing separately)
Fact.Description: The Schedule A state and local tax deduction limit before the modified adjusted gross income reduction: scheduleA:/saltCapBase, halved for a married person filing separately. Unresolved while the filing status is.

Fact.Name: Line 11 Worksheet line 7b — the state and local tax deduction limit's floor ($10,000; $5,000 if married filing separately)
Fact.Description: The amount the Schedule A state and local tax deduction limit is never reduced below: scheduleA:/saltCapFloor, halved for a married person filing separately. Unresolved while the filing status is.

Fact.Name: The business part of the home's real estate taxes that counts on line 11 for the gross income limitation
Fact.Description: The real estate taxes that sit inside line 14 when this business's deduction is figured. When the other state and local taxes (Line 11 Worksheet line 7a, /form8829Line11WorksheetOtherStateAndLocalTaxes) reach the limit before any reduction (line 7c: $40,000, $20,000 if married filing separately), none of the business part is within the limit: all of it goes on line 17. Otherwise all of it (line 6) counts here. This is exact whenever the line 11 and line 17 split cannot change the deduction: line 7b (line 5 at most $10,000, $5,000 if married filing separately) puts all of line 6 on line 11, and when line 14 is no more than line 8, moving an amount from line 11 to line 17 leaves lines 28, 34 and 36 unchanged. The printed lines 14, 15, 26 and 27 carry the split the state and local tax deduction limit gives (form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line11WorksheetRealEstateTaxesOnLine11). A return where the split would change the deduction and turns on the limit (the worksheet's iteration) is refused by form8829:/knockoutForm8829ItemizerMortgageInterestAndTaxesNotSplit. $0 when there is no business part.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 lines 16 and 17 of a return that itemizes — excess mortgage interest and excess real estate taxes
Fact.Description: For a regular-method business on a return that itemizes: the business part of the home mortgage interest that the home mortgage interest limits leave off line 10 (line 16), plus the business part of the real estate taxes that is not on line 11 (line 17, ../form8829Line11RealEstateTaxesForTheIncomeLimit). These are operating expenses: they join line 26 (../form8829OperatingExpensesWithCarryover) and are allowed only up to the income limit left after line 14. $0 otherwise.

Fact.Name: The personal part of the home's real estate taxes, for Schedule A line 5b
Fact.Description: On a return that itemizes: the home's real estate taxes (../form8829HomeRealEstateTaxes) less their business part (../form8829Line11WorksheetRealEstateTaxesBusinessPart, $0 unless the regular method is figured). Pub. 587: the personal portion is the real estate taxes paid for the home reduced by the business portion deducted or carried over. Schedule A adds it to line 5b (scheduleA:/realEstateTaxesIncludedInStateLocalTaxes). $0 on a return that does not itemize.

Fact.Name: The personal part of the home mortgage interest, for Schedule A line 8a
Fact.Description: On a return that itemizes: the home mortgage interest (../form8829HomeMortgageInterest) less its business part (../form8829HomeMortgageInterestBusinessPart, $0 unless the regular method is figured). Schedule A adds it to line 8a (scheduleA:/scheduleALine8aHomeMortgageInterestOn1098) and applies the home mortgage interest limits to it with the rest of the interest there, which gives the personal portion of the deductible interest: "only include the personal part of your deductible mortgage interest on Schedule A". $0 on a return that does not itemize.

Fact.Name: The personal part of the Form 8829 homes' real estate taxes, all businesses
Fact.Description: The sum over the Schedule C businesses of /scheduleCs/*/form8829PersonalHomeRealEstateTaxes; $0 when the business list is unanswered.

Fact.Name: The personal part of the Form 8829 homes' mortgage interest, all businesses
Fact.Description: The sum over the Schedule C businesses of /scheduleCs/*/form8829PersonalHomeMortgageInterest; $0 when the business list is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 15 — gross-income limit remaining after mortgage interest and taxes
Fact.Description: Line 8 (../homeOfficeGrossIncomeLimitation, the gross income limitation) minus ../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesDeduction, floored at $0 — "Subtract line 14 from line 8. If zero or less, enter -0-." This is the budget the operating-expense tier (../form8829AllowableOperatingExpenses) and, after that, the depreciation tier (../form8829AllowableExcessCasualtyAndDepreciation) compete for.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 25 — carryover of prior-year operating expenses
Fact.Description:
The amount from the filer's PRIOR-YEAR Form 8829, line 43 (or, if no 2024 Form 8829 was filed, the operating expenses shown in Part IV of the last Form 8829 filed, or line 6a of a 2024 Simplified Method Worksheet if the method changed) — §280A(c)(5)'s flush language treats last year's disallowed operating-expense excess as "a deduction allocable to such use in the succeeding taxable year," and this is that carry-forward, entering this year's Part II. Optional — enter 0 when there is no carryover (the common case, and the prior default). Feeds ../form8829OperatingExpensesWithCarryover, widening the room ../form8829AllowableOperatingExpenses can allow this year.
NOT COMPUTED, because computing it would require modeling last year's Form 8829 in full — the same posture every other multi-year carryover this module documents as a deferral takes (e.g. ../homeOfficeRegularDeduction's own single-year gross-income-limit reading). This intake accepts whatever figure the filer's own records state.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 26 — operating expenses plus prior-year carryover
Fact.Description: ../writableForm8829DirectExpenses times ../form8829DaycareHoursRatio (line 6; 1 unless the space is a daycare facility not used exclusively for business, where Pub. 587 Example 1 enters "$171 (34.25% × $500) on line 20, column (a)"), plus ../writableForm8829IndirectExpenses times ../form8829BusinessPercentage (line 7, daycare-ratio-adjusted where it applies), plus ../writableForm8829OperatingExpenseCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear — "Add line 23, column (a), line 24, and line 25." For a filer who claims the standard deduction, lines 16 and 17 inside line 23 carry the business part of the home's mortgage interest and real estate taxes (../form8829StandardDeductionMortgageInterestAndTaxes). Divide-by-zero guard: total area 0 resolves the indirect term to 0 (unreachable under the gate, as ../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesDeduction states for its own identical guard). The carryover-in term is read IsComplete-else-$0, the same posture ../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesDeduction takes on its own two writables, so a return that never answers the carryover computes exactly as it did before this fact existed.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 27 — allowable operating expenses
Fact.Description: The smaller of ../form8829RemainingLimitAfterMortgageInterestAndTaxes (line 15) or ../form8829OperatingExpensesWithCarryover (line 26) — "Enter the smaller of line 15 or line 26." The middle tier of the layered order: capped by whatever budget remains after mortgage interest and taxes are deducted in full, and itself the first claim on that budget, ahead of depreciation (../form8829AllowableExcessCasualtyAndDepreciation).

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 28 — limit remaining for excess casualty losses and depreciation
Fact.Description: ../form8829RemainingLimitAfterMortgageInterestAndTaxes minus ../form8829AllowableOperatingExpenses, floored at $0 — "Limit on excess casualty losses and depreciation. Subtract line 27 from line 15." The budget the depreciation tier (../form8829AllowableExcessCasualtyAndDepreciation) competes for; already non-negative by construction (line 27 is a LesserOf against this fact's own minuend), the floor is kept for the same reason every sibling Subtract in this module keeps one.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 31 — carryover of prior-year excess casualty losses and depreciation
Fact.Description: The amount from the filer's PRIOR-YEAR Form 8829, line 44 (or, if no 2024 Form 8829 was filed, the excess casualty losses and depreciation shown in Part IV of the last Form 8829 filed, or line 6b of a 2024 Simplified Method Worksheet if the method changed) — the depreciation twin of ../writableForm8829OperatingExpenseCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear, and — per the same i8829 instruction pairing that names both lines together ("Line 25 and Line 31") — usually the LARGER carryover figure, since Pub. 587's own tie-break caps depreciation last and it is disallowed first. Optional — enter 0 when there is no carryover. Feeds ../form8829DepreciationWithCarryover, widening the room ../form8829AllowableExcessCasualtyAndDepreciation can allow this year.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 32 — excess casualty losses and depreciation plus prior-year carryover
Fact.Description: form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line29ExcessCasualtyLosses (line 29: derived from a linked Form 4684 home casualty, else the filer's entry, else $0) plus ../form8829HomeDepreciation (line 30) plus ../writableForm8829ExcessCasualtyAndDepreciationCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear (line 31) — "Add lines 29 through 31." ../form8829HomeDepreciation is already guaranteed complete wherever this fact is reached (../regularHomeOfficeInputsComplete requires it, directly or via Part III); the carryover-in term is read IsComplete-else-$0, the same posture every other new optional input in this tier takes.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 33 — allowable excess casualty losses and depreciation
Fact.Description: The smaller of ../form8829RemainingLimitAfterOperatingExpenses (line 28) or ../form8829DepreciationWithCarryover (line 32) — "Enter the smaller of line 28 or line 32." The LAST tier of the layered order, exactly matching Pub. 587's own tie-break ("with depreciation of your home taken last"): whatever budget mortgage interest/taxes and operating expenses leave behind is what depreciation (and its carryover-in) can claim.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 33 less line 35 — the casualty and depreciation tier Schedule C line 30 keeps
Fact.Description: The third tier of Schedule C line 30 (../homeOfficeRegularDeduction): line 33 (../form8829AllowableExcessCasualtyAndDepreciation, lines 29 through 31 capped at line 28) less line 35 (form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line35CasualtyPortion, the casualty loss portion carried to Form 4684 line 27 instead), on every Schedule C. Printed line 36 subtracts line 35 from line 34 before the amount reaches Schedule C line 30, so Schedule C line 30 is printed line 36 in whole dollars. On a Schedule C that a Form 4684 home casualty names, line 29 and line 35 come from the linked event; on any other they are the filer's entries, $0 when blank. An attested home casualty whose Schedule C is not yet named leaves form8829:/scheduleCs/*/hasLinkedHomeCasualty Incomplete, and this fact runs off its Switch and stays Incomplete rather than taking a figure computed without the link.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 42 — depreciation allowable (business portion of home)
Fact.Description:
The depreciation allowable on the business portion of the home for 2025 (Form 8829 Part III line 42 = line 40 business basis × line 41 depreciation percentage), entered as an already-computed business-portion Dollar amount and carried to Part II line 30. OPTIONAL — enter 0 when none (e.g. a renter, or a home-office in rented space).
NO LONGER THE ONLY ROUTE, and the old SCOPE-OUT text this Description carried is retired. Part III lines 37-42 now COMPUTE — see the section header below — and this writable is the FALLBACK: the route for a return outside the modeled placed-in-service domain, and for every return that has not answered Part III. When both are supplied the computed figure wins. Read ../form8829HomeDepreciation, never this fact, if you want the effective line 42; the two remaining consumers of this path are that Switch's fall-through arm and ../regularHomeOfficeInputsComplete's either-route leg.
Depreciation is limited last, as on Form 8829 lines 28 and 33 (after the operating expenses): see the third tier of ../homeOfficeRegularDeduction.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 37 — the smaller of the home's adjusted basis or its fair market value
Fact.Description:
The line-37 entry: the cost or other basis of the home INCLUDING LAND, or, if less, the fair market value of the home on the date it was first used for business. Both figures are taken as of the date business use began and are NOT adjusted for depreciation claimed or for changes in fair market value after that year (i8829 Lines 37 Through 40).
WHAT GOES IN, AND WHAT STAYS OUT. The basis includes permanent improvements made BEFORE the day business use began. It does NOT include additions and improvements placed in service on or after that day (../writableHomeFirstUsedForBusinessDate): i8829 says "Do not include any amounts on lines 37 through 40 for these expenditures"; they are listed one by one in ../homeAdditions, which depreciates them on the line 42 add-on. An improvement entered both here and there is depreciated twice.
INCLUDING LAND IS LOAD-BEARING AND DIFFERS FROM PUB 587'S PROSE. The form takes the smaller of two INCLUSIVE-of-land figures and then subtracts land on line 38; Pub. 587's narrative instead takes the smaller of two EXCLUSIVE-of-land figures. The two orders can disagree when the land share of basis and of fair market value differ. THE FORM CONTROLS here, because these are the form's own lines — the divergence is named rather than silently smoothed, and the Pub 587 worked example is pinned by entering its published exclusive-of-land figure on line 37 with a 0 line 38, where the two orders coincide.
OPTIONAL. Unanswered means the Part III computation is not in play and the attested ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation is used instead — see ../form8829Part3IsModeled. Include in the basis any addition or improvement placed in service on or before the first day you used the home for business (ruling IN-12: the same day counts as basis); leave out one placed in service after that day, which is listed separately (../homeAdditions) for line 42 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, page 5 "that were placed in service after you began to use your home for"; row FED-1040SC-F8829-LINE42-ADDITIONS-040).

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 38 — value of land included on line 37
Fact.Description:
The cost or other basis of the land the home sits on, or, if less, the fair market value of that land on the date the home was first used for business — subtracted from line 37 because land is not depreciable ("You cannot depreciate the cost or value of the land. You recover its cost when you sell or otherwise dispose of the property").
OPTIONAL — enter 0 when line 37 was already entered exclusive of land, which is how the Pub 587 worked example's published figures map onto this form. Unanswered leaves Part III unmodeled (../form8829Part3IsModeled), it does NOT default to 0: a silent 0 would treat every land-inclusive line 37 as fully depreciable and OVERSTATE the deduction, which is the one direction a defaulting rule must never take.

Fact.Name: Date (month, day and year) this home was first used for business
Fact.Description:
The DATE business use of this home began, asked to the day, not the month. Pub. 587 lists "The month and year you started using your home for business" as an input to the depreciation deduction, and the i8829 Line 41 tables key on it; the day is needed as well, for three readers. ../homeAdditions/*/rowIsModeled compares an improvement's placed-in-service date with this date by day (an improvement finished before this day belongs in the line 37 basis, one finished on or after it on the line 42 add-on), and line 37's fair market value is taken on this date. The simplified method's part-year average (../simplifiedMethodQualifiedUseStartDate) counts a 2025 start month only when at least 15 days of it follow this date. The Line 41 tables' boundaries are dates too (May 12/13 1993, the 1994 and 2025 year boundaries). A month picker that stores the 1st would move an improvement finished earlier that month onto line 42 and count a start month the 15-day rule excludes. ASKED WHEN: the home office is claimed by either method (the regular method, for Part III; the simplified method, when business use of the home began in 2025 or the business began in 2025).
A DATE INSIDE 2025 selects the twelve-row month table; a date from 1994-01-01 through 2024-12-31 selects the single printed 2.564% row. A date before 1994 is ACCEPTED here on purpose — the Limit does not fence the modeled domain, ../form8829Part3IsModeled does, so a filer with a 1985 home can still record the truth and ride the attested route.
UPPER LIMIT 2025-12-31: a home first used for business after the tax year cannot generate a 2025 deduction at all, so a later date is a data error rather than an unmodeled case.

Fact.Name: Binding contract to buy or build this home, or construction started, before May 13, 1993
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION, per business: whether the purchase or construction of this home was under a binding contract in effect before May 13, 1993, or construction of it had already begun by that date. Only ever asked of a home first used for business between 1993-05-13 and 1993-12-31; see ../form8829DepreciationPercentage and ../form8829Part3IsModeled, the only two facts that read it.
WHY IT IS AN INTAKE AND NOTHING ELSE ON THE RETURN CARRIES IT. It is a historical fact about a contract that was already in effect thirty-two years before this return, in the same class as ../writableHomeFirstUsedForBusinessDate, and no line of Form 8829, of Schedule C or of any information return reveals it. That is why the i8829 Line 41 table can only route this row to "the percentage given in Pub. 946" instead of printing a percentage of its own: the IRS cannot print one either without knowing this answer.
WHAT IT DECIDES, AND IT IS THE WHOLE RECOVERY PERIOD. IRC 168(c) said 31.5 years for nonresidential real property until Pub. L. 103-66 section 13151(a) substituted 39 years, and section 13151(b) made that substitution apply to property placed in service on or after May 13, 1993 EXCEPT property placed in service before January 1, 1994 under a pre-May-13-1993 binding written contract or whose construction had begun by then. So TRUE keeps this home on 31.5-year property (Pub. 946 Table A-7) and FALSE moves it to 39-year property (Table A-7a, the 2.564% row this dictionary already computes for every other pre-2025 placement).
BOTH HALVES OF THE STATUTORY CONDITION ARE ENCODED, and the placed-in-service half is not decorative: an attested TRUE on a home first used for business in 1995 changes nothing, because section 13151(b)(2) needs the placement to be before 1994 as well. The date fence lives on the two consumers rather than here, so this writable stays a plain Boolean a filer can answer without knowing which window it lands in.
UNANSWERED IS NEITHER TRUE NOR FALSE, and that is the point rather than an omission. Both consumers reach this fact through IsComplete, so an unanswered attestation leaves the 1993-05-13..1993-12-31 window OUTSIDE ../form8829Part3IsModeled exactly as it was before this intake existed, and the return rides the attested ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation. Guessing FALSE would be the dangerous direction: it would hand a home whose 31.5-year recovery period is already SPENT the full 2.564% and overstate the deduction. Guessing TRUE would understate it for the far larger population that had no such contract. The window is excluded rather than defaulted for exactly that reason.

Fact.Name: Business use of this home stopped before the end of 2025
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the filer stopped using the home for business before the end of the year. That is a PRINTED ROW of the i8829 Line 41 table and it does not carry a percentage: it routes to "the percentage given in Pub. 946 as adjusted by the instructions under Sale or Other Disposition Before the Recovery Period Ends in that publication".
THIS IS NO LONGER A PURE EXCLUSION. An earlier draft of this Description said "Pub. 946 is not vendored, so this dictionary detects the population and hands it back to the attested line-42 route". Pub. 946 IS vendored, and that section of it now DRIVES a computation: with ../writableHomeOfficeUseStoppedDate answered and the home first used for business before the filing year, the full-year figure is adjusted by ../form8829PartYearFraction and the return stays on the computed route. What still falls back is the COMPOUND case — first used for business and given up in the same year — because no cited document composes the two mid-month conventions.
UNANSWERED IS NOT FALSE. ../form8829Part3IsModeled requires this answered, because the cost of guessing "no" is a silently overstated deduction for exactly the population the printed table singles out. A filer who leaves it unanswered keeps the attested route, which is where they already were.

Fact.Name: Date business use of this home stopped (drives the Pub. 946 disposition fraction)
Fact.Description:
The date in the filing year on which business use of this home ended. Required whenever ../writableHomeOfficeUseStoppedDuringYear is true and the Part III computation is wanted; unanswered simply leaves the business on the attested line-42 route.
WHAT IT IS FOR. Pub. 946's "Sale or Other Disposition Before the Recovery Period Ends" says a mid-month-convention property's deduction for the year of disposition is a full year of depreciation times a fraction whose numerator is the number of months (INCLUDING PARTIAL MONTHS) the property was in service and whose denominator is 12, with the month of disposition treated as one-half month. Only the MONTH of this date is consulted; the day is collected because a date is what a filer has and because a month enum could not express the filing-year bounds the Limits carry.
"DISPOSED OF" COVERS CESSATION OF BUSINESS USE, in the publication's own words: "You have disposed of your property if you have permanently withdrawn it from use in your business or income-producing activity because of its sale, exchange, retirement, abandonment, involuntary conversion, or destruction." The i8829 Line 41 row that sends this population here says "stopped using your home for business", which is that withdrawal.
BOUNDED TO THE FILING YEAR by its Limits, and bounded again inside ../form8829CessationIsModeled, which is the gate that actually fences the domain.

Fact.Name: Simplified method — first day of qualified business use of this home in 2025
Fact.Description: The day this home's qualified business use began within 2025, for the monthly-averaging rule of the simplified method. It is ../writableHomeFirstUsedForBusinessDate when that date falls in 2025, and January 1, 2025 when it is earlier. When that date is unanswered and the business began during 2025 (../writableStartedOrAcquiredBusinessThisYear true), it is ../writableBusinessBeganDate: home use for the business cannot begin before the business does, so that date is a floor, and it can still count months before the home was actually put to business use; the filer who knows the home first-use date answers it. When the business began during 2025 and neither date is answered, this stays Incomplete, because a business that began during the year has a part-year average the graph cannot guess. On every other return it is January 1, 2025, the full year.

Fact.Name: Simplified method — last day of qualified business use of this home in 2025
Fact.Description: The day this home's qualified business use ended within 2025, for the monthly-averaging rule of the simplified method: ../writableHomeOfficeUseStoppedDate when ../writableHomeOfficeUseStoppedDuringYear is true (Incomplete until that date is answered), otherwise December 31, 2025.

Fact.Name: Simplified Method Worksheet — months of 2025 with at least 15 days of qualified business use
Fact.Description: The number of months (0-12) that count toward the simplified method's average monthly allowable square footage. A month counts when qualified business use of this home covered at least 15 of its days: "if your qualified business use was less than 15 days in a month, you must use -0- for that month". Qualified use runs from ../simplifiedMethodQualifiedUseStartDate to ../simplifiedMethodQualifiedUseEndDate, so a month counts when the use starts no later than the 15th day before its end, ends no earlier than its 15th, and the whole period is at least 15 days long. That covers a start during the year (Pub. 587 Example 1: use from July 20 counts August through December, 5 months), a stop during the year (a February 15 stop counts January and February), and both. 12 on a full-year return, so ../homeOfficeDeductionSimplified's months over 12 term is 1 there. Incomplete when either date is. An area change during the year that is not a full start or stop is not averaged here; the square feet answered apply to every counted month.

Fact.Name: No additions or improvements placed in service after business use of this home began
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION OF ABSENCE, per business, on the ../writableNoUnmodeledAmtItems pattern. The filer states that no additions or improvements used at least partially for business were placed in service AFTER business use of the home began.
WHY IT GATES THE COMPUTATION. i8829 "Lines 37 Through 40" says such expenditures are NOT included on lines 37 through 40 and are instead depreciated separately and ADDED into line 42 with an attached statement. So for a filer who has them, line 42 is strictly more than line 40 × line 41, and computing only 40 × 41 would UNDERSTATE their deduction while looking authoritative. Rather than understate, this dictionary asks, and a business that cannot attest absence keeps its attested line-42 figure — which can and should carry the add-on.
UNANSWERED IS NOT TRUE and frees nobody: ../form8829Part3IsModeled requires this answered AND true, so an unanswered return keeps exactly the treatment it had before this section.
[ THE PARAGRAPHS ABOVE ARE KEPT VERBATIM and two of their clauses are now overtaken. (1) "requires this answered AND true" is now "requires this ANSWERED, and then either TRUE or ../homeAdditionsAreModeled": the add-on it calls "a NAMED gap rather than a computation this unit builds" IS built, at ../form8829AdditionsDepreciation, over the new ../homeAdditions collection. The unanswered posture is UNCHANGED - ../form8829Part3IsModeled still requires this attestation answered, so a return that never reached the question still keeps the attested figure. (2) "a business that cannot attest absence keeps its attested line-42 figure" is now true only of a business that cannot attest absence AND cannot list its expenditures; one that lists them all, in rows this dictionary can compute, gets a computed line 42 with the add-on in it.
WHAT A FALSE ANSWER NOW DOES, which is the application asked-when for the new group: it opens the "Additions and improvements to your home" screen (see ../homeAdditions, whose Description carries the full screen specification) and requires at least one row. A FALSE answer with no rows listed, or with a row this dictionary cannot compute, keeps the attested route exactly as a FALSE answer always did - so shipping this question WITHOUT the new screen is safe and changes nothing.]

Fact.Name: Additions and improvements placed in service after business use of this home began
Fact.Description:
COLLECTION ROOT, per business: one item per addition or improvement, used at least partially for business, that was placed in service AFTER business use of this home began. A collection nested inside a /scheduleCs item, on the /scheduleCs/*/otherExpenses and scheduleE:/formK1s/*/atRiskActivityShares pattern, because the expenditures belong to ONE home office and the printed add-on table assigns each of them its own percentage by its own placed-in-service month.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION for the collection itself (the application builds the screen from this Description; it should never need to open an IRS document). SCREEN: "Additions and improvements to your home", inside the home-office topic of this Schedule C, immediately after the "Did you make any additions or improvements?" question that ../writableNoHomeAdditionsOrImprovements already carries. ASKED WHEN: ../writableNoHomeAdditionsOrImprovements is answered NO (that is, the filer DOES have such expenditures). It is never asked of a filer who attested absence, and never asked while that attestation is unanswered. QUESTION: "Add each addition or improvement you made to this home after you started using it for business." An add-a-row affordance with a per-row sub-form carrying the three writables below; at least ONE row is required once the filer answered NO, because an empty table contradicts the answer that summoned it and would silently drop the filer's add-on (../homeAdditionsAreModeled requires a size greater than zero for exactly that reason). HELP: "The IRS treats work you did on your home AFTER you started using it for business separately from the home itself. Do not include it in the cost of the home you entered earlier; list it here instead, one row per item, and we will figure the depreciation on each one. A new roof, a new furnace, an added room and a rewired office are all examples. Work you did BEFORE you started using the home for business is part of the home's cost and belongs in the home cost question, not here." (i8829 "Lines 37 Through 40": https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, page 5; Pub. 587 "Depreciating permanent improvements": https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p587.pdf, page 9.) UNANSWERED POSTURE: a collection the filer never opened is COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE at ../homeAdditionsAreModeled through an IsComplete on this root, which is the idiom scheduleE:/formK1s/*/atRiskActivitySharesRecorded uses and the reason it uses it - a CollectionSize or a CollectionSum over an absent root resolves PLACEHOLDER rather than Complete. A filer who answered NO and then opened no rows therefore stays on the attested ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation, which is exactly where they were before this unit. VALIDATION: a repeating group, unbounded. The printed form has no rows for it at all - the instruction says to attach a statement - so nothing caps the count. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../homeAdditions/*/depreciationAllowed per row, then ../form8829AdditionsDepreciation, then the second term of ../form8829ComputedHomeDepreciation (Form 8829 line 42), then Schedule C line 30. FOR THE AMT PER-ASSET SURFACE: this is the collection-root shape the AMT per-asset surface inherits.

Fact.Name: What this addition or improvement was
Fact.Description:
Free text naming one addition or improvement, for the statement i8829 "Line 42" requires the filer to attach ("Attach a statement showing your computation and include the amount you figured in the total for line 42").
SCREEN SPECIFICATION. SCREEN: the per-row sub-form of "Additions and improvements to your home" (see ../.. for the group). ASKED WHEN: a row exists, i.e. always for every row the filer added; it is the first field of the row. QUESTION: "What did you add or improve?" HELP: "A short description is enough - 'new roof', 'furnace', 'added a room'. This goes on the statement that has to be attached to Form 8829 explaining how you figured line 42." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, page 6.) UNANSWERED POSTURE: BLANK ON THE RETURN, and it does NOT refuse. Nothing in the graph reads it, so a row with a date and a cost but no description still computes; the row's line on the attached statement simply carries no label. It is not part of ../rowIsModeled for that reason - refusing a whole business's computed line 42 over a missing label would be a data-completeness refusal with no tax consequence behind it. VALIDATION: String, free text, no Min or Max, optional. WHAT IT FEEDS: the attached statement only. No computed line moves when it is answered. FOR THE AMT PER-ASSET SURFACE: the AMT per-asset surface inherits this exact column, for the same reason - Form 6251's own adjustment detail is a statement, not a printed grid.

Fact.Name: Date this addition or improvement was placed in service
Fact.Description:
The date this expenditure was placed in service. It is the KEY of the i8829 "Line 42" add-on table, exactly as ../../../writableHomeFirstUsedForBusinessDate is the key of the Line 41 table for the home itself, and Pub. 587 says why the two tables are the same one: an improvement is depreciated "over the recovery period that would apply to your home if you began using it for business at the same time as the improvement".
MODELED AS A Day RATHER THAN A MONTH ENUM for the same reason the home's date is: the add-on table's boundaries are DATES (May 12/13 1993, the 1994 and 2025 year boundaries), and only the MONTH is consulted once the date is inside 2025 - by the add-on TABLE. ../rowIsModeled condition (2) consults the DAY; see the correction under HELP.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION. SCREEN: the per-row sub-form of "Additions and improvements to your home". ASKED WHEN: a row exists. REQUIRED. QUESTION: "When was it placed in service?" HELP: "Use the date the work was finished and ready for use - the actual day, not just the month, and not the day you paid for it or started it. It has to be ON OR AFTER the date you started using this home for business; work finished before that date is part of the home's cost, which you entered earlier." (i8829 "Line 42" table: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, page 6; Pub. 587 "Depreciating permanent improvements": https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p587.pdf, page 9.) [THE APPLICATION MUST NOT BUILD A MONTH PICKER HERE, because ../rowIsModeled condition (2) compares this date BY DAY against ../../../writableHomeFirstUsedForBusinessDate: a month picker stores day 1, so an improvement finished LATER IN THE SAME MONTH business use of the home began would resolve the comparison as "earlier", close ../../../homeAdditionsAreModeled for the WHOLE business, and drop the filer back to their attested Form 8829 line 42 with no signal. The screen must warn on a date that is earlier than the home's first-business-use date rather than accept it silently. The home's own date is described as a month and year and is stored as the 1st when captured as a month; because condition (2) is day-inclusive, an improvement finished on or after that 1st is admitted, so the month-captured home date does not refuse a same-month improvement. Only an improvement captured as a month (the 1st) against a home date that is a real later day of the same month still refuses, which is why this date must be collected to the day.] UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED, and the refusal is per BUSINESS, not per row. ../rowIsModeled is false for a row with no date, ../../../homeAdditionsAreModeled then fails its every-row test, and the whole business drops back to the attested ../../../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation. That is deliberate: a row the filer began and did not finish means the add-on total is short, and a short add-on UNDERSTATES line 42 while looking authoritative, which is the exact failure ../../../writableNoHomeAdditionsOrImprovements was minted to prevent. VALIDATION: Day, collected to the DAY and not to the month (see the correction under HELP). MAX 2025-12-31 - an expenditure placed in service after the tax year cannot generate a 2025 deduction at all, so a later date is a data error rather than an unmodeled case; that is the same Limit and the same argument as the home's own date.
