NO MIN, deliberately: a 1985 improvement is ACCEPTED here so the filer can record the truth, and ../rowIsModeled - not the Limit - is what fences the computable domain, on the model of ../../../writableHomeFirstUsedForBusinessDate. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../depreciationPercentage (which row of the add-on table this expenditure takes), ../rowIsModeled, and through them ../depreciationAllowed and Form 8829 line 42. FOR THE AMT PER-ASSET SURFACE: the AMT per-asset surface inherits this column, and inherits the Day-not-enum argument with it.

Fact.Name: Cost or other basis of this addition or improvement
Fact.Description:
The FULL cost or other basis of one expenditure, before any business percentage is applied. i8829 "Lines 37 Through 40" asks for exactly this figure on the attached statement ("the cost or other basis of additions and improvements, used at least partially for business"), and the "Line 42" table then multiplies "the business part of their cost or other basis" by the table percentage - so the business part is computed here (../businessBasis), not asked.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION. SCREEN: the per-row sub-form of "Additions and improvements to your home". ASKED WHEN: a row exists. REQUIRED. QUESTION: "What did it cost?" HELP: "Enter the whole cost of the work, not just the business share - we apply your business percentage for you. Use what you paid, including installation. Do not subtract anything for the part of the home you do not use for business." (i8829 "Lines 37 Through 40": https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, page 5; the add-on table's "the business part of their cost or other basis": lines 375-382.) UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED, per business, exactly as for ../writableDatePlacedInService and for the same reason - a half-filled row makes the add-on total short, and a short add-on understates line 42. VALIDATION: Dollar. MIN $0 - a negative cost is a data error; the printed instruction knows only a cost or other basis. No Max. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../businessBasis (cost times the home's line-7 business percentage), then ../depreciationAllowed, then Form 8829 line 42. FOR THE AMT PER-ASSET SURFACE: the AMT per-asset surface inherits this column, including the whole-cost-not-business-share convention.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 39 — basis of building (line 37 minus line 38)
Fact.Description:
Line 37 less the line-38 land value, floored at 0. The form prints no floor; the floor is this dictionary's guard, because land basis exceeding the whole-property basis is a data error and a NEGATIVE line 39 would flow through line 40 into a negative line 42, REDUCING the home-office deduction below what the other expense lines earn. Floored, the worst such an entry can do is drop depreciation to 0. Each operand is the PRINTED line (form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line37HomeBasisOrFmv and ...Line38LandValue, each the answer floored at $0), so a negative answer that prints 0 on line 37 or 38 never makes line 39 differ from printed line 37 less printed line 38.
Incomplete until both inputs are answered — this is a form line, not a gate, so it refuses rather than defaulting; ../form8829Part3IsModeled is the complete-safe consumer.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 40 — business basis of building (line 39 × line 7)
Fact.Description:
The depreciable basis of the business part of the home: line 39 multiplied by ../form8829BusinessPercentage (line 7 — business area ÷ total area, daycare-ratio-adjusted where it applies; this fact used to inline "this dictionary's exclusive-use reading is line 1 ÷ line 2" here, which mis-stated the daycare population's own line 7 — closed by reading the canonical fact instead). The same fact ../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesDeduction and ../form8829OperatingExpensesWithCarryover now read too — one quantity, one fact, closing the gap this Description used to name as shared with those siblings.
DIVIDE-BY-ZERO GUARD: total area 0 resolves this to 0 rather than throwing, matching the guard ../homeOfficeRegularDeduction carries.
NO WHOLE-DOLLAR Round NODE, which is the accurate statement. The Dollar type carries a fixed CENT scale and rounds HALF_EVEN at every Multiply, so arbitrary precision does NOT survive a chain of them; what this fact declines is the whole-dollar Round, which stays downstream on ../homeOfficeRegularDeduction where it always was. Cent scale is what invariant #1 asks for and it is what reproduces the published Pub 587 answer of $147.66 exactly.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 41 — depreciation percentage (the 39-year and 31.5-year nonresidential MACRS tables)
Fact.Description:
The line-41 percentage, keyed on ../writableHomeFirstUsedForBusinessDate and, for one window, on ../writableHomeBindingContractBeforeMay131993. It answers TWO MACRS regimes, not one, and reads THREE printed sources: the two tables the i8829 Line 41 instruction prints, and Pub. 946 Table A-7 behind them.
THE 39-YEAR REGIME (a home first used for business after May 12, 1993). Nonresidential real property is depreciated straight-line over 39 years, and the twelve 2025 values are the published FIRST-YEAR percentages with the mid-month convention already inside them — the i8829 month table, Pub. 587 Table 2 and Pub. 946 Table A-7a all print the same twelve, so those cells are witnessed in three independent IRS documents. 2.564% is the same table's years-2-through-39 row and is what every in-domain pre-2025 placement takes.
THE 31.5-YEAR REGIME ALSO REACHES ROW (a), the 1993-05-13..1993-12-31 window, whenever the filer attests a binding contract or a construction start before May 13, 1993 (through ../writableHomeBindingContractBeforeMay131993; the statutory basis is IRC 168(c) as amended by Pub. L. 103-66 section 13151(a) and the section 13151(b)(2) transition rule, quoted on that writable). Those homes are not a constant: at recovery year 33, which is where a 1993 placement stands in the 2025 filing year, Table A-7's row is BLANK for months 1 through 6 and carries 0.132%, 0.397%, 0.661%, 0.926%, 1.190% and 1.455% for months 7 through 12. Since the window's floor is May 13, only months 5 through 12 can arise, so BAND 1b below returns 0% for May and June and a live cell for July onward. An UNANSWERED attestation takes no arm at all and leaves this fact Incomplete on that window, which is byte-identically what it did before the intake existed.
THE 31.5-YEAR REGIME (row (c) of the i8829 second table: first used after 1986 and before May 13, 1993) RESOLVES 0%, AND THE DERIVATION LIVES HERE rather than only in the section header, because this is the fact that returns the value. Two printed witnesses fix the regime: Pub. 946's "Office in the home" paragraph names this exact fact pattern ("31.5 years if you began using it for business before May 13, 1993"), and GDS recovery-period footnote 4 states the class rule itself ("31.5 years for property placed in service before May 13, 1993"). The table is therefore Pub. 946 Table A-7. THE ARGUMENT, in three steps: (1) PRINTED — Table A-7 has no row beyond recovery year 33, and its year-33 row is BLANK for months 1 through 6 while carrying live cells (0.132% … 1.455%) for months 7 through 12. (2) INFERRED — every column of Table A-7 sums to exactly 100.000%, months 1-6 terminating at year 32 and months 7-12 at year 33, so a blank cell is an EXHAUSTED recovery period rather than a missing figure. This step is arithmetic over the printed cells, not something the publication states, and the trust tag below splits on exactly this line. (3) CLOSED OVER THE POPULATION — for a calendar-year filer the 2025 recovery year is 2025 − Y + 1, so this row's domain [1987-01-01, 1993-05-12] runs from recovery year 33 (a 1993 placement, months 1-5, landing on the blank part of row 33) to year 39 (a 1987 placement, past the table entirely). Every member is at or past its own column's last live cell, so 0% is right for the WHOLE domain rather than a sampled point. The direction is not adverse: the basis is fully recovered, so 0 is the correct deduction rather than a denied one.
THE CASES ARE EXHAUSTIVE OVER THE MODELED DOMAIN AND HAVE NO True FALL-THROUGH, on purpose. A date OUTSIDE [1987-01-01, 1993-05-12] ∪ [1994-01-01, 2025-12-31] resolves this INCOMPLETE rather than silently taking a plausible number, and so does a date inside [1993-05-13, 1993-12-31] whose binding-contract attestation is unanswered. TWO POPULATIONS DEPEND ON THAT REFUSAL and both are named. [What refuses here is (i) row (a) with the binding-contract attestation UNANSWERED, which is the population the exclusion always protected, and (ii) everything before 1987, which stays outside this fact because the section header's bullet (d) keeps ../form8829Pub534HomeDepreciation off the cessation year on a convention conflict rather than on a document.] ROW (d)'s AND ROW (a)'s FLOORS ARE EXPLICIT IN CASES 1 AND 2 BELOW and both must stay there. An earlier draft tested only "date ≤ 1993-05-12" in case 1 and only "date ≤ 2024-12-31" in case 2, so the entire Pub. 534 population took the 0% derived for the 31.5-year regime and row (a) took 2.564% — answering two unsupported cases with plausible numbers in the one place this Description promises not to. FIXING CASE 1 ALONE WAS NOT ENOUGH and the node test is what proved it: with case 1 correctly rejecting a 1986 date, case 2's bare upper bound caught it anyway. Nothing reaches the refusal in practice — ../form8829Part3IsModeled fences the same two windows and is the only guard under which ../form8829ComputedHomeDepreciation is read — so the Incompleteness is a backstop rather than a live refusal, but it is the backstop whoever builds the Pub. 534 contract will land on.
THE STRUCTURE IS THE PROOF, AND IT IS NOT AN ORDERING ARGUMENT — that is the correction this paragraph carries. The body is FOUR BANDS, each fenced at BOTH ends (the 31.5-year window, the binding-contract window, the 39-year window, and the filing year), with month cases nested inside the second and the fourth so each one's floor is hoisted once rather than repeated. An earlier draft was a flat list of fourteen upper-bound cases that relied on order alone, and it was wrong in a way review caught only half of: a pre-1987 date took 2.564% from the pre-2025 case, and when that case gained a floor the same date took 2.461% from the January case instead. Floors were being chased one case at a time. Banding makes every refusal correct by construction, so adding a case later cannot silently re-open either gap.
TAX-YEAR-PINNED, AND BAND 1b IS THE MOST SHARPLY PINNED THING IN THIS FACT. Every Day literal below is a TY2025 boundary; the twelve percentages are the FIRST-YEAR row of Table A-7a, correct only for a home first used for business in the filing year; and the 0% depends on the filing year being far enough past 1993 to exhaust Table A-7 (it is, and it stays so in later years, but a TY2026 module must re-derive it rather than inherit it). BAND 1b's six live cells are the year-33 row and NOTHING ELSE: they are right for TY2025 alone, because 2025 − 1993 + 1 = 33 and Table A-7 has no row 34. In TY2026 the whole window collapses to 0% — every column of Table A-7 has terminated by then — so a TY2026 module that inherits this band unchanged would pay six percentages that the table no longer carries. That is what the TaxYear marker is for.

Fact.Name: The cessation leg of the Part III domain gate (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when this business's cessation facts are ones Part III can compute: either business use did NOT stop during the year, or it stopped AND the cessation date is answered, inside the filing year, AND the home was first used for business BEFORE the filing year.
TWO COMPOUND EXCLUSIONS, and they are the only judgement calls here. [THE FIRST: Pub. 946 Table A-7a's first-year row already carries the placed-in-service mid-month convention; nothing in the publication or in the i8829 Line 41 instruction says how to stack the disposition fraction on top of it for a home first used for business and given up in the SAME year. Rather than compose two conventions the sources do not compose, that population keeps the attested figure.]
THE SECOND IS THE SAME OBJECT AT THE OTHER END OF THE TABLE. A home on the binding-contract TRUE arm reads Pub. 946 Table A-7's row 33, which is the table's LAST row and a PARTIAL one. Table A-7 is 31.5-year straight line, so each month is 100/378 of basis and each year-33 cell converts to a month count: July 0.132% = 0.5 months, August 0.397% = 1.5, September 0.661% = 2.5, October 0.926% = 3.5, November 1.190% = 4.5, December 1.455% = 5.5. Every one of those recovery periods therefore ENDS in the first half of 2025 - mid-January through mid-June - and May and June placements are blank at row 33 because theirs ended in 2024.
THAT BREAKS THE DISPOSITION RULE'S OWN PRECONDITION, in two different ways, and neither has a cited answer. Pub. 946's section is headed "Sale or Other Disposition Before the Recovery Period Ends". (i) If business use stops AFTER the recovery period has already ended - an August 1993 placement is fully recovered by mid-February 2025, so a September cessation is seven months late - the section does not apply at all, and scaling the final cell by a months-over-12 fraction would STRAND the remainder of the basis permanently, contradicting this module's own "every column of Table A-7 sums to exactly 100.000%" argument. (ii) If business use stops DURING the final partial year, the section does apply, but nothing says how its fraction composes with a row that is already partial. Rather than pick, the whole TRUE window is excluded and those returns keep the attested figure.
THE EXCLUSION'S SCOPE IS THE WHOLE TRUE WINDOW, DELIBERATELY, NOT ONLY MONTHS 7-12. Separating case (i) from case (ii) would mean deriving each month's remaining recovery from a printed percentage - the 0.397% = 1.5 months conversion above - and no cited document performs that conversion; it is this dictionary's arithmetic, which is exactly the class this gate refuses rather than guesses. May and June placements are swept in with them, and that flip is HARMLESS in direction: their percentage is 0%, so they move from a computed $0 to the filer's own attested figure rather than losing a deduction. THE FALSE ARM IS NOT EXCLUDED and must not be: a FALSE answer puts the home on Table A-7a's flat years-2-through-39 row, 2.564%, which is a FULL row with no partial-row problem, so 2.564% x the disposition fraction is exactly the composition Pub. 946 prints (quarantined case scheduleC/f8829-binding-1993-08-15-contract-false-with-midyear-cessation-still-computes (inner_models/packages/ty2025/federal/schedule-c-business/examples/trunk-quarantine/)).
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, the ../mayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems idiom: every outer When is an IsComplete question, so this never propagates Incomplete. An unanswered cessation flag resolves it FALSE, which is inert — ../form8829Part3IsModeled's own outer guard already requires that flag answered, so the FALSE only ever confirms a gate that was closed anyway.

Fact.Name: Pub. 946 disposition fraction — months in service over 12
Fact.Description:
The fraction Pub. 946 applies to a full year of depreciation in the year a mid-month-convention property is disposed of: the number of months (INCLUDING PARTIAL MONTHS) the property was in service, over 12, with the month of disposition counted as one-half month. So a cessation in month M gives (M − 0.5)/12, spelled here as the exact Rational (2M − 1)/24 — 1/24 for January through 23/24 for December.
TOTAL AND COMPLETE-SAFE: 1/1 whenever business use did not stop, or the cessation flag is unanswered, so ../form8829ComputedHomeDepreciation can multiply by it unconditionally and every non-cessation return is arithmetically untouched. The twelve-case inner Switch has NO True fall-through, on the same principle as ../form8829DepreciationPercentage: a cessation date outside the filing year refuses rather than silently taking a full year. Nothing reaches it out of domain — ../form8829CessationIsModeled fences exactly the same window and is a conjunct of ../form8829Part3IsModeled.

Fact.Name: The i8829 Line 42 add-on percentage for THIS expenditure, by its own placed-in-service month
Fact.Description:
The add-on table's percentage for one addition or improvement, keyed on ../writableDatePlacedInService.
IT IS THE SAME PRINTED TABLE AS LINE 41, ON A DIFFERENT KEY, AND THAT IS WHY THIS FACT EXISTS BESIDE ../../../form8829DepreciationPercentage RATHER THAN REUSING IT. The i8829 "Line 42" add-on table reprints the Line 41 table row for row - the twelve 2025 months, the 2.564% row, the binding-contract row, the cessation row, the 1987-to-May-1993 row and the pre-1987 row - but keys every row on when the EXPENDITURE was placed in service instead of when the HOME was. Pub. 587 states the same rule in prose: an improvement is depreciated "over the recovery period that would apply to your home if you began using it for business at the same time as the improvement". So this is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY from the home's line 41 (different input, different value on the same return), not a second derivation of the same one, and the one-quantity-one-fact rule is satisfied. What is duplicated is the printed TABLE, and it is duplicated only because a Fact Graph fact cannot be parameterised over its input path; there is no abstraction in this dictionary that would let one fact answer both keys.
THE DRIFT HAZARD IS REAL AND IS NAMED HERE the way BAND 1b names its twin: this fact and ../../../form8829DepreciationPercentage read the same IRS table, so a table correction must land in BOTH. The bands below are a STRICT SUBSET of that fact's, deliberately - see the next paragraph - so a reader comparing them should expect this one to be smaller, not different.
THREE BANDS, EACH FENCED AT BOTH ENDS, NO True FALL-THROUGH. The structure and the argument are ../../../form8829DepreciationPercentage's, and the reason for the structure is the one recorded there: a flat list of upper bounds is only correct if every earlier case also carries a floor, and floors were once being chased one case at a time. BAND A, [1987-01-01, 1993-05-12], resolves 0 percent. This is the 31.5-year regime (Pub. 946 Table A-7). In the 2025 filing year the members of this band stand at recovery years 33 through 39; Table A-7's last row is 33 and its year-33 cells are blank for months 1 through 6; every column of the table sums to exactly 100.000 percent, so a blank cell is a SPENT recovery period rather than a missing figure. That exhaustion step is this dictionary's arithmetic and not the publication's, and the trust tag below splits on exactly that line - it is the same inference, on the same table, as BAND 1 of the home's own percentage. BAND B, [1994-01-01, 2024-12-31], resolves 2.564 percent: the add-on table's one printed row for an earlier placement, which is also Pub. 946 Table A-7a's years-2-through-39 row. BAND C, [2025-01-01, 2025-12-31], is the twelve-row month table the add-on table routes to ("the percentage in the line 41 instructions for the month placed in service"). The twelve values are the FIRST-YEAR row of Table A-7a with the mid-month convention already inside them, and the i8829 month table, Pub. 587 Table 2 and Pub. 946 Table A-7a all print the same twelve.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT, and each is a REFUSAL rather than a guess. (i) BEFORE 1987: the add-on table sends it to Pub. 534, and although ../../../form8829Pub534HomeDepreciation ships (dictionary/ty2025/scheduleC.xml, the row (d) bullet in this section's header), it is exported and off the cessation year on a mid-month versus full-month convention conflict that the row (d) bullet states in full. Wiring an ACRS percentage into an add-on that is then multiplied by ../../../form8829PartYearFraction, a MID-month fraction, would ship that same known-wrong convention on a second population. (ii) [1993-05-13, 1993-12-31]: the add-on table's binding-contract row. The home's own ../../../writableHomeBindingContractBeforeMay131993 answers the question the printed row asks, in the printed row's own words ("you either started construction or had a binding contract to buy or build that home before May 13, 1993"), so the window is REACHABLE and this exclusion is a SCOPE choice, not a documented impossibility. [NEITHER ARM OF THIS WINDOW IS BLOCKED BY A SOURCE. The TRUE arm does land on Table A-7's year-33 row, the table's LAST and a PARTIAL one, but ../../../form8829DepreciationPercentage's BAND 1b carries exactly that argument FOR THE HOME and answers the whole window on both arms, and ../../../form8829CessationIsModeled excludes the TRUE arm ONLY where a mid-year CESSATION is also present - it says in terms that "THE FALSE ARM IS NOT EXCLUDED and must not be". The FALSE arm is the printed 2.564 percent row and needs nothing but BAND B's floor moved down to 1993-05-12 under an answered-and-false guard. WHAT THIS UNIT LACKED WAS BUDGET, NOT AN ARGUMENT: reproducing BAND 1b's per-month year-33 reasoning, its IsComplete guard and its cessation cross-exclusion per ROW is a second copy of the hardest argument in this section, and the population it buys - an improvement placed in the last seven and a half months of 1993 on a home already in business use before then - is vanishing.] It is a NAMED GAP a successor should close rather than a boundary of the printed rule: a filer with such an expenditure keeps the attested ../../../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation, which is where they were before this unit.
TAX-YEAR-PINNED. Every Day literal below is a TY2025 boundary; the twelve percentages are Table A-7a's first-year row, correct only for an expenditure placed in service in the filing year; and BAND A's 0 percent depends on the filing year being far enough past 1993 to exhaust Table A-7. A TY2026 module must re-derive all three.
FOR THE AMT PER-ASSET SURFACE: the three-band, both-ends-fenced, no-fall-through structure is the part the AMT per-asset surface inherits, not the percentages.
[THERE ARE NOW FOUR BANDS, NOT THREE, and the NAMED GAP above is CLOSED rather than restated — the paragraph is kept verbatim because a reader must be able to see what was withdrawn and on what argument. The new band is [1993-05-13, 1993-12-31], fenced at both ends like the others and admitted only when ../../../writableHomeBindingContractBeforeMay131993 is COMPLETE. A true attestation takes Pub. 946 Table A-7 (nonresidential real property, mid-month, straight line 31.5 years), recovery year 33, keyed by the expenditure's OWN month: 0 percent for May and June, then 0.132%, 0.397%, 0.661%, 0.926%, 1.190% and 1.455% for July through December — the printed row cell for cell (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p946.pdf, page 74). A false attestation takes the printed 2.564 percent 39-year row. That is exactly what the Form 8829 line-42 add-on table prescribes: "after May 12, 1993, and before 1994, and you either started construction or had a binding contract to buy or build that home before May 13, 1993 → the percentage given in Pub. 946", and "after May 12, 1993, and before 2025 (except as noted below) → 2.564%" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, the line-42 table). The pre-1987 Pub. 534 refusal (i) is UNCHANGED and still stands.

Fact.Name: The business part of this expenditure's cost or other basis
Fact.Description:
The figure the add-on table multiplies by the percentage: "the business part of their cost or other basis". Pub. 587 says in terms which percentage that is - "Multiply the cost of the improvement by the business-use percentage" - so it is the HOME's line-7 business percentage, ../../../form8829BusinessPercentage (daycare-ratio-adjusted where it applies). An earlier version of this fact inlined "this dictionary's EXCLUSIVE-USE READING is line 1 divided by line 2" here, which mis-stated the daycare population the same way ../../../form8829BusinessBasisOfBuilding's own Description flagged as a shared gap - closed by reading the canonical fact instead, the way that sibling and ../../../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesDeduction / ../../../form8829OperatingExpensesWithCarryover now do too.
NO PER-ROW BUSINESS-PERCENTAGE INTAKE IS MINTED, AND THAT IS A DECISION WITH A DIRECTION. The records contract's column list said "business part" as though it were a per-row answer. It is not, on either printed source: the i8829 table says "the business part of their cost or other basis" without qualification and Pub. 587 names THE business-use percentage. THE GAP THIS LEAVES, named rather than hidden: an improvement made wholly INSIDE the business part of the home - rewiring the office, say - is arguably 100 percent business, and this fact gives it the home's percentage instead. The direction is TAXPAYER-ADVERSE for that sub-population and it is adopted anyway, because the printed rule states no exception and minting an override would be this dictionary answering a question no cited document asks. A successor that mints one owes the source that authorises it.
DIVIDE-BY-ZERO GUARD: total area 0 resolves this to 0 rather than throwing, the same guard ../../../form8829BusinessBasisOfBuilding carries. It is unreachable under the gate - ../../../form8829Part3IsModeled already requires a positive total area - and is kept for the same reason that fact keeps its own.
NO WHOLE-DOLLAR Round NODE. The Dollar type carries a fixed cent scale and rounds HALF_EVEN at every Multiply; the whole-dollar rounding happens once, downstream, on ../../../homeOfficeRegularDeduction, exactly where it happens for the home's own term.
FOR THE AMT PER-ASSET SURFACE: the AMT per-asset surface inherits this shape - a per-row basis derived from a per-row cost and a form-level percentage - and inherits the named gap with it.

Fact.Name: Depreciation allowed on this addition or improvement (one line of the Form 8829 line 42 statement)
Fact.Description:
The add-on table's own arithmetic for one expenditure: the business part of its cost or other basis times the percentage its placed-in-service month selects.
THE THIRD TERM IS THE SHIPPING DISPOSITION FRACTION AND IT IS REUSED, NOT REDERIVED. ../../../form8829PartYearFraction implements Pub. 946's "Sale or Other Disposition Before the Recovery Period Ends" months-over-12 rule, and the add-on table carries the SAME cessation row the Line 41 table does ("after May 12, 1993, and you stopped using your home for business before the end of the year, the percentage given in Pub. 946 as adjusted by the instructions under Sale or Other Disposition Before the Recovery Period Ends"). The fraction is TOTAL and complete-safe - 1/1 on every return that did not cease business use - so this Multiply is arithmetically inert except on the disposition population, exactly as it is in ../../../form8829ComputedHomeDepreciation. That is the one-quantity-one-fact answer: there is one disposition fraction on this return and both terms of line 42 read it.
THE COMPOUND CASE IS EXCLUDED, in ../rowIsModeled rather than here: an expenditure placed in service in 2025 on a home given up in 2025 would stack the mid-month placed-in-service convention that Table A-7a's first-year row already carries against the mid-month disposition fraction, and no cited document composes them. It is the per-row twin of the exclusion ../../../form8829CessationIsModeled already carries for the home itself.
NO WHOLE-DOLLAR Round NODE, for the reason ../businessBasis states.
INCOMPLETE OUT OF DOMAIN, on purpose, inherited from ../depreciationPercentage: an expenditure whose date falls in a band this dictionary refuses leaves this fact Incomplete rather than taking a plausible number. Nothing reaches it in practice - ../rowIsModeled fences the same domain and ../../../homeAdditionsAreModeled is the only guard under which ../../../form8829AdditionsDepreciation sums these rows - so the Incompleteness is a backstop, which is the same posture ../../../form8829DepreciationPercentage records for its own.
FOR THE AMT PER-ASSET SURFACE: the per-row computed deduction, and the fact that it stays Incomplete rather than defaulting out of domain, is the part the AMT per-asset surface inherits.

Fact.Name: This addition-or-improvement row is one Form 8829 line 42 can compute (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
TRUE only when this row's own facts are answered AND the row falls inside the domain ../depreciationPercentage can answer. FALSE closes ../../../homeAdditionsAreModeled for the WHOLE business, which sends the business back to the attested ../../../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, the ../../../form8829Part3IsModeled idiom: the outer Switch asks only IsComplete questions, each of which resolves to a concrete Boolean whether or not the underlying writable is answered, so this fact never propagates Incomplete into the business-level gate.
FOUR CONDITIONS, each of them a refusal with a stated reason. (1) THIS ROW'S DATE AND COST ARE ANSWERED. A half-filled row makes the add-on total short, and a short add-on understates line 42 while looking authoritative. (2) THE EXPENDITURE WAS PLACED IN THE APPLICATION STRICTLY AFTER THE DAY BUSINESS USE OF THE HOME BEGAN (ruling IN-12; formerly day-inclusive). The comparison is by day, not by month, because line 37 caps the home's basis at its fair market value on the first-use DATE: an improvement finished earlier in the same month belongs in that basis on line 37, under the cap, and moving it to line 42 would let it escape the cap (or be counted twice if the filer also left it in line 37). The first-use day itself counts as on or after. The month still sets the depreciation percentage; it does not decide the line. The partition itself is printed on both sides: i8829 "Lines 37 Through 40" routes expenditures "placed in service after you began to use your home for business" to line 42, and Pub. 587 puts improvements made BEFORE that date into the basis of the home ("Add the costs of permanent improvements made before you began using your home for business to the basis of your property"). THE EQUALITY CASE (superseded by ruling IN-12): an improvement placed in service on the first-use day itself is part of the home's basis on lines 37-40, not a line 42 row, because line 37 is the basis "on the date you first used the home for business" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, page 5) and only an expenditure placed in service strictly after that day is separate (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, page 5). Such a row is FALSE here: it is not a line 42 row. When every listed row is in place by the first-use date, the business still computes Part III (../../../homeAdditionsAllInTheFirstUseBasis opens ../../../form8829Part3IsModeled) with line 42 the home figure alone; the filer includes those expenditures in ../../../writableForm8829HomeBasisOrFmv. Both dates are asked to the day (../../../writableHomeFirstUsedForBusinessDate says why), so the line 37 intake (../../../writableForm8829HomeBasisOrFmv) and this collection partition the improvements without overlap. (3) THE DATE IS INSIDE THE MODELED BANDS. [1987-01-01, 1993-05-12] or [1994-01-01, 2024-12-31] or [2025-01-01, 2025-12-31]; the pre-1987 row and the 1993 binding-contract window are excluded, and ../depreciationPercentage's Description argues both. (4) NOT THE COMPOUND OF A 2025 PLACEMENT AND A 2025 CESSATION. Table A-7a's first-year row already carries the placed-in-service mid-month convention and ../../../form8829PartYearFraction is the mid-month DISPOSITION convention; nothing cited composes the two. This is the per-row twin of the first compound exclusion in ../../../form8829CessationIsModeled, which excludes exactly this shape for the home itself, and it is asked here rather than there so the home's own gate keeps its committed behaviour byte-identically.
WHAT IS NOT ASKED HERE: the description. Nothing computes from it, so refusing a whole business's line 42 over a missing label would be a data-completeness refusal with no tax consequence behind it.
FOR THE AMT PER-ASSET SURFACE: this per-row complete-safe domain predicate, and the every-row aggregation over it at ../../../homeAdditionsAreModeled, are the pair the AMT per-asset surface inherits.
[CONDITION (3) NOW ADMITS A FOURTH BAND. The sentence above naming [1993-05-13, 1993-12-31] as excluded is kept verbatim and is now false: the window is admitted whenever ../../../writableHomeBindingContractBeforeMay131993 is COMPLETE, which is the same fence ../depreciationPercentage's new band uses, so the two stay in lockstep and a row can never be modeled on a band the percentage refuses. CONDITION (2) now compares by day, day-inclusive (see (2) above).]

Fact.Name: Every listed addition or improvement was in place by the first business-use date (in the line 37 basis)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the filer said the home has additions or improvements (../writableNoHomeAdditionsOrImprovements answered No), listed at least one (../homeAdditions), and every listed row was placed in service on or before the first day of business use (../writableHomeFirstUsedForBusinessDate). Such expenditures are part of the home's basis on line 37, the basis "on the date you first used the home for business" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, page 5); only those placed in service after that day are figured separately on line 42 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, page 5 "that were placed in service after you began to use your home for"). So the business computes Part III with line 42 the home figure alone, adding no add-on (../form8829Part3IsModeled reads this beside ../homeAdditionsAreModeled). Ruling IN-12, row FED-1040SC-F8829-LINE42-ADDITIONS-040. FALSE when any row is after the first-use date or has an unanswered date (complete-safe).

Fact.Name: This business's additions-and-improvements table is one Form 8829 line 42 can compute (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
TRUE only when the filer answered NO to ../writableNoHomeAdditionsOrImprovements AND opened the ../homeAdditions table AND listed at least one row AND EVERY row is one ../homeAdditions/*/rowIsModeled accepts. It is the second arm of the additions conjunct in ../form8829Part3IsModeled: the first arm is the attestation of ABSENCE, which is what every return that existed before this unit takes.
COMPLETE-SAFE, AND THE COLLECTION ROOT IS WHY THE OUTER GUARD IS SHAPED THIS WAY. A CollectionSize or a Count over a collection root the return never opened resolves PLACEHOLDER rather than Complete, and a Placeholder reaching ../form8829Part3IsModeled would blank Schedule C line 30 on returns that resolve today. An IsComplete on the ROOT is the instrument that stops it, and it is not invented here: scheduleE:/formK1s/*/atRiskActivitySharesRecorded uses exactly this guard over the nested ../atRiskActivityShares collection and records the same reason. Measured on a scratch probe: a CollectionSum over an absent nested root resolves Placeholder; IsComplete over that same absent root resolves Complete FALSE; over an EMPTY root it resolves Complete TRUE and the sum is Complete 0.
AT LEAST ONE ROW IS REQUIRED, and that conjunct is not decoration. A filer who answered NO to the absence attestation has said they HAVE such expenditures; an empty table then contradicts the answer that summoned it, and treating it as a $0 add-on would UNDERSTATE line 42 in precisely the way ../writableNoHomeAdditionsOrImprovements was minted to prevent. Such a return stays on the attested figure instead.
EVERY ROW, NOT ANY ROW. Count over a Boolean collection counts the TRUE items, so "as many trues as the collection has rows" is "every row" - the scheduleE:/formK1s/*/atRiskActivitySharesAnswered idiom, copied deliberately. ONE unmodelable row closes the gate for the whole business rather than dropping that row from the sum, because a dropped row is a short add-on and a short add-on understates line 42. The direction is taxpayer-protective in both branches: the filer keeps their own attested figure, which can carry the add-on this dictionary cannot itemise.
AN UNANSWERED ATTESTATION CHANGES NOTHING. The outer Switch requires it answered, so a return that never reached the question resolves this FALSE and takes the attested route, byte-identically the pre-unit behaviour.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 42 add-on — depreciation on additions and improvements placed in service after business use began
Fact.Description:
The second term of Form 8829 line 42: the total depreciation allowed on the additions and improvements the filer listed, which i8829 "Line 42" says to "include in the total for line 42" alongside line 40 times line 41.
TOTAL, AND COMPLETE-SAFE $0 ON THE GATE-FALSE BRANCH: $0 whenever ../homeAdditionsAreModeled is false, which is every return that existed before this unit, so ../form8829ComputedHomeDepreciation can add it unconditionally and every committed fixture is arithmetically untouched. ON THE GATE-TRUE BRANCH it inherits the same backstop Incompleteness ../homeAdditions/*/depreciationAllowed records - a true cessation flag whose cessation date is unanswered or outside the filing year leaves ../form8829PartYearFraction Incomplete. That shape is unreachable through the wiring, because it makes ../form8829CessationIsModeled false, which closes ../form8829Part3IsModeled, which is the only route into this fact; it is stated anyway because this fact is exported. The Switch is what keeps it complete-safe rather than the sum itself: a CollectionSum over a nested collection root the return never opened resolves PLACEHOLDER, and the leading Case reads only ../homeAdditionsAreModeled, which is complete-safe by construction.
NO WHOLE-DOLLAR Round NODE, for the reason ../form8829ComputedHomeDepreciation states: line 42 carries cents and the whole-dollar rounding happens once, downstream, on ../homeOfficeRegularDeduction.
WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. It does not build the attached statement itself. i8829 "Line 42" also says "Attach a statement showing your computation" and "Enter 'See attached' below the entry space", and that is a DISCLOSURE surface rather than a number: the CONTENT of the statement is exactly ../homeAdditions/*/writableDescription, ../homeAdditions/*/writableCostOrOtherBasis, ../homeAdditions/*/writableDatePlacedInService and ../homeAdditions/*/depreciationAllowed, all of them exported, so nothing further is owed by this dictionary; what remains is the print-template and MeF binding, which are not dictionary computation. It also does not touch the Form 4562 line 19j routing the same instruction describes, because Form 4562 is not modeled in this repo at all.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 Part III is computed for this business (complete-safe domain gate)
Fact.Description:
TRUE only when every Part III input is answered AND the return falls inside the domain this dictionary can compute — see the section header above for the three exclusions and why each is an exclusion rather than a guess. FALSE sends the business to the attested ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation, which is where every return was before this fill.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, on the ../mayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems idiom: the outer Switch asks only IsComplete questions, each of which resolves to a concrete Boolean whether or not the underlying writable is answered, so this fact NEVER propagates Incomplete into ../regularHomeOfficeInputsComplete. An unanswered collection item resolves it FALSE.
THE ELECTION IS DELIBERATELY NOT A CONJUNCT. ../electsRegularHomeOfficeMethodComplete does not appear here, so a business that supplies Part III inputs while electing the simplified method still resolves a computed line 42. Nothing spends it as a deduction — ../homeOfficeRegularDeduction is gated on the election — but ../mayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems does see it, which is the same asymmetry the attested writable already had and the conservative direction on an AMT contradiction check.
TAX-YEAR-PINNED: the domain's upper bound is the filing year's last day and its floors are derived from the filing year's distance from the 1993 regime change, so every Day literal below moves with the tax year.
THE THIRD Any ARM IS A TWIN, NOT A COPY-PASTE CONVENIENCE. It reproduces BAND 1b of ../form8829DepreciationPercentage exactly - same two Day fences, same IsComplete guard - because this gate and that band must open on precisely the same returns. A drift between them opens the gate on a return whose percentage refuses, which would take a filer who was riding an attested figure and hand them an Incomplete line 42.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 42 — depreciation allowable, computed (line 40 × line 41, plus the additions-and-improvements add-on)
Fact.Description:
The computed line-42 figure. NO WHOLE-DOLLAR Round NODE: Form 8829 line 42 carries cents, the Dollar type's fixed cent scale with HALF_EVEN at every Multiply is what carries them, and the IRS's own published answer for this computation is $147.66. The whole-dollar rounding happens once, downstream, on ../homeOfficeRegularDeduction, exactly where it happened before this fill. On the published example no rounding pressure arises at any step, so the cent-exact match is real rather than a HALF_EVEN coincidence.
Only ever read under ../form8829Part3IsModeled (via ../form8829HomeDepreciation), so its out-of-domain Incompleteness — inherited from ../form8829DepreciationPercentage — is unreachable in practice.
[TWO TERMS. The paragraphs above describe the FIRST term: line 40 × line 41 × the disposition fraction. The second is ../form8829AdditionsDepreciation, the additions-and-improvements add-on i8829 "Line 42" says to "include ... in the total for line 42" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8829.pdf, page 6). It is a complete-safe $0 on every return that does not carry a modelable ../homeAdditions table - which is every return without that table - so this fact is VALUE-IDENTICAL on all of them, and the published Pub. 587 $147.66 answer the first paragraph names is still reproduced cent-exact (quarantined case scheduleC/p587-frankie-part3-depreciation-example (inner_models/packages/ty2025/federal/schedule-c-business/examples/trunk-quarantine/), committed UNEDITED). The no-whole-dollar-Round argument covers both terms.]

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 42 — depreciation allowable (effective: computed, else attested)
Fact.Description:
THE fact every consumer of Form 8829 line 42 reads. Computed from Part III when ../form8829Part3IsModeled, otherwise the filer's attested ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation.
PRECEDENCE IS COMPUTED-WINS, and it is the point of the fill rather than an accident of Switch order. When a return supplies both, the attested figure is the one the engine cannot check and the computed figure is the one derived from checkable inputs, so the computed figure controls and a stale or mis-stated line 42 stops being spendable. The attested writable is NOT retired: it is the whole route for every return outside the modeled domain, and for every return that has not answered Part III — which is every return that existed before this fill, so this fact is value-identical to ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation on all of them.
COMPLETENESS PASSES THROUGH UNCHANGED on the fallback arm: an unanswered attested writable leaves this Incomplete exactly as reading the writable directly did, which is what keeps ../mayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems' IsComplete guard meaning the same thing it meant before.

Fact.Name: Alternate ACRS method elected over a 45-year recovery period for this home
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION, per business: whether the alternate ACRS method was elected over a 45-YEAR recovery period for this home in the tax year it was placed in service. Only ever asked of a home first used for business in 1981 through 1986 (the ACRS window); see ../form8829Pub534HomeDepreciation, which is the only fact that reads it.
WHY IT IS AN INTAKE AND NOTHING ELSE ON THE RETURN CARRIES IT. Pub. 534 prints the alternate recovery periods as ELECTIVE and class-specific: 15-year real property may be recovered over 15, 35 or 45 years, 18-year real property over 18, 35 or 45 years, and 19-year real property over 19, 35 or 45 years. The election had to be made by the return due date, including extensions, for the tax year the property was placed in service, and once made it can be changed only with the consent of the Commissioner, who grants consent only in extraordinary circumstances. So it is a historical and effectively irrevocable fact about the home, decided up to forty-four years before this return, and no line of Form 8829, Schedule C or this dictionary reveals it.
PER-HOME, NOT PER-CLASS. Pub. 534 imposes a single class-wide recovery percentage for all property in a class placed in service in the same tax year for 3-, 5- and 10-year property only; it states no such constraint for 15-, 18- or 19-year REAL property. So this attestation sits on the collection item, which is also the grain Form 8829 works at.
THE TWO-WAY FOLD IS THIS DICTIONARY'S PROPOSAL, NOT A PUB. 534 STATEMENT, and it is safe for the TY2025 VALUE rather than for the semantics. FALSE folds together "regular ACRS" and "the 35-year alternate period was elected", because in the 2025 filing year a home placed in service in 1981 through 1986 stands at recovery year 40 through 45, and every Pub. 534 table for those two treatments has already terminated: their last printed rows are the 16th, 19th, 20th and 36th. Both therefore yield 0 percent, and the fold cannot move a TY2025 figure. A successor that ever needs to DISTINGUISH regular from 35-year (a TY2026 module, where recovery year 46 is live and month-dependent; a short tax year; an amended prior year) must re-derive that collapse before reusing this Boolean, and should widen it to an Enum over the elected period rather than reinterpret the flag.
UNANSWERED IS NEITHER TRUE NOR FALSE, and that is deliberate. ../form8829Pub534HomeDepreciation reaches this fact through IsComplete and falls back to the attested ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation when it is unanswered, so a filer who does not know what was elected in 1984 is never guessed in either direction.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 41 for a home first used for business in 1981 through 1986 (Pub. 534 ACRS percentage)
Fact.Description: The Pub. 534 ACRS percentage for a home first used for business from 1981 through 1986, which stands at recovery year 40 through 45 in 2025: 2.2 percent when the alternate ACRS method over 45 years was elected (../writableHomeAcrs45YearAlternateElected true; Table 14 row 12-45th and Table 15 row 11-45th print 2.2 in every month column), and 0 percent otherwise (every regular and 35-year alternate table has ended by year 40). Incomplete while the election is unanswered. Read by ../form8829Pub534HomeDepreciation and printed on line 41 through form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line41DepreciationPercentage on the Pub. 534 route.

Fact.Name: This business's Form 8829 line 42 is computed by Pub. 534 ACRS (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the home was first used for business from January 1, 1981 through December 31, 1986 (the ACRS band), business use did NOT stop during the year (../writableHomeOfficeUseStoppedDuringYear answered false), the 45-year alternate election is answered, lines 37 and 38 and both areas are answered with a positive total area, and the additions and improvements are either attested absent or all listed in rows ../homeAdditionsAreModeled accepts. Then line 42 is line 40 times the Pub. 534 percentage (../form8829Pub534HomeDepreciation) plus the additions add-on, and the filer's attested line 42 is not needed. A stop of business use during the year stays off this route: Pub. 534 prints a full-month disposition convention for 15-year and some 18-year real property, and this graph does not compose it; that population keeps the attested ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation. Complete-safe: every leg is an IsComplete test or read behind one, so it is FALSE, never Incomplete, on a return that does not answer them.

Fact.Name: Form 8829 line 42 for a home first used for business before 1987 (Pub. 534 ACRS)
Fact.Description:
The line-42 depreciation allowable for the LAST row of the i8829 "Line 41" second table: a home first used for business "before 1987", whose percentage the instruction routes to Pub. 534, Depreciating Property Placed in Service Before 1987. Business basis of building (line 40) times the Pub. 534 ACRS percentage.
THE DOMAIN IS A BAND FENCED AT BOTH ENDS, and neither end is optional. ACRS itself has both: "You cannot use ACRS for property you placed in service before 1981 or after 1986." Above the band, a placement after 1986 is MACRS and already has a shipping route through ../form8829DepreciationPercentage. Below it, a pre-1981 placement is pre-ACRS, and computing it needs a useful life the taxpayer estimated, a salvage value they estimated, and the method they actually elected. None of the three is in this graph and none is a lookup, so this fact does not resolve there. That is a data-completeness refusal, the only kind this project lets stand permanently, and it is expressed by the ABSENCE of a fall-through case rather than by a zero, because a zero would be an answer.
WHAT COLLAPSES, AND WHY THE ANSWER IS A TWO-ARMED SWITCH RATHER THAN A TABLE. Pub. 534's appendix prints seventeen ACRS percentage tables keyed on property class, month placed in service and elected recovery period. In the 2025 filing year, a home placed in service in 1981 through 1986 stands at recovery year 40 through 45, and at that depth class and month stop mattering: every regular table and every 15-, 18-, 19- and 35-year alternate table has already run out (last rows: the 16th, 19th, 20th and 36th), so each yields 0 percent, while BOTH 45-year alternate tables print a FLAT 2.2 across all twelve month columns exactly over the rows that contain 40 through 45 (Table 14, row 12-45th, for 18-year real property placed after June 22, 1984 and for 19-year real property; Table 15, row 11-45th, for 18-year real property placed after March 15 and before June 23, 1984 and for 15-year real property placed after December 31, 1980). So the ONLY discriminator left is whether the 45-year alternate period was elected, which is what ../writableHomeAcrs45YearAlternateElected records.
TABLE 17 IS THE ONE TABLE STILL LIVE AT RECOVERY YEAR 40, AND IT CANNOT REACH A HOME. The paragraph above is an exhaustion argument, so the one appendix table it does not enumerate has to be disposed of out loud rather than silently. Pub. 534's Table 17 is a FORTY-year schedule, headed "40-Year Recovery Period" at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p534.pdf, page 20, whose row "2-40th" prints 2.5 in all twelve month columns at line 1833 - so a home placed in service in 1986, which stands at recovery year 40 in TY2025, would sit inside a LIVE row of it rather than a terminated one. What excludes it is its own heading, which limits the table to 18- or 19-year LISTED property not used predominantly. Listed property is the section 280F class the same publication describes at lines 151 and 153: "Listed property includes cars, other" / "means of transportation, and certain" computers. A dwelling unit is none of those; the business use of a home is a section 280A question, which is the whole subject of Form 8829. So Table 17 never reaches this fact's population, and the collapse to 0 percent outside the 45-year election survives it. This paragraph exists because the pre-fill contract for this row named Table 17 among the tables the fill would have to account for, and an exhaustion census that drops a named table without a word is not one a reader can check.
THIS IS A TY2025 FACT AND THE TAX-YEAR PIN IS LOAD-BEARING. In TY2026 a 1981 placement reaches recovery year 46, which is the PARTIAL final row of both 45-year tables and IS month-dependent (Table 14's 46th row runs 0.1 through 2.1 across the twelve columns; Table 15's runs an em dash through 2.1). The flat-2.2 collapse dies that year, and a TY2026 module that inherited this body unchanged would ship a wrong constant silently.
UNANSWERED ELECTION KEEPS THE ATTESTED FIGURE. When the election flag is unanswered this fact resolves to ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation, the filer's own line-42 entry, because neither computed arm is safe to guess: guessing FALSE would zero a real deduction, and guessing TRUE would invent one. The IsComplete question comes FIRST in both answered arms.
WIRED FOR A HOME STILL IN BUSINESS USE AT YEAR END. ../form8829HomeDepreciation takes this fact (plus the additions add-on) whenever ../form8829Pub534IsModeled: the ACRS band, the election answered, business use NOT stopped during the year, and the additions attested absent or all modeled. A full year of use involves no disposition convention, so the printed 2.2 or 0 percent applies as it stands. A home whose business use STOPPED during the year stays on the attested figure: Pub. 534 prints a FULL-month convention for 15-year real property and for 18-year real property placed before June 23, 1984 (no deduction for the month of disposition), while ../form8829PartYearFraction implements Pub. 946's MID-month disposition convention; that reconciliation is still open. The line 41 percentage is ../form8829Pub534DepreciationPercentage.

Fact.Name: Regular home-office method — all inputs answered (complete-safe gate)
Fact.Description:
True only when the regular method is elected AND every Form 8829 input is answered — business area, total area, indirect expenses, direct expenses, and home depreciation. Built from IsComplete checks, each of which resolves to a concrete Boolean whether or not the underlying writable is answered, so this gate NEVER propagates Incomplete: an elected-but-unanswered return resolves this false and the regular deduction falls to a complete 0 (no latent Incomplete taint into Sch C net → total income — the defensive-gating lesson applied). The divide-by-zero guard (total area > 0) is applied downstream in ../homeOfficeRegularDeduction, where total area is guaranteed answered.
THE MORTGAGE-INTEREST/TAX TIER AND BOTH CARRYOVER-IN INTAKES ARE NOT GATED HERE, ON PURPOSE: ../writableForm8829IndirectMortgageInterestAndTaxes, ../writableForm8829DirectMortgageInterestAndTaxes, ../writableForm8829OperatingExpenseCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear, and ../writableForm8829ExcessCasualtyAndDepreciationCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear are each individually complete-safe $0 when unanswered — the common case, since most filers have neither a mortgage/tax component nor a prior-year carryover — so requiring them here would refuse the regular method for every filer who answers the five inputs this gate already names but leaves those four blank.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line 30 — business use of home (regular / Form 8829 method)
Fact.Description:
The Form 8829 regular-method allowable deduction, LAYERED to match Part II's own line 8→14→27→28→33 sequence (superseding the earlier aggregate reading below). Three tiers, in order:
TIER 1 (line 14, ../form8829MortgageInterestAndTaxesDeduction): an itemizer's deductible mortgage interest and real estate taxes, direct plus indirect × business-use percentage ($0 for a filer who claims the standard deduction, whose amounts are in tier 2). Added IN FULL, uncapped by the gross-income limitation — §280A(c)(5)(B)(i) excepts these amounts because they are deductible whether or not the home is used for business. It still reduces the budget available below it (line 15 = line 8 − line 14, ../form8829RemainingLimitAfterMortgageInterestAndTaxes).
TIER 2 (line 27, ../form8829AllowableOperatingExpenses): direct + indirect × percentage operating expenses (insurance, rent, repairs, utilities, other; for a filer who claims the standard deduction, also the home's mortgage interest and real estate taxes on lines 16 and 17) plus the prior-year carryover-in (line 25, ../writableForm8829OperatingExpenseCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear), capped at the tier-1 remainder.
TIER 3 (line 33 less line 35, ../form8829AllowableDepreciationAfterLinkedCasualty): line 29 excess casualty losses, home depreciation (Part III line 42) and the prior-year excess-casualty/depreciation carryover-in (line 31, ../writableForm8829ExcessCasualtyAndDepreciationCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear), capped at whatever the first two tiers leave — depreciation taken LAST, Pub. 587's own tie-break — less the line 35 casualty portion carried to Form 4684. So line 30 is printed Form 8829 line 36 in whole dollars.
Sum of the three tiers, whole-dollar rounded. Complete-safe 0 when the regular method is not elected or any of the five originally-required inputs is unanswered (../regularHomeOfficeInputsComplete false) and when total area is 0 (divide-by-zero guard); the mortgage/tax and both carryover-in writables default $0 unanswered independently of that gate (see their own facts).
CARRYOVERS. This year's line 25 and line 31 carryovers are intakes (../writableForm8829OperatingExpenseCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear and ../writableForm8829ExcessCasualtyAndDepreciationCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear), because no prior-year return is on this one. The carryovers to 2026 (Part IV lines 43 and 44) are form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line43OperatingCarryoverToNextYear and form8829:/scheduleCs/*/form8829Line44CasualtyDepreciationCarryoverToNextYear.

Fact.Name: This business's net profit excluded from U.S. gross income under section 931 or 933
Fact.Description:
The part of THIS business's Schedule C line 31 that is territory income excluded from U.S. gross income under section 931 (Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands) or section 933 (Puerto Rico). Optional; unanswered gives ../excludedTerritoryNetProfit $0.
AN ENTRY, NOT A COMPUTATION, and the graph cannot derive it: a Schedule C carries no geography. Nothing here applies the section 937(a) bona fide residence test or sources receipts to a possession; non-negativity is the only check on the writable itself, and the one relationship that CAN be enforced without a cross-fact Limit - that a business cannot exclude more than it earned - is enforced one level down, in ../excludedTerritoryNetProfit's Derived body. Same shape and same reasoning as schedule1A:/writableExcludedTerritoryQualifiedTips.
THE $0 TAIL IS TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE and is stated rather than buried: a filer with excluded Schedule C income who is never asked keeps the whole QBI admission this unit would deny. That population is refused today by ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion, which is the protection, exactly as it is for the two Schedule 8812 exclusion entries themselves.
INTENDED AS A DECOMPOSITION OF AN EXCLUSION ALREADY COLLECTED, NOT A NEW AMOUNT - AND THE INTENT IS NOT ENFORCED. A filer who excludes this income reports the same dollars on Schedule 8812 line 2a or 2c, which is what the seven MAGI surfaces read; this intake is meant to say WHICH business those dollars came out of. NOTHING MECHANICALLY TIES THE TWO TOGETHER: the engine has no cross-fact Limit, so a filer who answers here and leaves line 2a at $0 gets no knockout and seven MAGI surfaces blind to the amount - phaseouts too small, credits over-claimed, the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction, which is the exact failure the knockout exists to prevent, reached by a new route that bypasses it. THAT IS A DISCLOSED HOLE, NOT A CLOSED ONE, and it is the same hole schedule1A's two excluded-territory intakes already carry for the same reason. It is narrowed, not closed, by a WITNESS rather than by an argument: tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleC/ pr933-whole-schedule-c-excluded-closes-qbi-gate answers BOTH - the per-item 18,000 and Schedule 8812 line 2a at 18,000 - and pins /flowIsKnockedOut Complete true, so the shape this unit is built for is the shape the corpus witnesses, and it is a refused one.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: This business's excluded territory net profit, complete-safe and clamped
Fact.Description:
= ../writableExcludedTerritoryNetProfit when answered, else $0, and in either case capped at what this business actually produced: min(entry, max(0, ../netProfit)).
THE CAP IS THE POINT OF HAVING THIS FACT AT ALL. Only income a business produced can be excluded from that business, so an entry larger than its own line 31 is a mis-entry, and without the cap the return would report one Schedule C profit and a larger amount excluded from it - /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax would go NEGATIVE on a profitable return. The engine has no cross-fact Limit (see lint_writable_dependency: a Dependency inside a Writable is a cycle hazard), so the bound is expressed here, in a Derived body, which is the sanctioned alternative that lint names.
A LOSS BUSINESS EXCLUDES NOTHING HERE, and that is a disclosed limitation rather than a reading of section 933. The max(0, ../netProfit) floor means a business whose line 31 is NEGATIVE contributes $0 to the return's excluded total even if it is entirely Puerto Rico source. The statute disallows deductions "properly allocable to or chargeable against" excluded income, so a genuinely excluded LOSS should not reduce U.S. taxable income either; leaving it in means /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax carries a loss it arguably should not. DIRECTION: U.S. income too LOW, tax too LOW, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE. It is left open because the disallowance limb it belongs to is deferred and modelling half of it here would be worse than naming it.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: This business's net profit subject to U.S. income tax (its line 31 less its own exclusion)
Fact.Description:
= ../netProfit MINUS ../excludedTerritoryNetProfit. The PER-ITEM twin of /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax, and identical to ../netProfit on every business that excludes nothing, which is every business on every committed return.
THREE CONSUMERS, ONE QUANTITY, and the reason they are one quantity is the reason this fact exists rather than three inline Subtracts. All three are QBI sites and Publication 1321 answers all three with one sentence ("Bona fide residents of Puerto Rico cannot take the Qualified Business Income Deduction related to their Puerto Rico source self-employment income they are excluding under Sec. 933", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1321.pdf, page 6): 1. qbi:/scheduleCs/*/qbiAttributableHalfSeTax's NUMERATOR - this item's share of its owner's Schedule SE line 13; 2. qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/scheduleCDerivedQbi's MINUEND - the ABOVE-threshold (Form 8995-A) per-business derivation; 3. through the return-level /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax, qbi:/qbiAutoDerivedAmount's minuend - the BELOW-threshold (Form 8995) one. WIRING (2) AND (3) WITHOUT (1) WOULD SHIP A QBI DEDUCTION THAT JUMPS AT THE SECTION 199A THRESHOLD for this population - the refused defect shape and this module's /writableQualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear records - so the three move together or not at all.
WHY THE HALF-SE-TAX NUMERATOR AND NOT ITS DENOMINATOR. That proration is (owner's line 13) x (this item's profit) / (owner's whole Schedule SE line-3 base), and only the middle term moves here. The denominator is the SELF-EMPLOYMENT base, which section 1402(a)(6) computes "without regard to section 933" and which therefore still contains the excluded income. The algebra is the point: with one owner, one business and no K-1 the item's share becomes line13 x nonexcluded / base, which is EXACTLY Publication 570's apportioned deduction (scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction) - so QBI's minuend and its subtrahend shrink by the same rule. With a K-1 in the base the item's share is line13 x nonexcluded/base while the whole allowed deduction is line13 x (base - excluded)/base; the difference is the K-1's share of the allowed deduction, which is correctly NOT attributed to a Schedule C trade or business.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, SIGNED - a loss business passes its loss through unchanged, because ../excludedTerritoryNetProfit is floored at $0 for a loss item. DIRECTION of that floor is disclosed on ../excludedTerritoryNetProfit itself and is unchanged here. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: This business made a profit and was never asked how much of it was excluded
Fact.Description:
TRUE when THIS business has a POSITIVE line 31 and ../writableExcludedTerritoryNetProfit is unanswered. A KNOCKOUT INPUT and nothing else: it aggregates into /possessionUntreatedScheduleCNetProfit, which feeds ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion. It changes no deduction.
AN ANSWERED $0 DISCHARGES IT, which is why the test is IsComplete rather than an amount - exactly schedule1A:/possessionUntreatedTipsOrOvertime's reading, and for the same reason: a filer who says none of this business was excluded has ANSWERED the question, and every treatment built on the answer is then correct at zero rather than merely absent.
THE PROFIT CONDITION IS LOAD-BEARING, not a convenience. A $0 or loss business can exclude nothing (../excludedTerritoryNetProfit is capped at max(0, line 31)), so an unanswered intake on such a business leaves nothing inert and refusing on it would refuse returns this dictionary computes right. It is also what keeps every committed knockout fixture unmoved: the eight cases that answer a Schedule 8812 line 2a or 2c and carry a Schedule C all carry a $0 one.
COMPLETE ON EVERY RETURN BY CONSTRUCTION, because it feeds a knockout and an Incomplete member would leave flow:/flowIsKnockedOut unresolved on returns that resolve it today. The All opens with IsComplete(../netProfit) and All short-circuits to Complete(false), so an item whose receipts and expenses were never entered yields a Complete false rather than propagating its own incompleteness. IsComplete itself always returns a COMPLETE boolean (IsCompleteOperator returns Result(x.complete, true)).

Fact.Name: Schedule C net profit excluded from U.S. gross income under section 931 or 933
Fact.Description:
The return's total excluded Schedule C net profit: the sum over every entered business of ../excludedTerritoryNetProfit. $0 on every committed return, because no committed case answers the per-item intake.
THE IsComplete-THEN-CollectionSize DOUBLE GUARD is /scheduleCNetProfit's shipping shape, used verbatim and for the same reason: /scheduleCs is UNANSWERED on every return with no Schedule C, and a bare CollectionSum over an unanswered collection would make this fact Placeholder - which would propagate into /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax and from there into the QBI admission gate. Both no-collection arms are a Complete $0.
DOES NOT CARRY THE WORKING INTEREST. scheduleE:/workingInterestNetProfit is routed onto Schedule C without an item of its own, so it has no place to record an exclusion and is deliberately absent from this sum. DIRECTION: a filer whose oil or gas working interest is territory income cannot exclude it, so U.S. income is too HIGH and tax too HIGH - taxpayer-ADVERSE, and bounded by the same intake gap /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit already discloses (the working interest has no owner intake at all).
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, NON-NEGATIVE, whole dollars.

Fact.Name: This business's excluded territory net profit, as a term of the PRIMARY filer's own Schedule C total
Fact.Description: ../excludedTerritoryNetProfit when this business is the PRIMARY filer's and is not a statutory employee business, else 0. The gate is the one ../primaryFilerNetProfit uses, so the sum of this field is exactly the part of /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit that /scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit removes from /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax. Non-negative (../excludedTerritoryNetProfit is clamped to 0 and to the business's own line 31). Complete safe $0 on every business that does not answer the exclusion.

Fact.Name: This business's excluded territory net profit, as a term of the SECONDARY filer's own Schedule C total
Fact.Description: ../excludedTerritoryNetProfit when this business is the SECONDARY filer's and is not a statutory employee business, else 0. The twin of ../primaryFilerExcludedTerritoryNetProfit, gated as ../secondaryFilerNetProfit is, so the two partition the section 931/933 exclusion of every non-statutory business between the spouses. Non-negative. Complete safe $0 on every business that does not answer the exclusion.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's excluded territory Schedule C net profit (non-statutory businesses)
Fact.Description: The sum over every entered business of ../primaryFilerExcludedTerritoryNetProfit: the section 931/933 exclusion carried by the businesses whose line 31 forms the Schedule C term of /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit. Read by the Schedule SE trader carve-out on the Schedule 8812 line 18a base and on the Publication 570 self-employment fraction, where the trader's Schedule C profit leaves self-employment income whole but only its NONEXCLUDED part sits in /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax. Does not carry the working interest, for the reason /scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit gives. The IsComplete-then-CollectionSize double guard is /scheduleCNetProfit's shipping shape: an unanswered /scheduleCs gives a Complete $0. Dollar, non-negative, whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's excluded territory Schedule C net profit (non-statutory businesses)
Fact.Description: The sum over every entered business of ../secondaryFilerExcludedTerritoryNetProfit: the section 931/933 exclusion carried by the businesses whose line 31 forms the Schedule C term of /secondaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit. The twin of /primaryFilerScheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit, read by the spouse's IRA compensation. The IsComplete-then-CollectionSize double guard is /scheduleCNetProfit's shipping shape: an unanswered /scheduleCs gives a Complete $0. Dollar, non-negative, whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Total Schedule C line 31 of the STATUTORY EMPLOYEE businesses on this return
Fact.Description:
The sum of /scheduleCs/*/statutoryEmployeeNetProfit over every entered business: the line 31 amount that the printed earned-income worksheets exclude from their Schedule C line 31 collection, because the same income is collected as Schedule C LINE 1 on its own line instead. The per item fact carries the full statement of the rule and the printed lines; it is not repeated here.
ITS ONE CONSUMER is scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax, the Schedule 8812 line 18a self-employment addend, which subtracts it to answer Earned Income Worksheet line 2b. The EIC-side twin scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome does NOT read this fact and must not: it already excludes a statutory business by summing the gated per filer totals, and reading this as well would subtract the same line 31 twice.
NOT SUBTRACTED INSIDE /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax ITSELF, deliberately. That fact's other consumer is /hasScheduleCNetProfit, the Schedule C arm of qbi:/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness, and whether a statutory employee's Schedule C is a qualified trade or business under IRC 199A is a DIFFERENT question with its own answer; this unit does not decide it and must not move that gate as a side effect.
SHAPED LIKE /scheduleCNetProfit: the IsComplete-then-CollectionSize double guard over /scheduleCs, so an absent or unanswered collection is a Complete $0 rather than a Placeholder, and Round at this level so the subtraction is whole dollar against a whole dollar minuend. Complete $0 on every committed return.
POPULATION WIDENED TO BOTH ARMS OF THE LINE 1 CHECKBOX by the per item fact's gate, not by any change to this body. It now covers the ATTESTATION-ONLY businesses as well as the routed ones, because this unit built their 2a add-back (/primaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeScheduleCLine1 and its secondary twin below) and the printed 2a/2b pair must key on ONE population. The paragraph above that says the EIC-side twin scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome must not read this fact is UNCHANGED and still binding, and now for both arms: that fact sums the per filer Schedule C totals whose own gate is /scheduleCs/*/isStatutoryEmployeeIncome, which already zeroes an attested business. On the attestation fixture tests/nodes/ty2025/income/statutory-attestation-only-schedule-c-keeps-pre-existing-18a this fact moves 0 -> 40,000 and Schedule 8812 line 18a moves 60,000 -> 70,000, the worksheet's own foot. The committed corpus is unmoved.

Fact.Name: PRIMARY filer's total Schedule C line 1 across his ATTESTATION-ONLY statutory businesses
Fact.Description:
The sum of /scheduleCs/*/primaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeLine1 over every entered business: the Schedule C LINE 1 amount that every printed earned-income worksheet adds back on its own line, for the arm of the line 1 checkbox that no box-13 W-2 explains. The per item fact carries the full statement of the rule and the printed lines; it is not repeated here.
ITS CONSUMERS ARE THE TWO income.xml ADD-BACK QUANTITIES AND NOTHING ELSE: income:/primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages (the per filer chain - Form 2441 lines 4/5 and its Part III pair, the cdcc eligibility gates, the section 129 $5,000 screen, the section 219 compensation ceiling) and income:/statutoryEmployeeWagesInEarnedIncome (the return level chain - Schedule 8812 line 18a, its section 32 twin, eitc:/eitcEarnedIncomeBase and the section 63(c)(5)(B) floor). Those two chains are disjoint - the seam banner above income:/primaryFilerEarnedIncomeBaseWithStatutoryEmployeeWages states the property and this unit re-measured it by grep - so no consumer takes the add-back twice.
THE COMPANION EXCLUSION is /statutoryEmployeeScheduleCNetProfit above, whose gate this unit returned to /scheduleCs/*/isStatutoryEmployeeIncome so that the 2a add-back and the 2b exclusion cover ONE population. The two facts must be landed and retired together.
SHAPED LIKE /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit's first term: the IsComplete-then-CollectionSize double guard over /scheduleCs, so an absent or unanswered collection is a Complete $0 rather than a Placeholder. NOT Rounded, unlike /statutoryEmployeeScheduleCNetProfit: that fact is a subtrahend against a whole dollar minuend, and this one is an addend inside income.xml facts that Round at their own printed lines, beside cents preserving routed sums.

Fact.Name: SECONDARY filer's total Schedule C line 1 across her ATTESTATION-ONLY statutory businesses
Fact.Description: The secondary (MFJ spouse) twin of /primaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeScheduleCLine1, which carries the consumer list, the disjoint chain argument and the pairing with /statutoryEmployeeScheduleCNetProfit. Sums /scheduleCs/*/secondaryFilerAttestationStatutoryEmployeeLine1 under the same double guard, cents preserved, Complete $0 on every committed return.

Fact.Name: Schedule C net profit subject to U.S. income tax (line 31 less the section 931/933 exclusion)
Fact.Description:
= /scheduleCNetProfit MINUS /scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit. Identical to /scheduleCNetProfit on every return that excludes nothing, which is every committed case.
⚠ NOT income:/grossIncomeSubjectToUsTax, DESPITE THE NAME, and the two must not be substituted for each other. That fact is the NUMERATOR of Publication 570's apportionment fraction: GROSS income from all sources less the exclusions, attested rather than derived because gross income is not line 9 (the records file states why). This fact is a NET figure - one Schedule C line - and it is a SUBTRAHEND-style adjustment to Schedule 1 line 3, not a fraction numerator. The shared phrase "subject to U.S. tax" names the same DISTINCTION (included versus excluded), not the same quantity, and nothing here feeds that fraction.
THIS IS THE INCOME-TAX FIGURE; /scheduleCNetProfit REMAINS THE COMBINED LINE 31. The two must diverge, because section 933 takes the income out of gross income for income tax while section 1402(a)(6) leaves it in the self-employment tax base "without regard to section 933". This unit builds the divergence and consumes it in ONE place; the rest is deferred, with the reason below.
THE ONE CONSUMER RE-POINTED, AND WHY IT IS THE ONE THAT COULD BE. /hasScheduleCNetProfit is the Schedule C arm of qbi:/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness and has EXACTLY ONE dependency site in the whole dictionary (qbi.xml, /hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness). Publication 1321 settles its answer without a second rule: "Bona fide residents of Puerto Rico cannot take the Qualified Business Income Deduction related to their Puerto Rico source self-employment income they are excluding under Sec. 933" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1321.pdf, page 6). A filer who excludes EVERYTHING loses a QBI admission the publication denies: was true, now false. THE PARTIAL EXCLUDER IS NOT ALWAYS UNCHANGED, and the counterexample is stated rather than left for a review to find. The gate reads the RETURN-LEVEL net, so it can also flip on a filer who excludes only part: a 60,000 fully excluded business beside a 55,000 LOSS gives /scheduleCNetProfit 5,000 (gate true) and /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax -55,000 (gate false). The new answer is the consistent one - this gate already returned false for any return whose Schedule C nets a loss, and the non-excluded side here IS a loss - but "the gate is unchanged for a partial excluder" would be false, so it is not claimed. What IS claimed is narrower: the gate can only move from true to false, never the reverse, because the exclusion is non-negative. AN EARLIER REVIEW CLAIMED THIS BOOLEAN COULD NOT BE CLASSIFIED because it "gates QBI (EXCLUDE) and SE tax (INCLUDE)" at once. THAT IS FALSE AGAINST THIS TREE and the source of the error is named here rather than left to be re-derived: the claim came from /hasScheduleCNetProfit's own Description, which said it "gates the SE tax and any QBI linkage". No Schedule SE fact has read it since the per-filer split - the Schedule SE chains read /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit and /secondaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit directly. The stale sentence is corrected in place.
WHAT IS DEFERRED, WITH THE REASON, so the gap is not read as an oversight. Seven money consumers of /scheduleCNetProfit have an EXCLUDE answer that this fact would serve - income:/totalIncome, income:/totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi, socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3, qbi:/qbiAutoDerivedAmount, scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome, scheduleE:/section8582Magi and scheduleE:/rentalSection179IncomeLimit - and none of them is re-pointed here. TWO OF THEM ARE ARITHMETICALLY ENTANGLED WITH A RULE THIS UNIT DOES NOT BUILD. /qbiAutoDerivedAmount is (Schedule C net profit) MINUS the attributable half of self-employment tax, and /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome is (Schedule C net profit + K-1 + farm) MINUS /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction. Publication 570 chapter 4 prorates that subtrahend for exactly this filer - "figure the self-employment tax on the nonexcluded income by multiplying your total self-employment tax (from Schedule SE (Form 1040)) by the following fraction: Self-employment income subject to U.S. income tax / Total self-employment income (including excluded territory income)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p570.pdf, page 33) - and Publication 1321 states the all-excluded case flatly ("you cannot deduct one-half of self-employment tax (Schedule SE) if you are excluding your self-employment income (Schedule C)", lines 273-275). Moving the MINUEND to the excluding figure while the SUBTRAHEND stays computed on the including figure makes both differences too small: QBI too small (taxpayer-adverse) and Schedule 8812 line 18a earned income too small (taxpayer-adverse).
