Moving the SUBTRAHEND alone, without moving the income, is the defect to avoid - it would deny a deduction computed on income the return still reports as taxable, taxpayer-adverse and unsupported by the publication, whose disallowance is conditioned on "if you are excluding". THE TWO ARE MUTUALLY REQUIRED: neither is safe without the other, and both together are a larger unit than this one. ⚠ THE QBI HALF OF THAT ENTANGLEMENT IS DISCHARGED, AND THE OTHER HALF IS NOT. Publication 570 chapter 4's proration now exists at scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxOnNonexcludedIncome and is taken at scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction, so /qbiAutoDerivedAmount moved BOTH of its halves together: its minuend to this fact, and its subtrahend through the per-item ../netProfitSubjectToUsTax, which shrinks each business's share of its owner's line 13 by the same nonexcluded fraction. The above-threshold twin (qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/scheduleCDerivedQbi) moved with it, because moving one and not the other makes the deduction jump at the section 199A threshold. /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome DID NOT MOVE, and the reason is a per-consumer one rather than an arithmetic one: its subtrahend is now pinned to scheduleSE:/fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction so that BOTH halves keep today's reading, which is the "or not at all" arm of the same rule. The evidence and the three gaps that block the move are on that fact. AND ONE OF THE SEVEN HAS NO VENDORED ANSWER AT ALL: scheduleE:/rentalSection179IncomeLimit, the Form 4562 line 11 business-income limitation. Nothing in Publication 570, Publication 1321, Publication 946 or the Form 4562 instructions says whether "taxable income from the active conduct of a trade or business" is measured before or after a section 933 exclusion. Re-bodying /scheduleCNetProfit would answer that question silently, in the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction (smaller limit, less section 179). Not re-pointing it leaves today's answer standing and visible. THE THREE THAT ARE SETTLED AND STILL DEFERRED, so the deferral is not mistaken for doubt: /totalIncome and its IRA bound follow section 933 itself; /section8582Magi follows AGI because section 469(i)(3)(E) names no exclusion section (26 U.S.C. 469, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section469&num=0&edition=2024, the walk already recorded on ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion); and socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3 must EXCLUDE rather than include, because that same fact already adds ctcOdc:/puertoRicoIncomeExclusion933 and /possessionIncomeExclusion931 back under section 86(b)(2) (socialSecurity.xml lines 1669 and 1671) - classifying it INCLUDE would count the income twice and over-tax the benefits. They are deferred only because they belong in the same move as the two entangled ones, and a partial application is what /scheduleCNetProfit's own Description warns against.
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ ⚠⚠ THE DEFERRAL IS DISCHARGED. THIS TABLE IS THE OPERATIVE ONE; EVERYTHING ABOVE IT IS THE RECORD OF WHAT WAS LEFT OPEN. Every consumer of /scheduleCNetProfit was RE-DERIVED against its own authority rather than moved as a block, and the classifications were re-read from the primary sources rather than inherited from the paragraphs above. Eight sites, six of them money: MOVED to this fact (EXCLUDE - section 933(1) takes the income out of gross income, and Publication 1321 says it in plain words: "The income you receive from Puerto Rico sources (except income received as a civilian or military employee of the U.S. government) is not subject to U.S. income tax", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1321.pdf, page 1): 1. income:/totalIncome - Schedule 1 line 3 / Form 1040 line 9. THE UNIT'S HEADLINE. 2. income:/totalIncomeUpperBoundForIraMagi - the section 219(g) dominance bound, moved in LOCKSTEP with (1) or it stops dominating tightly. Its tsv row moved too. 3. socialSecurity:/socialSecurityBenefitsWkshtLine3 - section 86(b)(2) defines this base as AGI "determined without regard to ... 911, 931, and 933" (26 U.S.C. 86, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section86&num=0&edition=2024), and the two possession exclusions are already in as explicit ADD-BACKS. So the line-3 term must be the NONEXCLUDED figure: with the combined line 31 the excluded profit arrived TWICE. Net effect for a filer who reports the exclusion consistently: the double count is removed, provisional income falls, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE and CORRECT. For a filer who answers the per-item intake but leaves Schedule 8812 line 2a at $0 the residual REVERSES - see that fact. 4. scheduleE:/section8582Magi - IRC 469(i)(3)(E) lists what AGI is determined without regard to (section 86 inclusions; the sections 85(c)/135/137 exclusions; the sections 219/221/250 deductions; any passive activity loss) and does NOT name section 931 or 933 (26 U.S.C. 469, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section469&num=0&edition=2024). It therefore follows PLAIN AGI, which excludes the income. Note the contrast with (3): two MAGI statutes, two lists, opposite treatments of the same dollars - which is the whole reason each consumer was classified separately. STAYED on /scheduleCNetProfit: 5. scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome (INCLUDE) - section 1402(a)(6) computes net earnings from self-employment "without regard to section 933". Its subtrahend is pinned by name to scheduleSE:/fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction so BOTH halves keep today's reading; the three gaps that block the Schedule 8812 line-18a half are on that fact and are unchanged by this unit. 6. scheduleE:/rentalSection179IncomeLimit (UNSOURCED, left standing and said so) - nothing in Publication 570, Publication 1321, Publication 946 or the Form 4562 instructions says whether Form 4562 line 11's "taxable income from the active conduct of a trade or business" is measured before or after the exclusion. Moving it would answer that silently and taxpayer-ADVERSELY. Direction if the reading left standing is wrong: line 11 too high, section 179 over-allowed, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE. NEVER READ IT (verified, not assumed): 7-8. the two per-filer Schedule SE terms /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit and /secondaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit are CollectionSums over /scheduleCs/*/primaryFilerNetProfit and /scheduleCs/*/secondaryFilerNetProfit. THE TWO ENTANGLED CONSUMERS ARE BOTH RESOLVED. qbi:/qbiAutoDerivedAmount moved both halves together at step 1. /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome takes the "or not at all" arm on both, which is item 5. ⚠ A NINTH CONSUMER EXISTS AND THE TABLE ABOVE IS INCOMPLETE, NOT WRONG. scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax reads THIS fact as its minuend — it is the Schedule 8812 line-18a twin of item 5, built rather than re-bodied precisely so item 5's section 1402(a)(6) reading could stay. ITEM 5 IS UNCHANGED AND ITS REASONING SURVIVES INTACT; what changed is that the "three gaps that block the Schedule 8812 line-18a half" it points at are all discharged, by IRC 24(d)(1)(B)(i)'s "which is taken into account in computing taxable income" clause. So this fact now has a consumer on each side of that split, which is what the per-consumer discipline was for. WITNESSES: tests/nodes/ty2025/income/pr933-total-income-excludes-schedule-c-exclusion (Form 1040 line 9 41,000 against 101,000 before; SSBW line 3 101,000 against 161,000; Form 8582 line 6 41,000; the IRA bound 41,000; and /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome and /rentalSection179IncomeLimit both UNMOVED at 92,935 and 100,000, which is what makes the per-consumer split a measurement rather than a claim) and the complete-safe twin pr933-total-income-exclusion-unanswered-is-identity (exclusion unanswered => every one of those surfaces is byte-identical to the pre-unit figure). ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, integer cents, SIGNED (a loss passes through), whole dollars. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Excluded possession income in the oil and gas working interest profit
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "How much of your oil and gas working interest net profit is income from sources within Puerto Rico (or a U.S. territory) that you exclude?" HELP TEXT: enter 0 when the well or property is not in Puerto Rico or the territory whose income you exclude: only income from sources within the possession is excluded. ASKED WHEN: the return reports a Puerto Rico or territory income exclusion on Schedule 8812 and a working interest net profit (scheduleE:/workingInterestNetProfit above $0). UNANSWERED POSTURE: the return is refused through /possessionUntreatedScheduleCNetProfit (condition of ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion). An amount above $0 is also refused there: the excluded part of a working interest is not yet apportioned. VALIDATION: Dollar, at least $0.

Fact.Name: A profitable Schedule C exists whose excluded-territory part was never asked
Fact.Description:
TRUE when at least one entered business satisfies ../possessionExclusionUnasked, OR when a positive oil-and-gas working interest is routed onto Schedule C without a per-business exclusion intake. A KNOCKOUT INPUT and nothing else: it is condition (v) of ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion, which refuses a possession return only where the Publication 570 chapter 4 treatment cannot be applied to the whole of it. It changes no deduction.
THE CONDITION LANDS WITH THE TREATMENT rather than after it. The per-item exclusion intake feeds three money treatments - the Publication 570 apportionment of the half-self-employment-tax deduction (scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction, and through it Schedule 1 line 15, Schedule 8812 line 22 and the section 24(d)(2) social-security comparison) and both QBI derivations. A filer who reports an exclusion at Schedule 8812 line 2a or 2c and is never asked the per-item question has ALL THREE go inert: the full half-SE deduction, the full QBI. DIRECTION: deductions too LARGE, tax too LOW, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE - the worst class, and the same one conditions (iii) and (iv) exist for.
WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH TO LEAVE THE $0 TAIL ALONE. The tail is RIGHT for every return with no exclusion at all, which is every committed return, and wrong for exactly the population the knockout screens. That is the same trade schedule1A:/possessionUntreatedTipsOrOvertime records, and the answer is the same: keep the tail, detect the population.
DOES NOT RE-TEST THE EXCLUSION. The knockout's outer conjunct already requires a non-zero Schedule 8812 line 2a or 2c, so this fact is a bare data-completeness question and is TRUE on plenty of ordinary returns that the knockout never looks at.
THE IsComplete-THEN-CollectionSize DOUBLE GUARD is /scheduleCNetProfit's shipping shape, used verbatim: /scheduleCs is UNANSWERED on every return with no Schedule C, and a bare Count over an unanswered collection would make this fact Placeholder - which would propagate into flow:/flowIsKnockedOut on returns that resolve it Complete today. Both no-collection arms are a Complete false.
THE WORKING-INTEREST ARM ASKS FIRST. /writableWorkingInterestExcludedTerritoryNetProfit asks how much of the working interest profit is excluded possession income; answered $0 (a well whose income is not from a possession, which IRC 933(1) and 931(a) never exclude), the arm is off. Unanswered, or answered above $0, it fires as below.
THE WORKING-INTEREST ARM IS THE SAME COMPLETENESS FAILURE AT RETURN LEVEL. scheduleE:/workingInterestNetProfit is the net oil-and-gas working-interest profit that scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit includes as a second Schedule C line 31, but it has no /scheduleCs/*/writableExcludedTerritoryNetProfit question. A positive value therefore cannot be safely apportioned; refusing the possession return is the conservative result. It is deliberately a guard only: the number is not added to /scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit, because no working-interest exclusion amount was entered. A zero or loss working interest does not open this branch.
WORLD-1: FALSE on every committed return, and on every committed node-test fixture that answers an exclusion. Of the twenty-eight fixtures answering a Schedule 8812 line 2a or 2c, twenty-seven carry no Schedule C or a $0 one, and the twenty-eighth (scheduleC/pr933-whole-schedule-c-excluded-closes-qbi-gate) ANSWERS the per-item intake. Negative control: tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleSE/pr933-se-deduction-answered-zero-exclusion-is-identity, a 100,000 Schedule C beside a 60,000 line-2a entry with both items answered $0, which resolves this FALSE and the knockout FALSE.

Fact.Name: Has a Schedule C net profit
Fact.Description:
Whether the Schedule C shows a positive net profit SUBJECT TO U.S. INCOME TAX. The Schedule C arm of qbi:/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness, and its only consumer.
It reads /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax rather than /scheduleCNetProfit, so that a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico who excludes the whole of a Schedule C under section 933 no longer opens the QBI admission on it: "Bona fide residents of Puerto Rico cannot take the Qualified Business Income Deduction related to their Puerto Rico source self-employment income they are excluding under Sec. 933" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1321.pdf, page 6). Value-identical on every return that excludes nothing, which is every committed case.
⚠ THE SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE WAS STALE AND A REVIEW REASONED FROM IT. It read: "Whether the Schedule C shows a positive net profit (gates the SE tax and any QBI linkage)." IT DOES NOT GATE THE SE TAX and has not since the per-filer split: the Schedule SE chains read scheduleC:/primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit and /secondaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit directly, and this boolean has exactly ONE dependency site in the whole dictionary, in qbi:/hasQualifiedTradeOrBusiness. An adversarial review used the old sentence to conclude that this fact "gates QBI (EXCLUDE) and SE tax (INCLUDE)" and therefore could not be classified at all - a blocker that does not exist. It is quoted rather than deleted for the same reason ctcOdc:/puertoRicoIncomeExclusion933 quotes its own retracted paragraph: a Description that is merely out of date reads exactly like one that is current.
PARTIAL EXCLUSION IS NOT ADDRESSED BY THIS GATE, only by the amount facts it does not reach. A filer who excludes part of one business still has positive non-excluded profit, so this stays true and qbi:/qbiAutoDerivedAmount still derives QBI from the WHOLE /scheduleCNetProfit - including the excluded part. DIRECTION: QBI too large, deduction too large, tax too low, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE; the population is refused today by ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion, and closing it is the deferred half recorded on /scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax above.

Fact.Name: This business deducted none of the Form 6251 items whose AMT treatment Schedule C's collapsed expense total hides
Fact.Description:
ATTESTATION OF ABSENCE, per business. The filer states that this Schedule C deducted NO depreciation, section 179 expense or amortization, NO depletion, NO circulation costs, NO research and experimental costs, NO mining exploration or development costs, NO intangible drilling costs, NO section 169 pollution-control-facility amortization, and reports NO long-term contract - i.e. that none of Form 6251 lines 2d, 2l, 2o, 2p, 2q, 2r or 2t, and neither of line 3's Schedule-C routes, has anything to draw from this business.
UNANSWERED IS NOT TRUE and never frees anyone: the consumer ../mayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems defaults TRUE, so a return that does not state this keeps exactly the treatment it has today. That is the whole safety argument for a fill that RELEASES rather than refuses.
AN ABSENCE, NOT A CONCLUSION. The filer is not asked whether an AMT adjustment exists - that is the computation this dictionary cannot do. The filer is asked whether the deductions exist, which is a question about their own Schedule C.
DELIBERATELY OVER-BROAD IN ONE PLACE, said plainly rather than implied: amortization appears here as a whole even though only some amortization regimes (section 169; the section 173/174/616-617 costs on lines 2o/2q/2r) create an AMT item. A business that amortizes a section 197 intangible and nothing else is therefore not freed by this attestation although it could safely be. Widening it is a later narrowing of the knockout, not a defect of this one, and the conservative direction is the one that cannot under-state AMTI.
THE OTHER SCHEDULE C INTAKES, checked rather than assumed. ../writableActualVehicleOperatingCosts is line-9 operating costs and its own Description records that depreciation and section 179 belong on line 13, not there - so the vehicle intake neither carries nor contradicts this attestation. ../form8829HomeDepreciation IS a depreciation figure the module can see, and an answered positive value CONTRADICTS this attestation; the contradiction is resolved against the attestation in ../mayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems. That consumer used to read the ATTESTED ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation, and once Form 8829 Part III could be COMPUTED a business could answer basis, land, date and the two Part III attestations, carry a real home-office depreciation deduction, leave the attested writable untouched, and be believed here. It now reads the effective line 42, which is the attested writable on every return that has not answered Part III.

Fact.Name: This business may carry an AMT item this dictionary cannot see
Fact.Description:
TRUE unless the business affirmatively attests absence AND nothing the module can see contradicts it. Complete-safe TRUE - the direction that keeps today's treatment - so an unanswered attestation, an unanswered collection item and a partially answered return all leave form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference exactly where it was.
THE CONTRADICTION CONJUNCT IS NOT DECORATIVE. ../form8829HomeDepreciation is the one depreciation figure this module holds as its own number (Form 8829 line 42, the business portion of the home — computed from Part III where the return is in the modeled domain, and the attested ../writableForm8829HomeDepreciation otherwise, which is what this conjunct read before and what it still reads on every return that has not answered Part III), and a return that resolves it above $0 while attesting that the business deducted no depreciation has contradicted itself. Freeing that return would release exactly the understatement arm 1 of the knockout exists to prevent - and the home is section 1250 property, whose pre-1999 AMT life is 40 years against a 39-year regular life, so the adjustment is real rather than theoretical. The contradiction is resolved AGAINST the attestation, and the resolution is complete-safe on its own (IsComplete-guarded, so an unanswered Form 8829 line 42 does not make this Incomplete).

Fact.Name: Any Schedule C on this return may carry an AMT item this dictionary cannot see
Fact.Description:
The return-level roll-up form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference arm 1 reads. TRUE when ANY business fails ../mayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems, which is the shipping collection idiom in this module (a Count of the per-item flags compared GreaterThan Int 0, as /scheduleCs/proprietorUnansweredOnMfj). A two-business return is freed only when BOTH attest, which is the quantifier the knockout needs: one un-attested business is enough to hide the adjustment.
THE COLLECTION GUARD IS FIRST AND IS THE LANDMINE THIS REPO HAS PAID FOR THREE TIMES. A size test over an unanswered collection does not resolve, so the Count sits inside a Switch whose When is IsComplete(/scheduleCs); the fall-through is TRUE, not Incomplete and not False, because the consumer is a knockout that must stay Complete on every return and because "we cannot see the businesses" is not a reason to release one.
Exported: form6251 is the consumer and it is another module.

Fact.Name: Total of Part III lines 35 through 39 (Schedule C line 40)
Fact.Description:
Schedule C Part III line 40 for THIS business: add lines 35 through 39. Sums the five complete safe readings of the line 35 to line 39 intakes, so an unanswered detail line contributes 0 instead of making the whole total Incomplete.
WHAT IT PRINTS ON A BUSINESS WITH NO INVENTORY: 0. Every term defaults to 0, so a Schedule C whose Part III is untouched resolves this to 0 and the printed line 40 carries a zero rather than a blank. That is deliberate and it is the module's posture everywhere else: ../scheduleCGrossIncome treats each unanswered Part I intake as 0 by the same IsComplete idiom. The alternative, a plain sum that stays Incomplete until all five lines are answered, would blank line 40 on a return that legitimately answered only some of them, which is the worse of the two errors.
NOTHING DOWNSTREAM CONSUMES IT. Schedule C line 42, cost of goods sold, remains the attested ../writableCostOfGoodsSold that line 4 subtracts; this fact exists so the printed line 40 can carry its own arithmetic.

Fact.Name: Allowed section 179 deduction already included in this Schedule C business's net profit
Fact.Description: Enter the allowed current-year section 179 expense deduction allocated to THIS Schedule C business and already included in its expenses and line 31 net profit. It is asked for each Schedule C business that does not name its Form 4562 copy, because line 13 combines section 179 with other depreciation; a business that names its copy takes the copy's line 12 when this is unanswered. Fact.Name: Rent or lease of vehicles, machinery, and equipment (Schedule C line 20a)
Fact.Description:
Schedule C line 20a: the business portion of THIS business's rental cost for vehicles, machinery, and equipment it rented or leased, as a positive amount. BOUNDARY, the way ../writableLine24bDeductibleMeals states its own: if the filer leased a VEHICLE for a term of 30 days or more, IRC §280F(c)(2) requires the deduction be reduced by a lease-inclusion amount from a published IRS table (Pub. 463 ch. 4, "Leasing a Car") before the figure is entered here — the printed line asks for the ALREADY-REDUCED amount, and the graph does not apply the reduction or vendor the table, so the filer (or preparer) must apply it themselves. Machinery and equipment leases carry no such reduction; only a leased VEHICLE does.
../line20aVehicleMachineryAndEquipmentRentEntered reads this fact complete safe and is a term of ../line28TotalExpenses whenever ../expenseDetailLinesAnswered — answering this intake changes line 28, the same as any other line 8 through 27a detail line. ../writableTotalExpenses's own Description states the collapsed total must exclude every detail line separately reported this way. QUESTION TEXT: "What was the business portion of your rent or lease of vehicles, machinery and equipment? If you leased a vehicle for 30 days or more, enter the amount after subtracting the lease inclusion amount (Pub. 463, chapter 4, Leasing a Car)." NOT A DEFECT (row FED-1040SC-LINE20A-LEASE-INCLUSION-045, ARGUE): the line is the business portion of the rental cost, reduced by the filer by any inclusion amount: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 8 "enter on line 20a the business portion of your rental cost. But if you leased a vehicle for a term of 30 days or more, you may have to reduce your deduction by the inclusion amount. See Leasing a Car in chapter 4 of Pub. 463 to figure this amount." The instructions send the reduction to a Pub. 463 table the filer applies; the intake asks the reduced amount and says so.

Fact.Name: Total other expenses (Schedule C line 48, carried to line 27b)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part V line 48 for THIS business: "Total other expenses. Enter here and on line 27b". The sum of the Part V rows (../otherExpenses/*/writableAmount, each floored at $0) plus the IRC section 195 start-up deduction (../startUpExpendituresDeduction), which the instructions put in Part V ("Amortization. Include amortization in this part"; "Business startup costs"). $0 plus that deduction when Part V was never opened or is empty. It is the line 27b term of ../line28TotalExpenses on the itemized arm, and the printed line 27b and line 48 boxes both carry it, so printed lines 8 through 27b add to line 28.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C itemises its lines 8 through 27b
Fact.Description:
True when the filer answered ANY of the twenty two detail expense intakes on lines 8 through 27a, or entered any Part V other-expense row (line 48). This is the M2 mutual exclusion switch for Schedule C line 28 and it is the reason ../writableTotalExpenses can be retired without deleting it: one printed line, at most one intake path, and the more specific path wins.
GLOBAL, NOT PER LINE, and deliberately so. Answering advertising alone suppresses the collapsed total even though the total also stood for the other twenty one lines, because a filer who has begun itemising has told us the collapsed figure is superseded rather than additional. DIRECTION: taxpayer ADVERSE where a filer answers both and itemises incompletely, since the unitemised expenses are dropped; it is never an over deduction, and the intake rule is unchanged, which is to answer ONE expense path. This is exactly the posture form8396:/mortgageCreditCarryforwardVintageSlotsAnswered documents for the same shape.
LINE 9 IS NOT IN THE LIST, on purpose: the car and truck line is already COMPUTED (../carTruckExpenses) rather than intaken, so it is an unconditional term of line 28 and cannot be evidence of itemising.
A LINKED FORM 4562 COPY (../writableForm4562CopyNumber) COUNTS ONLY WITHOUT A COLLAPSED TOTAL. The collapsed ../writableTotalExpenses already includes line 13, so a copy linked beside it is not evidence of itemising and does not drop the collapsed total; a copy linked with no collapsed total is the line 13 detail line.
THE PART V ROW TABLE IS IN THE LIST: the last disjunct is All(IsComplete(../otherExpenses), CollectionSize(../otherExpenses) > 0) - a NONEMPTY Part V row table selects detailed mode, an absent or empty one does not, and the IsComplete on the collection ROOT keeps the predicate complete-safe on a return that never opened Part V.
IsComplete never propagates incompleteness, so this fact is Complete on every return and FALSE on a return that answers none of them.

Fact.Name: Total expenses before expenses for business use of home (Schedule C line 28)
Fact.Description:
Schedule C line 28 for THIS business: "Total expenses before expenses for business use of home. Add lines 8 through 27b". It is the fact ../tentativeProfit now subtracts.
TWO ARMS, ONE PRINTED LINE. When ../expenseDetailLinesAnswered the total is the sum of the twenty two complete safe detail readings for lines 8 and 10 through 27a, PLUS the computed line 9 (../carTruckExpenses), PLUS line 27b, which is ../line48TotalOtherExpenses. Otherwise it is the collapsed attestation ../writableTotalExpenses plus that same line 9 — which is EXACTLY the pair of subtrahends ../tentativeProfit carried before this edit, so every committed line 29, line 31, QBI and self employment tax figure is byte identical.
LINE 9 IS ADDED ONCE, HERE, AND IS NOT ALSO SUBTRACTED BY LINE 29. That is the single most dangerous thing about this edit and it is why the change to ../tentativeProfit had to land in the same one: line 29 used to subtract ../writableTotalExpenses AND ../carTruckExpenses as two subtrahends, and it now subtracts this fact alone. Keeping the old second subtrahend would deduct the standard mileage twice.
../startUpExpendituresDeduction (IRC §195) IS IN BOTH ARMS: on the itemized arm inside line 27b (../line48TotalOtherExpenses, Part V, where the instructions put amortization), on the collapsed arm as its own addend. It is computed from its own two intakes and ../writableTotalExpenses scopes it out of its total, so it is never entered twice.
../writableTotalExpenses IS RETIRED BY THE FIRST ARM, and retired means SUPPRESSED, not deleted: it keeps its path and its meaning for the very common return that reports one collapsed figure, and ../expenseDetailLinesAnswered decides. Its own Description demanded exactly this of any successor, as does every one of the twenty two detail intakes: "A successor that later derives line 28 by adding these detail intakes must retire the collapsed total in the SAME unit, or line 29 subtracts every detail line twice."
NO ROUND HERE. Every term is already whole or is a filer typed Dollar, and ../tentativeProfit wraps the whole line 29 subtraction in its own Round, which is the posture: round the total, not the addends.
[LINE 27b IS NOW THE PART V ROW SUM. The detailed arm's line-27b term reads ../line48TotalOtherExpenses, which no longer wraps a collapsed attestation but sums ../otherExpenses/*/writableAmount; ../writableLine48TotalOtherExpenses is RETIRED (deleted, not suppressed). Everything the paragraphs above say about line 9 being added once and about ../startUpExpendituresDeduction being scoped out of both totals is UNCHANGED, and so is the no-Round argument.]

Fact.Name: Accounting method is other (Schedule C line F box 3)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line F box (3) for THIS business: a method that is neither cash nor accrual.
