Fact.Name: Schedule C line 41 as entered, or 0
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of ../writableLine41InventoryAtEndOfYear: that intake's value when it is answered, else 0. It is the subtrahend of ../costOfGoodsSold, so a Part III that lists its costs and leaves ending inventory blank subtracts 0 rather than going Incomplete. Same one box idiom as its five line 35 to line 39 siblings above.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C worked its Part III inventory schedule
Fact.Description:
True when the filer answered ANY of the six Part III dollar lines: lines 35 through 39 (the cost detail) or line 41 (ending inventory). It is the domain gate for ../costOfGoodsSold, the same shape ../form8829Part3IsModeled is for the Form 8829 home depreciation line, and it is the M2 mutual exclusion switch between the two intake paths for line 42.
WHY THE GATE EXISTS AT ALL. Every Part III line is complete safe to 0, so a Part III that was never touched computes line 40 minus line 41 as 0 minus 0 = 0. Without this gate a Schedule C that attests its cost of goods sold on line 4 and never opens Part III would have that attestation silently replaced by $0, which would ADD the whole cost of goods sold back into gross income. The gate is what keeps the attestation standing until the worksheet is genuinely in play.
LINE 33, LINE 34 AND THE LINE 33 VALUATION BOXES ARE NOT IN THE LIST, on purpose: they are method and change of method questions, not amounts, and a filer may answer them on a return whose amounts still come from the line 4 attestation.
IsComplete never propagates incompleteness, so this is Complete on every return and FALSE on every committed one: no committed scenario answers a Part III dollar line.

Fact.Name: Cost of goods sold (Schedule C line 42, carried to line 4)
Fact.Description:
Schedule C Part III line 42 for THIS business: "Cost of goods sold. Subtract line 41 from line 40. Enter the result here and on line 4". COMPUTED from the worksheet when ../part3IsAnswered, and otherwise the attestation ../writableCostOfGoodsSold, passed through unchanged INCLUDING its Incomplete.
THIS IS THE COMPUTED ELSE ATTESTED SWITCH ../form8829HomeDepreciation ALREADY USES for Form 8829 line 42, and the domain gate is the point of it. ../line40AddLines35Through39 was an orphan subtotal: it computed and printed, and nothing subtracted line 41 from it, so the printed line 42 carried the attestation as a name claim while the printed line 40 carried arithmetic that reached nothing. Both halves are now the same number on a worked Part III.
THE FALL THROUGH KEEPS THE ATTESTATION'S INCOMPLETE and does not floor it at $0. That matters: ../costOfGoodsSoldOrZero and ../scheduleCGrossIncome each apply their own IsComplete guard around this fact, exactly as they applied it around the attestation before, so line 5 and line 7 are unchanged term for term on every return that leaves line 4 blank. Making this fact complete safe instead would have moved the guard from a real "did the filer answer line 4" question to one that is always true.
BYTE IDENTICAL ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS: ../part3IsAnswered is false on every committed return, so this equals ../writableCostOfGoodsSold there, which is what line 4, line 5 and line 7 read before.
NO FLOOR AT ZERO. Line 42 as the form prints it is a subtraction and this fact does not clamp it: an ending inventory larger than line 40 gives a negative cost of goods sold, which is a Part III the filer has mis-stated rather than a number to silently repair. The attestation arm keeps its own Min 0 limit.

Fact.Name: Cost of goods sold as entered, or 0 (Schedule C line 4)
Fact.Description:
Complete safe reading of ../costOfGoodsSold: Schedule C line 42's value when it resolves, else 0. The twin of ../returnsAndAllowancesOrZero and for the same reason: printed line 5 subtracts it and must not blank on a Schedule C with no inventory.
THE GUARDED FACT IS ../costOfGoodsSold, not the attestation ../writableCostOfGoodsSold, which is the Part III computation when Part III was worked and that same attestation otherwise. The guard itself is untouched and still asks a real question, because the fall through arm of ../costOfGoodsSold passes the attestation's Incomplete straight through: on a Schedule C with no inventory this is $0 exactly as before.

Fact.Name: Made no payments requiring a Form 1099 (Schedule C line I, No)
Fact.Description: The printed No box of Schedule C line I for THIS business: the negation of ../writableMadePaymentsRequiringForm1099. Incomplete while line I is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Did not materially participate in this business (Schedule C line G, No)
Fact.Description: The printed No box of Schedule C line G for THIS business: the negation of ../writableMateriallyParticipated. Incomplete while line G is unanswered, so neither box is checked on a Schedule C that never answered it.

Fact.Name: Has no evidence supporting the vehicle deduction (Schedule C line 47a, No)
Fact.Description: The printed No box of Schedule C Part IV line 47a for THIS business: the negation of ../writableHasEvidenceSupportingVehicleDeduction. Incomplete while line 47a is unanswered.

Fact.Name: No other vehicle is available for personal use (Schedule C line 46, No)
Fact.Description:
The printed No box of Schedule C Part IV line 46 for THIS business: the negation of ../writableHasAnotherVehicleForPersonalUse. Incomplete while line 46 is unanswered.
THE DELIBERATE TWIN of the staged /form4562Vehicles/*/hasNoOtherVehicleForPersonalUse: the same negation of the same question, asked of a different collection. Form 4562 Part V Section B asks it once per VEHICLE; Schedule C Part IV asks it once per BUSINESS, and the form's own heading says Part IV is completed only by a filer who is NOT required to file Form 4562 for that business, so the two tables are never both in play for one activity and neither collection can stand in for the other.

Fact.Name: No change in inventory quantities, costs or valuations (Schedule C line 34, No)
Fact.Description: The printed No box of Schedule C Part III line 34 for THIS business: the negation of ../writableInventoryMethodChangedThisYear. Incomplete while line 34 is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Closing inventory valued by another method (Schedule C line 33c)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part III line 33 box (c) for THIS business: a valuation method that is neither cost nor the lower of cost or market. Derived as the negation of ../usesCostOrLowerOfCostOrMarketInventoryValuation, the same construction line F box (3) uses and for the same reason. The explanation the box calls for is an attachment, not a printed box, so no write in fact accompanies it.

Fact.Name: Gross receipts or sales (Schedule C line 1, as printed)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 1 for THIS business as the form prints it: the filer's gross receipts (../writableGrossReceipts, a negative answer counted as $0) plus the box 1 wages of every statutory employee Form W-2 linked to this Schedule C (../statutoryEmployeeWagesFromLinkedW2s), which the instructions put on line 1 ("Enter your statutory employee income from box 1 of" Form W-2, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 5). On a statutory employee Schedule C with no other receipts answered, it is the wages alone. Incomplete when the receipts are unanswered and no statutory W-2 is linked, so an unanswered line 1 prints blank, not 0. The printed line 1 box and the minuend of ../line3GrossReceiptsLessReturnsAndAllowances; ../scheduleCGrossIncome (line 7) carries the same two terms, so printed lines 1, 3, 5 and 7 add. ../writableGrossReceipts itself is unchanged and still read bare by qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/scheduleCLinkResolves.

Fact.Name: Returns and allowances (Schedule C line 2, as printed)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 2 for THIS business as the form prints it: ../writableReturnsAndAllowances, a negative answer printed and counted as $0. The instructions report returns and allowances as a positive number (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sc.pdf, page 6 "Report your sales returns and allowances as a positive number"); the computation (../returnsAndAllowancesOrZero) already counts a negative answer as 0, so printing the floored figure keeps printed lines 1, 2 and 3 adding. Incomplete, and printed blank, while line 2 is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Gross receipts less returns and allowances (Schedule C line 3)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 3 for THIS business: line 1 gross receipts less line 2 returns and allowances. DERIVED, NOT INTAKEN: both terms already ship as intakes, so a third intake could contradict them. The subtrahend is the complete safe ../returnsAndAllowancesOrZero while the minuend is the printed line 1 (../line1GrossReceipts: the receipts plus any linked statutory employee W-2 wages), which mirrors ../scheduleCGrossIncome exactly: an unanswered line 2 contributes 0, but an unanswered line 1 leaves the whole line blank rather than printing a spurious 0. PRINT ONLY: line 7 keeps its own inline arithmetic, so nothing downstream moves.

Fact.Name: Gross profit (Schedule C line 5)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 5 for THIS business: line 3 less line 4 cost of goods sold. Built on ../line3GrossReceiptsLessReturnsAndAllowances and the complete safe ../costOfGoodsSoldOrZero for the same reasons line 3 gives. PRINT ONLY: ../scheduleCGrossIncome (line 7) continues to compute the same chain inline and is what the rest of the return reads, so this fact cannot move a committed figure. It also cannot part from line 7: the two agree term for term, line 7 being this fact plus the complete safe reading of line 6.

Fact.Name: Other expenses listed in Schedule C Part V (this business)
Fact.Description: The Part V other expense rows for THIS business: one item per business expense the filer lists that is not included on lines 8 through 27a or line 30. A collection nested inside a /scheduleCs item, because Part V is a table printed once per Schedule C and each of its nine printed rows is one expense with its own description and amount. The printed page has nine rows; the collection itself is unbounded and the register's column axis is what limits what prints.

Fact.Name: Amount of this other expense (Schedule C Part V)
Fact.Description:
The amount printed in the right column of one Schedule C Part V row, as a positive number. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer. In particular it does NOT feed ../../writableLine48TotalOtherExpenses: that shipped intake is the filer supplied Part V total that printed line 27b also carries, and the amount entered here is already inside it. A successor that derives line 48 by summing these rows must retire the collapsed total in the SAME unit, or line 28 counts every listed expense twice.
[IT IS NO LONGER RECORD ONLY. The sentence above is kept verbatim and is now false: the row feeds ../line48TotalOtherExpenses, which is Schedule C line 48 and line 27b, and a nonempty Part V row table now selects detailed expense mode for line 28 through ../expenseDetailLinesAnswered.]

Fact.Name: Description of this other expense (Schedule C Part V)
Fact.Description: The description printed in the left column of one Schedule C Part V row: what the expense was. Free text. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Returns and allowances as entered, or 0 (Schedule C line 2)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of ../writableReturnsAndAllowances: that nonnegative intake's value, floored at $0, when it is answered, else 0. The module's own idiom, the guard ../scheduleCGrossIncome already wraps INLINE around this same intake, named here so the printed line 3 can subtract it without going Incomplete on a Schedule C that never answered line 2.

Fact.Name: Some investment in this activity is not at risk (Schedule C line 32b)
Fact.Description: The printed box 32b for THIS business: the negation of the shipped attestation ../writableAllInvestmentAtRisk, which is box 32a. Derived rather than intaken because 32a and 32b are the two halves of one answer, and a second intake could contradict the first. Incomplete while 32a is unanswered, so neither box is checked until the filer answers.

Fact.Name: This business uses the cash or the accrual method (Schedule C line F)
Fact.Description: True when THIS business answered either of the two named line F methods. A helper with one consumer, ../accountingMethodIsOther, which is the printed box (3): line F asks for exactly one of three methods, so 'other' is precisely 'neither of the two named ones'. Complete safe by the Any operator's own rule: true as soon as either box is true, and Incomplete while both are unanswered, so box (3) stays unchecked on a Schedule C whose line F was never asked.

Fact.Name: Closing inventory was valued at cost or at the lower of cost or market (Schedule C line 33)
Fact.Description: True when THIS business answered either of the two named line 33 valuation methods. A helper with one consumer, ../inventoryValuationMethodIsOther, which is the printed box (c). Complete safe by the Any operator's own rule: Incomplete while both named boxes are unanswered, so box (c) stays unchecked on a Schedule C with no Part III.

Fact.Name: The vehicle evidence is not written (Schedule C line 47b, No)
Fact.Description: The printed No box of Schedule C Part IV line 47b for THIS business: the negation of ../writableVehicleEvidenceIsWritten. Incomplete while line 47b is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Vehicle not available for personal use off duty (Schedule C line 45, No)
Fact.Description: The printed No box of Schedule C Part IV line 45 for THIS business: the negation of ../writableVehicleAvailableForPersonalUse. Incomplete while line 45 is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Did not and will not file the required Forms 1099 (Schedule C line J, No)
Fact.Description: The printed No box of Schedule C line J for THIS business: the negation of ../writableWillFileRequiredForms1099. Incomplete while line J is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Accounting method is accrual (Schedule C line F box 2)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line F box (2) for THIS business: the filer keeps the books on the accrual method. The second of the two line F intakes; see ../writableAccountingMethodIsCash for why the three way choice is modelled as two Bools and a derived third. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Accounting method is cash (Schedule C line F box 1)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line F box (1) for THIS business: the filer keeps the books on the cash method. One of the three mutually exclusive line F boxes. THE MUTUAL EXCLUSION IS NOT ENFORCED IN THE GRAPH and that is stated rather than hidden: the writable template offers no Enum, so a three way radio has to be modelled as Bools, and the interview is what stops a filer answering two of them true. Only two of the three are intakes: ../accountingMethodIsOther is derived as the negation of this box or the accrual box, so no third answer can contradict these two. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Commuting miles driven (Schedule C line 44b)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part IV line 44 box (b) for THIS business: the number of miles the vehicle was driven for commuting during the tax year. Sibling of the shipped ../writableBusinessMilesDriven, which is box (a) and which the standard mileage amount reads. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer. Note that ../writableVehicleTotalMiles is the total miles the actual expense method needs, not the sum of the three line 44 boxes, and this fact does not change that.

Fact.Name: Another vehicle is available for personal use (Schedule C line 46, Yes)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part IV line 46 for THIS business: the filer or the filer's spouse has another vehicle available for personal use. The printed No box is ../hasNoOtherVehicleForPersonalUse. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Has evidence supporting the vehicle deduction (Schedule C line 47a, Yes)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part IV line 47a for THIS business: the filer has evidence to support the vehicle deduction. The printed No box is ../hasNoEvidenceSupportingVehicleDeduction. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Inventory quantities, costs or valuations changed (Schedule C line 34, Yes)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part III line 34 for THIS business: there was a change in determining quantities, costs, or valuations between opening and closing inventory. The printed No box is ../inventoryMethodDidNotChangeThisYear. The explanation a Yes calls for is an attachment. Such a change is a change of accounting method, which needs the IRS's consent under IRC 446(e) (26 U.S.C. 446, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section446&num=0&edition=2024 "secure the consent of the Secretary"; generally Form 3115; rows FED-1040SC-LINE33-34-INVENTORY-METHOD-033 and FED-1040SC-LINEF-ACCOUNTING-METHOD-031) and a section 481(a) adjustment the filer figures. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Closing inventory valued at cost (Schedule C line 33a)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part III line 33 box (a) for THIS business: closing inventory was valued at cost. One of the three mutually exclusive line 33 boxes; as on line F, only two are intakes and the third, ../inventoryValuationMethodIsOther, is their negation, so no third answer can contradict these two. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Closing inventory valued at the lower of cost or market (Schedule C line 33b)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part III line 33 box (b) for THIS business: closing inventory was valued at the lower of cost or market. The second of the two line 33 intakes. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Line 1 income was statutory employee wages (Schedule C line 1 checkbox)
Fact.Description:
The checkbox printed on Schedule C line 1 for THIS business: the line 1 income was reported to the filer on a Form W-2 whose Statutory employee box was checked. NOT derived from /formW2s/*/statutoryEmployee, and the grain is why: that fact is per W-2 and this form is per Schedule C, nothing in the graph links a W-2 to a Schedule C, and the formW2s module is not declared for this form.
NO LONGER RECORD ONLY. It is now the SELF EMPLOYMENT TAX GATE for this business, read through the complete safe wrapper ../isStatutoryEmployeeIncome by ../primaryFilerNetProfit and ../secondaryFilerNetProfit: when the box is checked, this Schedule C's line 31 still reaches Schedule 1 line 3 through ../netProfit and /scheduleCNetProfit, but it contributes 0 to Schedule SE line 2, which is what the Line 31 instruction prints ("do not report this amount on Schedule SE (Form 1040), line 2"). Before this edit a statutory employee Schedule C was charged self employment tax it does not owe, with nothing in the graph to detect it. Unanswered still means not a statutory employee, so no committed figure moved.

Fact.Name: Principal business or profession (Schedule C line A)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line A for THIS business: the principal business or profession, including the product or service. Free text; the form places no format on it. The graph models the business (/scheduleCs) but has never held its trade description, so the printed box had no fact at all. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Principal business activity code (Schedule C line B)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line B for THIS business: the six digit principal business activity code the filer copies from the instructions' code list. TYPED String, NOT Int, and deliberately: the code is an identifier whose leading digits are significant, and an Int would drop a leading zero on the codes that carry one. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Employer identification number (Schedule C line D)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line D for THIS business: the employer identification number, when the business has one. TYPED EIN, unlike the union typed identifying-number boxes elsewhere in the dictionary: line D asks only for an EIN, and a sole proprietor with no EIN leaves it blank rather than substituting a social security number, which an unanswered EIN models exactly. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Business street address (Schedule C line E)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line E for THIS business: the business street address including suite or room number. TYPED String, not the graph's Address type: the writable template has no Address form, the printed box is one line of free text, and the city, state and ZIP footer prints from its own sibling intake. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Business city, state and ZIP code (Schedule C line E)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line E footer for THIS business: city, town or post office, state, and ZIP code, as one printed line. Sibling of the street address intake and typed the same way and for the same reason. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Made payments requiring a Form 1099 (Schedule C line I, Yes)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line I for THIS business: the filer made payments during the tax year that would require filing one or more Forms 1099. The printed No box is ../didNotMakePaymentsRequiringForm1099. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Materially participated in this business (Schedule C line G, Yes)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line G for THIS business: the filer materially participated in the operation of the business during the tax year. The printed No box is ../didNotMateriallyParticipate, the negation of this attestation rather than a second intake. NOT derived from the Schedule E or Schedule F material participation facts: those are per K-1 and per farm and say nothing about a sole proprietorship. CONSUMED: ../passiveActivityLossLimitationApplies reads this fact directly (an IsComplete guard, so an unanswered line G still leaves ../netProfit untouched) and its negation ../didNotMateriallyParticipate, to decide whether IRC §469 suspends this business's current-year loss.

Fact.Name: Other accounting method, as specified (Schedule C line F box 3 write in)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line F box (3) write in for THIS business: the name of the accounting method when it is neither cash nor accrual. Free text. The box beside it, ../accountingMethodIsOther, is derived; this is the only line F intake that is not a Bool. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Other miles driven (Schedule C line 44c)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part IV line 44 box (c) for THIS business: the number of miles the vehicle was driven for purposes other than business or commuting. The third of the line 44 boxes. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Total square footage of the home, simplified method (Schedule C line 30 box a)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 30 box (a) for THIS business: the total square footage of the home, asked only of simplified method filers. NOT ../writableHomeOfficeTotalArea, and the audience is why: that fact's own Description scopes it to Form 8829 line 2 and says it is used ONLY when the regular method is elected, so mapping it here would print the Form 8829 denominator for filers this box does not address and print nothing for the filers it does. The part of the home used for business, box (b), already ships as ../writableHomeOfficeSquareFeet. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer. The Simplified Method Worksheet amount that line 30 itself prints comes from ../homeOfficeDeduction and does not read this box.

Fact.Name: Started or acquired this business during the tax year (Schedule C line H)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line H for THIS business: the filer started or acquired the business during the tax year. A single check here box with no No twin, which is why it has no derived sibling. It gates the IRC §195 start-up-expenditure election below: ../startUpExpendituresFirstYearDeduction and ../startUpExpendituresAmortizationDeduction both read it directly, because §195(b)(1)(A)'s first-year allowance is for "the taxable year in which the active trade or business begins" and this box is the only fact on this return that states that year is 2025. Answered No or left unanswered, the election facts default to $0 and the printed box still carries the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Date this business began or was acquired (Schedule C line H, feeds the §195 start-up-cost computation)
Fact.Description: The calendar date THIS business began operating or was acquired. Question text: "On what date did this business begin or did you acquire it?" Help text: this is the date IRC §195(b)(1)(B) uses to start the 180-month period over which any start-up expenditures not covered by the first-year allowance are amortized — the same event line H's check box already discloses, dated rather than merely flagged. Asked when: right after ../writableStartedOrAcquiredBusinessThisYear (line H) is answered Yes; and, when line H is No, asked of a business that elected to deduct start-up expenditures in an earlier year (question text: "Did this business begin in 2010 or later and deduct start-up costs in the year it began? If so, on what date did it begin?"), because a business that began from 2010 through 2024 still deducts 2025's share of its 180 months (../startUpExpendituresPriorYearAmortization, FED-1040SC-SECTION195-STARTUP-035). Unanswered posture: the §195 amortization term treats an unanswered date the same as an unmade election — ../startUpExpendituresAmortizationDeduction resolves $0 rather than guessing a month, so the return is unaffected; the first-year allowance itself does not need this date and is unaffected either way. Validation: any calendar date; with line H Yes, a date that does not fall in 2025 contradicts line H and is treated the same as unanswered rather than trusted, since no cited authority resolves that contradiction for the filer; with line H No, a date before 2025 starts the later-year amortization. Feeds: ../startUpExpendituresMonthsRemainingInTaxYear and ../startUpExpendituresAmortizationDeduction (a 2025 start), ../startUpExpendituresBeganBeforeThisYear and ../startUpExpendituresPriorYearMonthsInTaxYear (an earlier start), all reaching Schedule C line 28 through ../startUpExpendituresDeduction.

Fact.Name: Total start-up expenditures for this business (IRC §195)
Fact.Description: The total amount THIS business paid or incurred investigating or creating the active trade or business before it began — IRC §195(c)(1)'s "start-up expenditure": a cost that would be currently deductible if the business already existed (a pre-opening market survey, advertising, employee training, and similar costs of investigating or creating the business), other than an amount for which a deduction is allowable under IRC §163(a), §164, §174 or §174A (domestic research or experimental expenditures are deducted under §174A, not here). Question text: "How much did you pay or incur investigating or creating this business before it began? Do not include interest, taxes, or research or experimental expenditures." Asked when this business began in 2025 (line H Yes), and of a business that began from 2010 through 2024 and elected to deduct start-up expenditures in the year it began (line H No, ../writableBusinessBeganDate before 2025): for that business the question is the total start-up expenditures of the year it began, and 2025 deducts its share of the 180 months (../startUpExpendituresPriorYearAmortization, FED-1040SC-SECTION195-STARTUP-035) in Part V, the part of Schedule C where amortization goes; the filer does not also enter that share as a Part V row. Help text: entering an amount here IS the §195(b) election to deduct these costs rather than capitalize them — §195(a) disallows the deduction outright absent an election, and §195(d)(1) requires the election no later than the return's filing deadline (including extensions), which is exactly when this intake is answered. Asked when: right after ../writableBusinessBeganDate, in either case above. Unanswered posture: complete-safe $0 — no election, no deduction, the pre-§195 default the return otherwise took. Validation: whole dollars, minimum $0. Feeds: ../startUpExpendituresFirstYearDeduction (the $5,000 first-year amount, phased out dollar for dollar above $50,000 of expenditures) and ../startUpExpendituresAmortizableRemainder (the balance, amortized ratably over the 180 months ../writableBusinessBeganDate starts), both reaching Schedule C line 28 through ../startUpExpendituresDeduction.

Fact.Name: Start-up expenditures as entered, or $0 (IRC §195)
Fact.Description: Complete safe reading of ../writableStartUpExpendituresIncurred: that intake's value when it is answered, else $0. The module's own idiom (../returnsAndAllowancesOrZero is the same shape over a sibling intake), named here so ../startUpExpendituresFirstYearDeduction and ../startUpExpendituresAmortizableRemainder can compute without going Incomplete on a Schedule C that never answers the election.

Fact.Name: IRC §195(b)(1)(A) first-year start-up-expenditure allowance
Fact.Description: The lesser of (i) the start-up expenditures incurred, or (ii) $5,000 reduced (but not below zero) by the amount by which the expenditures exceed $50,000 — §195(b)(1)(A)'s own two-branch test, spelled the way the statute states it rather than simplified, so a reader can match each Dollar literal to the clause that names it. $0 whenever ../startUpExpendituresIncurredOrZero is $0 (unelected or the business did not begin this year), and $0 again once expenditures reach $55,000, where the $5,000 cap is fully phased out. FULLY PHASES OUT AT $55,000, DELIBERATELY UNDISCLOSED AS A SEPARATE FACT: the phase-out is dollar for dollar above $50,000, so $50,000 of excess (at $100,000 of expenditures) already exceeds the $5,000 cap it is reducing — no expenditure amount above $55,000 changes this fact's answer, which the GreaterOf floor at $0 states directly.

Fact.Name: IRC §195(b)(1)(B) amortizable remainder of start-up expenditures
Fact.Description: The start-up expenditures left after the first-year allowance — ../startUpExpendituresIncurredOrZero minus ../startUpExpendituresFirstYearDeduction — the amount §195(b)(1)(B) allows "as a deduction ratably over the 180-month period beginning with the month in which the active trade or business begins." $0 whenever the election is unmade, and $0 again for a filer whose entire expenditure amount was already absorbed by the first-year allowance (any amount at or under $5,000, with no phase-out).

Fact.Name: Months of the §195 180-month amortization period that fall in 2025
Fact.Description:
The count of whole months from ../writableBusinessBeganDate's own month through December, inclusive — the number of the 180 amortization months §195(b)(1)(B) allows that land in THIS tax year: 12 for a January start, 1 for a December start. Unlike Pub. 946's depreciation mid-month convention (../form8829PartYearFraction), §195(b)(1)(B) states no half-month rule, so the month of the start itself counts whole.
DEFAULTS TO 0 RATHER THAN REFUSING WHEN ../writableBusinessBeganDate IS ANSWERED BUT FALLS OUTSIDE 2025: unlike ../form8829PartYearFraction's twelve-case switch, which is fenced upstream by ../form8829CessationIsModeled so an out-of-domain date can never reach it, this fact sits directly under ../startUpExpendituresDeduction, which is an unconditional addend of ../line28TotalExpenses on EVERY Schedule C — an Incomplete here would carry every detail-line total and every collapsed total Incomplete on a return whose only defect is one contradictory disclosure date with no printed line of its own. $0 is the same posture ../startUpExpendituresIncurredOrZero already takes for an unmade election, and it is what the amortization term already defaults to for a business that never answers the date at all.

Fact.Name: Current-year IRC §195(b)(1)(B) ratable amortization of start-up expenditures
Fact.Description: ../startUpExpendituresAmortizableRemainder times ../startUpExpendituresMonthsRemainingInTaxYear over 180 — the ratable monthly amount §195(b)(1)(B) allows, for the months of the 180-month period that fall in this first, partial year of amortization. $0 whenever the remainder is $0 or the months figure is $0 (unanswered date, or a date outside 2025).

Fact.Name: This business began before 2025 and states its start-up expenditures (IRC 195, a later year of the 180 months)
Fact.Description: TRUE when THIS business began before January 1, 2025 (../writableBusinessBeganDate answered and earlier than 2025), Schedule C line H is not answered Yes, and the total start-up expenditures of the year it began are answered (../writableStartUpExpendituresIncurred). Such a business is in a later year of the 180-month amortization period IRC 195(b)(1)(B) starts in the month the business began, so 2025 carries its share (../startUpExpendituresPriorYearAmortization). FALSE otherwise, including on every business that began in 2025, whose first-year allowance and first months are figured by ../startUpExpendituresFirstYearDeduction and ../startUpExpendituresAmortizationDeduction. Source-of-record FED-1040SC-SECTION195-STARTUP-035.

Fact.Name: The IRC 195(b)(1)(A) first-year allowance taken in the year this business began (before 2025)
Fact.Description: For a business that began before 2025 (../startUpExpendituresBeganBeforeThisYear), the amount IRC 195(b)(1)(A) allowed in the year it began: the lesser of the start-up expenditures or $5,000 reduced (not below zero) by the expenditures over $50,000; for a business that began in 2010, $10,000 and $60,000 in their place (IRC 195(b)(3), 26 U.S.C. 195, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title26-section195&num=0&edition=prelim). The remainder after this allowance is what the 180 months spread. $0 when the business did not begin before 2025 or the expenditures are unanswered.

Fact.Name: Months of a pre-2025 business's 180-month IRC 195 period that fall in 2025
Fact.Description: For a business that began before 2025 (../startUpExpendituresBeganBeforeThisYear): 12 when it began in 2011 or later (its 180 months, 15 years from the month it began, run past December 2025); for a business that began in 2010, the months of 2025 before the month it began (the period beginning in month M of 2010 ends in month M - 1 of 2025): 0 for January 2010, 11 for December 2010; 0 for a business that began before 2010, whose period ended before 2025. 0 when the business did not begin before 2025.

Fact.Name: 2025 IRC 195(b)(1)(B) amortization of a business that began before 2025
Fact.Description: The start-up remainder of a business that began before 2025 (../writableStartUpExpendituresIncurred less ../startUpExpendituresPriorYearFirstYearAllowance) times ../startUpExpendituresPriorYearMonthsInTaxYear over 180, rounded to the cent: the ratable share of the 180-month period that falls in 2025. Example: a business that began January 1, 2024 with $20,000 of start-up expenditures took $5,000 in 2024; 2025 carries $15,000 x 12/180 = $1,000 in Part V. $0 when the business did not begin before 2025. A term of ../startUpExpendituresDeduction. Source-of-record FED-1040SC-SECTION195-STARTUP-035.

Fact.Name: Total IRC §195 start-up-expenditure deduction for this business (Schedule C, Part V/line 27b)
Fact.Description: ../startUpExpendituresFirstYearDeduction plus ../startUpExpendituresAmortizationDeduction: the whole current-year IRC section 195 deduction. It is a Part V amount ("Include amortization in this part"), so it is a term of ../line48TotalOtherExpenses and reaches line 28 through printed line 27b; on the collapsed arm of ../line28TotalExpenses it is added on its own. No filer answer collapses into this figure: it is computed from ../writableStartUpExpendituresIncurred and ../writableBusinessBeganDate, and ../writableTotalExpenses scopes it out of its own total. In the year the business began (line H Yes) it is the first-year allowance plus that year's months of amortization; for a business that began before 2025 it is 2025's share of the 180 months (../startUpExpendituresPriorYearAmortization, FED-1040SC-SECTION195-STARTUP-035). $0 when no expenditure amount is entered.

Fact.Name: Vehicle available for personal use off duty (Schedule C line 45, Yes)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part IV line 45 for THIS business: the vehicle was available for personal use during off duty hours. The printed No box is ../vehicleNotAvailableForPersonalUse. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: The vehicle evidence is written (Schedule C line 47b, Yes)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part IV line 47b for THIS business: the evidence supporting the vehicle deduction is written. The printed No box is ../vehicleEvidenceIsNotWritten. The form asks 47b only of a 47a Yes; that conditional is an interview rule and this fact does not encode it. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Date the vehicle was placed in service (Schedule C line 43)
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part IV line 43 for THIS business: the date the filer placed the vehicle in service for business purposes. TYPED Day, one fact for one date, even though the form prints it in three boxes: the month, day and year boxes are filler transforms of this one value (the ~dateMonth, ~dateDay and ~dateYear convention Form 8828's date intakes already use), not three separate facts that could disagree. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: Filed or will file the required Forms 1099 (Schedule C line J, Yes)
Fact.Description: Schedule C header line J for THIS business: having answered line I Yes, the filer did or will file the required Forms 1099. The printed No box is ../willNotFileRequiredForms1099. The form asks line J only of a line I Yes; that conditional is an interview rule, not a graph one, and this fact does not encode it. RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the graph consumes it and no computed line moves when it is answered; it exists so the printed box can carry the filer's own answer.

Fact.Name: (Writable) Is this business's net profit or loss community income?
Fact.Description: THE PER-BUSINESS CHARACTER INPUT for Form 8958 line 5, the Schedule C twin of formW2s:/formW2s/*/writableIsCommunityIncome. Form 8958 splits a sole proprietorship's income evenly: "A spouse's or RDP's wages and self-employment income from a sole proprietorship are community income and must be evenly split" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 3, LEFT column), and Publication 555 says the same of "net profits from a sole proprietorship" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, page 5, LEFT column). Which income is community is state law (IRC 66(d)(2)), so the question is put per business. SCREEN SPEC. Implement the screen from this paragraph; no IRS document has to be opened. QUESTION: "Is the net profit or loss from {../writableBusinessName} community income?" HELP TEXT: "In a community property state, the net profit of a business you or your spouse runs while you are married and domiciled in that state is usually community income, and each of you reports half of it. Answer No only if your state's law treats this business's income as one spouse's separate income. Either way, enter the business's WHOLE net profit or loss on this Schedule C: the return halves community income itself. Answer the Schedule SE question about community income taxed to your spouse with $0 for this business: its whole net profit is already on this Schedule C. If only you carried on the business, also answer the Schedule SE question about exempt community income with $0. If you and your spouse both carried on the business, answer exempt community income with your spouse's share of its net profit, or of its loss as a negative amount, so that self-employment tax is figured on your own share only." Cite for the help text: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 3 and https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p555.pdf, page 5, LEFT column of each; for the two Schedule SE sentences, 26 U.S.C. 1402, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1402&num=0&edition=2024, LEFT column, and https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sse.pdf, page 2, RIGHT column. ASKED WHEN: filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is true — a married filer filing separately, domiciled in a community property state and not relieved by IRC 66(a) — and the return claims Schedule C income (/claimsScheduleCIncome). Asked once per item of /scheduleCs, on every Schedule C the return carries. Never asked on any other return. UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED, not defaulted. Silence makes ../isCommunityIncome FALSE, so nothing is allocated, and makes /scheduleCs/communityPropertyCharacterisationIncomplete TRUE, which makes filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete FALSE and leaves filers:/knockoutSubjectToCommunityPropertyLaws refusing the return. VALIDATION: Boolean. Yes / No, no third option and no default. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../form8958Line5RowIsAllocatedCommunityIncome, hence Form 8958 line 5 columns B and C (../form8958Line5ColumnBThisReturnShare, ../form8958Line5ColumnCSpouseShare) and /communityPropertyScheduleCAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded, the half that leaves Schedule 1 line 3. THE MODEL, stated so the two Schedule SE community income questions are not answered twice. This Schedule C carries the business's WHOLE line 31. Form 8958 line 5 column A is that whole, column B the half, and Schedule 1 line 3 receives the half. Schedule SE keeps reading the whole (/primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit), and IRC 1402(a)(5)(A) has two arms (26 U.S.C. 1402, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1402&num=0&edition=2024, LEFT column): the income of a community business is that of "the spouse carrying on such trade or business" or, "if such trade or business is jointly operated", of "each spouse on the basis of their respective distributive share". The Schedule SE instructions say the same: "If both spouses participate, the income and deductions are allocated to the spouses based on their distributive shares" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sse.pdf, page 2, RIGHT column). Under the first arm this return's Schedule SE takes the whole business. Under the second it takes this spouse's share, reached by entering the other spouse's share as exempt community income (scheduleSE:/writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeExemptCommunityIncome), which Schedule SE subtracts from the whole. Community income taxed to spouse stays $0 under both arms. The Schedule SE instructions describe a different bookkeeping, each spouse's Schedule C showing that spouse's share with the operating spouse adding the other share back on Schedule SE line 3; both reach the same two figures, but mixing them charges self-employment tax on 150% of the business, which /scheduleCs/communityScheduleCAlsoEnteredAsScheduleSeAddBack reports. The model is for spouses only: section 1402(a)(5) "does not apply to RDPs. RDPs split self-employment income from sole proprietorships and partnerships for self-employment tax purposes" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 3, RIGHT column), so an allocation for registered domestic partners must not reuse it.

Fact.Name: This business's net profit or loss is community income
Fact.Description: ../writableIsCommunityIncome read complete safe: IsComplete first, so an unanswered character resolves FALSE, the fail closed direction (nothing allocated, refusal standing). An answered FALSE and an unanswered character part company only at ../communityPropertyCharacterisationMissing, which is true for silence alone.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C's community-property character question is unanswered
Some Schedule C community-property character is unanswered
Fact.Description: GreaterThan(Count of per-business unanswered characters, 0), the shape of formW2s:/formW2s/communityPropertyCharacterisationIncomplete. The seventh characterisable collection read by filers:/communityPropertyAllocationInputsComplete. FALSE on a return that claims no Schedule C (/claimsScheduleCIncome false, where every business nets $0) or whose /scheduleCs collection was never opened: that return has no Schedule C income and so owes no character, the same reading this module's /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit gives an absent collection ($0, never unresolved). A return holding any Schedule C item has the collection, so an unanswered character on it still reads TRUE and still refuses. Fail closed on every item that exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 5 row is an allocated community income row
Fact.Description: True when this Schedule C sits on a return that must allocate community income AND the filer has characterised the business's income as community income: the condition the line 5 column facts and the adjustment switch on. False on every other return and on a separate-property business, so silence about a business's character never allocates it.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 5, the community half of this business's net profit or loss
Fact.Description: Half of ../netProfit, Schedule C line 31, on an allocated community row, and $0 on every other row and return. SIGNED: a community loss halves as a community profit does. Not rounded to whole dollars; the Form 1040 lines it reaches round at their own printed line.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 5 column B, this return's share of this business's net profit or loss
Fact.Description: The share of this Schedule C's line 31 that belongs on THIS separate return, which Form 8958 line 5 column B prints: the community half on an allocated community row, the whole ../netProfit on every other row. Column A is ../netProfit, so column B and ../form8958Line5ColumnCSpouseShare foot to it by construction.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 5 column C, the other spouse or RDP share of this business's net profit or loss
Fact.Description: Column A minus column B: ../netProfit less ../form8958Line5ColumnBThisReturnShare. On an allocated community row it is the half that leaves this return (an odd cent of the halving lands here, so the footing holds exactly); $0 on a separate-property row and off the gate.

Fact.Name: The Schedule C half that leaves this return under Form 8958
Fact.Description: A NEGATIVE addend on a profit (positive on a loss), cents-bearing: MINUS the sum of every Schedule C's Form 8958 line 5 column C, the part of each business's line 31 that belongs on the spouse's separate return. The exact column C, not the half, so Schedule 1 line 3 foots to the printed column B total by construction. It is the Schedule C twin of formW2s:/communityPropertyWagesAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded and is added wherever that fact's wage figure is post-allocation: Schedule 1 line 3 and the income totals that mirror it. Readers that take earned income without regard to community property law keep the whole. $0 on every return that does not allocate community income and on a return with no Schedule C collection.

Fact.Name: A community Schedule C is also added back on Schedule SE as community income taxed to spouse
Fact.Description: True when this return allocates a Schedule C as community income (any item's ../form8958Line5RowIsAllocatedCommunityIncome) AND scheduleSE:/writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeCommunityIncomeTaxedToSpouse is answered and not $0. The two describe the same business twice: Schedule SE already reads the whole of an allocated business's net profit, so an added-back spouse's share charges self-employment tax on 150% of it. The return is refused while both routes are positive, unless the filer answers that the add-back is only for a business that is not one of the Schedule C businesses on this return (/writableScheduleSeCommunityAddBackIncludesABusinessOnThisReturn answered No): a business the filer carried on whose share is reported on the spouse's separate Schedule C is added back legitimately. Clear the duplicate Schedule SE add-back, or answer that question, before filing. False on a return that never opened /scheduleCs, and Complete there.

Fact.Name: The Schedule SE community add-back includes a business on this return's Schedule C
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Does the community income taxed to your spouse that you entered for Schedule SE include any business that is also one of the Schedule C businesses on this return?" HELP TEXT: answer No when the add-back is only for a business you carried on whose share is reported on your spouse's separate Schedule C and is not entered as a Schedule C here. A Schedule C on this return that allocates community income already puts the whole business on your Schedule SE, so adding its spouse's share back again would tax it twice. ASKED WHEN: this return allocates a Schedule C as community income and scheduleSE:/writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeCommunityIncomeTaxedToSpouse is not $0. UNANSWERED POSTURE: treated as Yes; the return is refused by /scheduleCs/communityScheduleCAlsoEnteredAsScheduleSeAddBack. WHAT IT FEEDS: that refusal only.

Fact.Name: A Schedule C combines statutory employee wages with other receipts
Fact.Description: A Schedule C that carries the wages of a Form W-2 with box 13 "Statutory employee" checked also reports other gross receipts on line 1. The instructions require two Schedules C: one for the statutory employee income and one for self-employment income ("You cannot combine these amounts on a single Schedule C"). The statutory employee Schedule C stays off Schedule SE, so receipts combined into it would escape self-employment tax. The return is refused, and held with the named reason /scheduleCStatutoryEmployeeWagesOnTheirOwnScheduleC in flow:/flowIncomplete (ruling IN-280), until the other receipts are moved to their own Schedule C. True when at least one Schedule C names a linked statutory employee Form W-2 (../scheduleCs/*/hasLinkedStatutoryEmployeeW2) and answers line 1 gross receipts above $0; false on every other return.

Fact.Name: A passive Schedule C beside other passive activity
Fact.Description: A Schedule C business in which the filer did not materially participate (line G "No") is a passive activity. Its loss is allowed only against passive income, and its profit is passive income that frees other passive losses, both figured on Form 8582. The passive Schedule C businesses are pooled with each other (/scheduleCs/*/section469SuspendedPassiveLoss: losses allowed up to the passive Schedule C income, the excess allocated ratably), but the Schedule E pool (rentals and Schedule K-1s, scheduleE:/passiveIncomeTotal and scheduleE:/passiveSuspendedLossTotal) and the Schedule C pool do not read each other. The return is refused when a passive Schedule C shows a loss beside passive income in the Schedule E pool, or a passive Schedule C shows a profit beside a passive loss the Schedule E pool suspends. Not refused: line G unanswered or Yes; passive Schedule C losses and profits with no Schedule E passive activity (the Schedule C pool computes them); a passive profit beside no suspended loss. Narrowed by FED-1040SC-LINEG-PASSIVE-LOSS-028: a passive Schedule C loss beside another passive Schedule C profit used to be refused here.

Fact.Name: The return's only Form 461 trade or business items are Schedules C
Fact.Description: TRUE when the return has at least one Schedule C and answers no Schedule E rental (scheduleE:/hasScheduleERentalIncome), no Schedule K-1 (scheduleE:/writableHasK1Income, or Yes with the K-1 list scheduleE:/formK1s answered empty) and no Schedule F (scheduleF:/writableHasScheduleFFarmIncome) as Yes. On such a return Form 461 line 2 (Schedule 1 line 3) is the trade or business amount Form 461 nets, and /scheduleCForm461ExcessBusinessLoss computes Schedule 1 line 8p. FALSE otherwise: Form 461 lines 3 through 8 (Schedule E, K-1, Schedule F) are not computed, so line 8p stays the filer's typed Form 461 result (income:/writableSchedule1Line8pExcessBusinessLossAdjustment) and /knockoutScheduleCExcessBusinessLossNotFigured refuses a loss past the threshold with it unanswered. Not read here: a business Form 4797 gain or loss and business capital gains and losses (Form 461 lines 3-8), which no fact routes to Form 461 yet (named OPEN in the module records). Row FED-1040SC-LINE31-EXCESS-BUSINESS-LOSS-029.

Fact.Name: Form 461 excess business loss from the Schedules C (Form 461 line 16 as a positive number, Schedule 1 line 8p)
Fact.Description: Form 461 (2025) for a return whose only trade or business items are Schedules C (/scheduleCOnlyForm461Population): line 2 is Schedule 1 line 3 (/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax), lines 9 and 14 equal it (no other items, no line 13 adjustment), line 15 is the 2025 threshold, $313,000 or $626,000 on a joint return (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i461.pdf, page 1 "$313,000 ($626,000 for taxpayers filing a joint return)."), and line 16 is line 14 plus line 15; when line 16 is less than zero its absolute value is the excess business loss entered as a positive number on Schedule 1 line 8p (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f461.pdf, page 1 "If less than zero, enter the amount from line 16 as a positive number on Schedule"). $0 when Schedule 1 line 3 is not below minus the threshold. Wages are not a Form 461 item. The amount carries to 2026 as a net operating loss (form172:/form172EblWorksheetNolCarryoverToNextYear, line 3). Example: a single filer's Schedule C loss of $390,000 gives line 16 = -$77,000 and line 8p $77,000. Row FED-1040SC-LINE31-EXCESS-BUSINESS-LOSS-029.

Fact.Name: A Schedule C loss past the excess business loss threshold, Form 461 not figured
Fact.Description: The Schedule C net loss on this return (/scheduleCNetProfit below $0) is larger than the 2025 excess business loss threshold, $313,000, or $626,000 on a joint return, and the Form 461 result (income:/writableSchedule1Line8pExcessBusinessLossAdjustment, Schedule 1 line 8p) is not answered. IRC 461(l) disallows the part of the combined business losses above the threshold. A return whose only trade or business items are Schedules C computes Form 461 (/scheduleCForm461ExcessBusinessLoss) and is never refused here; on a return that also has a Schedule E rental, a Schedule K-1 or a Schedule F, Form 461 lines 3 through 8 are not computed, so without the answer the whole loss would reduce income. The return is refused until line 8p is answered; answer $0 when Form 461 shows no excess business loss (for example because other business income absorbs the loss).

Fact.Name: Forms 1099-NEC
Fact.Description: Form 1099-NEC, Nonemployee Compensation: the set of those forms the filer received for the tax year, one item per printed form. Each item names its recipient (../filer); /primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs, /secondaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs and /form1099Necs/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ block submission on an unfinished or misassigned form. Box 3 reaches Schedule 2 line 17k; no other box is routed. A Schedule C's gross receipts stay /scheduleCs/*/writableGrossReceipts, an all-sources figure the filer states there.

Fact.Name: This Form 1099-NEC's box 1 is reported off Schedule C line 1, or the difference is explained
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Is the box 1 amount on this Form 1099-NEC reported somewhere other than line 1 of a Schedule C on this return, or explained in a statement you attach?" HELP TEXT: box 1 nonemployee compensation from your trade or business goes on Schedule C line 1. Answer Yes if this form's box 1 is reported on Schedule F, as wages with Form 8919, or as other income on Schedule 1 (for example income from a sporadic activity), or if you attach a statement explaining why your Schedule C line 1 is less than your Forms 1099-NEC. ASKED WHEN: the total box 1 on this return's Forms 1099-NEC is more than the total Schedule C line 1 gross receipts, or the return has no Schedule C income and this form's box 1 is above $0 (then the statement reason does not apply: Yes means box 1 is reported on Schedule F, as wages with Form 8919, or as other income on Schedule 1). UNANSWERED POSTURE: No; the form's box 1 counts against Schedule C line 1 in /knockoutForm1099NecBox1AboveScheduleCLine1, and refuses the return in /knockoutForm1099NecBox1WithoutScheduleC when there is no Schedule C. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../box1ForScheduleCLine1.

Fact.Name: This Form 1099-NEC's box 1 counted against Schedule C line 1
Fact.Description: Box 1 (../writableNonemployeeCompensation, $0 when unanswered) unless ../writableBox1NotOnScheduleCOrExplained is answered Yes, then $0.

Fact.Name: Forms 1099-NEC box 1 counted against Schedule C line 1, every form on the return
Fact.Description: The sum of /form1099Necs/*/box1ForScheduleCLine1; $0 when no Form 1099-NEC was recorded.

Fact.Name: Forms 1099-NEC box 1 above Schedule C line 1, not explained
Fact.Description: This return claims Schedule C income, and the box 1 nonemployee compensation on its Forms 1099-NEC (/form1099NecBox1ForScheduleCLine1Total, leaving out every form answered as reported elsewhere or explained) is more than all its Schedule C line 1 gross receipts put together (/scheduleCReportedGrossReceiptsTotal). The Schedule C instructions say line 1 includes the amounts properly shown on Forms 1099-NEC and, when box 1 totals more than line 1, to attach a statement explaining the difference. The return is refused until line 1 includes the income or each unmatched Form 1099-NEC is answered as reported elsewhere or explained (/form1099Necs/*/writableBox1NotOnScheduleCOrExplained). Line 1 above the box 1 total is never refused. False on a return without Schedule C income.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC box 1 on a return with no Schedule C, not placed
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when this return claims no Schedule C income (/claimsScheduleCIncome false) and the box 1 nonemployee compensation on its Forms 1099-NEC (/form1099NecBox1ForScheduleCLine1Total, leaving out every form answered as reported elsewhere) is above $0. Without a Schedule C the amount reaches no line of the return: nothing else reads box 1.
WHY A REFUSAL AND NOT A ROUTE. The Form 1099-NEC recipient instructions give box 1 four destinations, and which one applies turns on facts only the filer knows: self-employment income goes on Schedule C or Schedule F (and Schedule SE); a filer who is really an employee reports it as wages with Form 8919; a filer who is not an employee and whose box 1 is not self-employment income (for example a sporadic activity or a hobby) reports it as other income on Schedule 1. Defaulting to any one of them would charge or drop self-employment tax on the wrong population, so the return is refused until the filer adds the Schedule C business or answers, per form, that box 1 is reported elsewhere (/form1099Necs/*/writableBox1NotOnScheduleCOrExplained), and enters it there: Schedule F, form8919:/form8919Firms, or income:/writableActivityNotEngagedForProfitIncome (Schedule 1 line 8j) or the Schedule 1 line 8z other-income entry.
The twin of form1099Misc:/knockoutForm1099MiscScheduleCReceiptsWithoutScheduleC; the return with a Schedule C is /knockoutForm1099NecBox1AboveScheduleCLine1's.
SCREEN: "You entered a Form 1099-NEC with nonemployee compensation in box 1, and your return has no Schedule C. If this is income from your business, add your Schedule C. If you report it somewhere else (Schedule F, wages with Form 8919, or other income on Schedule 1), say so on the form's screen and enter it there."

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC recipient on this return
Fact.Description: Which filer on this return received this Form 1099-NEC. SCREEN SPEC: ask "Who received this Form 1099-NEC?" with one choice per filer (the primary filer, and the spouse when the return has two filers), on every Form 1099-NEC item, before the numbered boxes; required. Help text: Choose the person named in the RECIPIENT'S name box (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099nec--2025.pdf, page 2). On a joint return, enter each spouse's forms under that spouse. The RECIPIENT'S TIN box is copied as printed into ../writableRecipientTin. Validation: one item of /filers. UNANSWERED: the form belongs to neither filer (../belongsToPrimaryFiler and ../belongsToSecondaryFiler both false), and /primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs blocks submission until it is answered; on a joint return /secondaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs blocks as well. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../belongsToPrimaryFiler, ../belongsToSecondaryFiler, ../secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ and the two incomplete-form guards; no dollar amount. Stored for the state and local returns.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC belongs to the primary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1099-NEC belongs to the primary filer: ../filer answered and equal to filers:/primaryFiler. An unanswered ../filer resolves false, not the Placeholder's primary filer, so an unassigned form belongs to neither filer; /primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs counts unassigned forms separately. Read only by the guards in this module.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC belongs to the secondary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1099-NEC belongs to the secondary filer: ../filer answered and equal to filers:/secondaryFiler. An unanswered ../filer, or a return with no secondary filer, resolves false. Read only by the guards in this module.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC calendar year
Fact.Description: Form 1099-NEC: the "For calendar year" entry printed in the form's title block, as a four-digit year (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099nec--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Calendar year shown on this Form 1099-NEC" (four digits), on every Form 1099-NEC item; never required. Help text: The year the payer printed after "For calendar year"; a form for another year belongs on that year's return or is a corrected prior-year form. Validation: exactly four digits. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — a Schedule C's gross receipts stay /scheduleCs/*/writableGrossReceipts, an all-sources figure the filer states there. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-NEC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC VOID box
Fact.Description: Form 1099-NEC: the VOID checkbox in the form's header; it prints on Copy A and Copy 1 only (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099nec--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the VOID box checked on this Form 1099-NEC?" (yes/no), on every Form 1099-NEC item; never required. Help text: A payer checks VOID only on a Copy A it did not mean to file, so the IRS scanner skips it; a correction is never marked VOID. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — a Schedule C's gross receipts stay /scheduleCs/*/writableGrossReceipts, an all-sources figure the filer states there. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-NEC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC CORRECTED box
Fact.Description: Form 1099-NEC: the CORRECTED checkbox in the form's header, printed on every copy (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099nec--2025.pdf, pages 2-3). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Is the CORRECTED box checked on this Form 1099-NEC?" (yes/no), on every Form 1099-NEC item; never required. Help text: A checked CORRECTED means this form replaces one the payer already sent; enter the corrected figures, not the originals. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — a Schedule C's gross receipts stay /scheduleCs/*/writableGrossReceipts, an all-sources figure the filer states there. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-NEC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC payer's name and address
Fact.Description: Form 1099-NEC: the PAYER'S name, street address, city or town, state or province, country, ZIP or foreign postal code, and telephone no. block, as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099nec--2025.pdf, page 2). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Name and address of the payer shown on this Form 1099-NEC" (free text), on every Form 1099-NEC item; never required. Validation: free text. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — a Schedule C's gross receipts stay /scheduleCs/*/writableGrossReceipts, an all-sources figure the filer states there. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-NEC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC payer's TIN
Fact.Description: Form 1099-NEC: the PAYER'S TIN box, as printed; a payer's TIN may never be truncated on the form (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099nec--2025.pdf, page 2; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099mec--2025.pdf, page 9). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Payer's TIN shown on this Form 1099-NEC" (nine digits), on every Form 1099-NEC item; never required. Help text: The instructions say a payer's TIN may not be truncated on any form. Validation: EIN. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; no federal computation reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal — a Schedule C's gross receipts stay /scheduleCs/*/writableGrossReceipts, an all-sources figure the filer states there. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-NEC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC box 1, nonemployee compensation
Fact.Description: Form 1099-NEC: box 1, "Nonemployee compensation" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099nec--2025.pdf, page 2; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099mec--2025.pdf, page 10). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 1 — Nonemployee compensation" (dollar amount), on every Form 1099-NEC item; required for the form to be complete (enter 0 when the box is blank). Help text: The instructions: "Enter nonemployee compensation (NEC) of $600 or more. Include fees, commissions, prizes and awards for services performed as a nonemployee, and other forms of compensation for services performed for your trade or business." NOT ROUTED, and deliberately: a Schedule C reports gross receipts from ALL sources on its own line, so /scheduleCs/*/writableGrossReceipts is a wider figure than this box and is left exactly as it is. This is the per-payer transcription beside it. Validation: Dollar, Min $0. UNANSWERED: ../isComplete is false and /primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs or /secondaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs blocks submission; no federal amount reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../isComplete; nothing federal — a Schedule C's gross receipts stay /scheduleCs/*/writableGrossReceipts, an all-sources figure the filer states there. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-NEC register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC box 3, excess golden parachute payments
Fact.Description: Form 1099-NEC: box 3, "Excess golden parachute payments" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099nec--2025.pdf, page 2; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/i1099mec--2025.pdf, page 11). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 3 — Excess golden parachute payments" (dollar amount), on every Form 1099-NEC item; required for the form to be complete (enter 0 when the box is blank). Help text: The instructions: "An excess parachute payment is the amount over the base amount (the average annual compensation for services includible in the individual's gross income over the most recent 5 tax years)." The recipient copy: "Box 3. Shows your total compensation of excess golden parachute payments subject to a 20% excise tax" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099nec--2025.pdf, page 5). Validation: Dollar, Min $0. UNANSWERED: ../isComplete is false and /primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs or /secondaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs blocks submission; the computation reads it as $0 through ../excessGoldenParachutePaymentsOrZero. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../isComplete, and through ../excessGoldenParachutePaymentsOrZero the 20% excise tax of Schedule 2 line 17k, schedule2:/form1099NecExcessParachutePaymentsTotal. It is not Schedule C gross receipts, which stay /scheduleCs/*/writableGrossReceipts. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-NEC register.

Fact.Name: This Form 1099-NEC's box 4 federal income tax withheld, or zero
Fact.Description: The answered box 4 backup withholding with cents intact, otherwise zero. No per-document rounding: /form1099NecFederalIncomeTaxWithheld sums these and Form 1040 line 25b rounds its total once. An unanswered box is not a filed $0: ../isComplete is false and the incomplete-form guards block submission.

Fact.Name: Total Form 1099-NEC box 4 federal income tax withheld
Fact.Description: Sum of box 4 backup withholding over every Form 1099-NEC on the return, with cents intact: an addend of the Form 1040 line 25b total, taxCalculations:/form1099Withholding, which rounds once. No filer filter, as /form1099MiscFederalIncomeTaxWithheld: a spouse-owned form on a return other than MFJ is refused by /form1099Necs/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ, and nothing on this collection allocates a community half. An empty or unopened collection contributes zero.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC is complete
Fact.Description:
Whether this Form 1099-NEC is complete: box 1 (../writableNonemployeeCompensation), box 3 (../writableExcessGoldenParachutePayments) and box 4 (../writableFederalWithholding) all answered. Each conjunct is an IsComplete test, so an abandoned item resolves false rather than Placeholder.
Box 1 is the amount the form reports; the recipient instructions send it to Schedule C or F, or to the Schedule 1 "Other income" line (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099nec--2025.pdf, page 5). Box 4 is backup withholding the recipient must "Include ... on your income tax return as tax withheld" (same file lines 104-108), which the Form 1040 instructions put in the line 25b total (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 39, middle column) and IRC 31(a)(1) allows as a credit. A zero is an answer; silence is not.
Box 3 shows excess golden parachute payments "subject to a 20% excise tax" (same file lines 100-102), the IRC 4999(a) tax that schedule2:/form1099NecExcessParachutePaymentsTotal computes on Schedule 2 line 17k. That total and /form1099NecFederalIncomeTaxWithheld read boxes 3 and 4 complete-safe, as $0 when unanswered; the $0 keeps the return computable and this conjunct keeps it from filing. The owner (../filer) is not a conjunct; the guards count an unassigned form on their own.
/primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs and /secondaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs count items that are not complete and block submission until they are.

Fact.Name: At least one of the primary filer's Forms 1099-NEC is incomplete
Fact.Description:
Whether at least one of the primary filer's Forms 1099-NEC is incomplete. When true, the return cannot be submitted.
Two independent counts. The first counts forms the primary filer owns (/form1099Necs/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler) whose /form1099Necs/*/isComplete is false: box 1, box 3 or box 4 left unanswered. The second counts forms with no recipient assigned (/form1099Necs/*/filer unanswered), on any return. It does not read the ownership alias, which resolves false on an unassigned form, so an unassigned form still blocks and this guard resolves Complete true rather than Placeholder.
Why it blocks: box 4 carries backup withholding that /form1099NecFederalIncomeTaxWithheld credits on Form 1040 line 25b, and an unfinished form would otherwise file with that box read as $0 withheld. The remedy is the filer finishing the form, so it is a submission block, not a knockout.
Complete false: nec-owner-single-primary-complete, nec-owner-filing-status-unanswered-no-refusal, nec-owner-collection-empty-guards-false and nec-owner-collection-absent-guards-false. The body is read only when /form1099Necs is answered; a return that never answers the collection resolves Complete false, as schedule2:/form1099NecExcessParachutePaymentsTotal reads the same collection. The secondary filer's arm is /secondaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs.

Fact.Name: At least one of the secondary filer's Forms 1099-NEC is incomplete
Fact.Description:
Whether at least one of the secondary filer's Forms 1099-NEC is incomplete. When true, the return cannot be submitted.
The secondary filer's arm of /primaryFilerHasIncompleteForm1099Necs, over /form1099Necs/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler, with the same count of forms that have no recipient assigned, fenced to a joint return: that count fires here only when filingStatus:/isFilingStatusMFJ is answered and true. A return without a secondary filer is blocked once, by the primary guard, and an unanswered filing status leaves this guard Complete false. Read the primary guard for why it blocks.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-NEC assigned to the secondary filer without a joint return
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1099-NEC is assigned to the secondary filer on a return that is not married filing jointly. True only when the filing status is answered and not MFJ, the return has a secondary filer, and ../belongsToSecondaryFiler is true; an unanswered filing status or owner resolves false. No community-property carve-out: nothing on this collection allocates a spouse's community half, so a spouse's Form 1099-NEC on a separate return in a community-property state stays refused here. Read by /form1099Necs/secondaryFilerUsedWithoutMFJ.

Fact.Name: A Form 1099-NEC is assigned to the secondary filer without a joint return
Fact.Description: Whether any Form 1099-NEC is assigned to the secondary filer on a return that is not married filing jointly. When true, the return cannot be submitted: one such form is enough, because a spouse's form has no place on a separate return.

Fact.Name: Total vehicle miles, complete-safe
Fact.Description: Preserves total miles when answered and supplies zero when unanswered, so the actual-expense denominator switch cannot select a value arm from an incomplete intake.

Fact.Name: Home total area, complete-safe
Fact.Description: Preserves total home area when answered and supplies zero when unanswered, so regular-method percentage switches cannot select a value arm from an incomplete intake.

Fact.Name: Daycare hours available, complete-safe
Fact.Description: Preserves daycare availability hours when answered and supplies zero when unanswered, so the positive-denominator switch cannot select its ratio arm prematurely.

Fact.Name: Daycare nonexclusive flag, complete-safe
Fact.Description: Preserves the daycare nonexclusive answer when answered and supplies false when unanswered, so the daycare ratio switch cannot select its value arm prematurely.

Fact.Name: Simplified-method shared-home flag, complete-safe
Fact.Description: Preserves the shared-home answer when answered and supplies false when unanswered, so the allocated-square-foot switch cannot select its value arm prematurely.

Fact.Name: Started-or-acquired flag, complete-safe
Fact.Description: Preserves the start-up election flag when answered and supplies false when unanswered, so the start-up expenditure switch cannot select its value arm prematurely.
